Hajj & Umrah Guides

Hajj & Umrah Guides

Step-by-step Umrah and Hajj, Rawdah & Nusuk app help, visa basics, packing and package enquiries.

Umrah at a Glance

Umrah, step by step

The five core steps every pilgrim follows, in order. Full detail is in Guide 1 below.

1

Ihram & Intention

Before crossing the Meeqat, wear Ihram, make the intention for Umrah and recite the Talbiyah on the way to Makkah.

2

Tawaf — 7 Rounds

Walk 7 rounds around the Kaaba, starting from the Black Stone corner, keeping the Kaaba on your left.

3

2 Rakat at Maqam-e-Ibrahim

After Tawaf, pray 2 rakat behind Maqam-e-Ibrahim if space allows, then drink Zamzam.

4

Sa'i — Safa to Marwah

Walk 7 lengths between Safa and Marwah, remembering the search of Hajrah (AS) for water.

5

Halq or Taqsir

Shave the head (Halq) or trim the hair (Taqsir). With this, your Umrah is complete and Ihram ends.

Complete Method · Tareeqa

How to perform Umrah — the complete method

Every step in order, in simple English — with the rulings and duas for each stage of the journey.

1

Prepare & wear Ihram

Before the Meeqat: bathe (ghusl) if easy, trim nails and remove unwanted hair, and apply perfume to the body — perfume is allowed before entering Ihram, not after. Men wear two unstitched white sheets (one around the waist, one over the shoulders) and open sandals that do not cover the ankle bone. Women wear their normal modest clothes; the face is not covered with a stitched niqab in Ihram.

2

Niyyat (intention) & 2 rakat

At or before the Meeqat, pray 2 rakat (Sunnah of Ihram, outside the disliked times), then make the intention in the heart and say: "O Allah, I intend to perform Umrah, so make it easy for me and accept it from me." With this intention you have entered Ihram and its rules now apply: no perfume, no cutting hair or nails, no hunting, no arguing or sinful talk, and for men no stitched clothing or covered head.

3

Talbiyah — at least once, then often

Immediately after the intention, recite the Talbiyah at least once — this is essential; then keep repeating it on the whole journey until Tawaf begins: "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak." Men raise their voice moderately; women keep their voice low. On seeing Makkah and entering Masjid al-Haram with the right foot, make heartfelt dua — the first sight of the Kaaba is a moment when duas are hoped to be accepted.

4

Tawaf — 7 rounds around the Kaaba

Be in wudu. Men uncover the right shoulder (Idtiba) for this Tawaf. Start in line with the Black Stone (Hajar-e-Aswad): face it, say Bismillah, Allahu Akbar, signal towards it with the right hand (do not push through the crowd to kiss it). Walk anti-clockwise with the Kaaba on your left, completing 7 rounds; men walk briskly (Ramal) in the first 3 rounds if it is easy. Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, recite: "Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah…" (Qur'an 2:201). Tawaf ends after the 7th round at the Black Stone line.

5

2 rakat at Maqam-e-Ibrahim

After Tawaf, pray 2 rakat behind Maqam-e-Ibrahim if you find space without troubling anyone; otherwise anywhere in the Haram. It is recommended to recite Surah Al-Kafirun in the first rakat and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second. Men cover both shoulders again after Tawaf.

6

Drink Zamzam

Go to the Zamzam area, face the Qibla, say Bismillah and drink Zamzam in three breaths until you are full, making the dua: "O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision and healing from every illness."

7

Sa'i — 7 lengths between Safa & Marwah

Go to Safa, face the Kaaba, raise the hands and make dua, reciting the verse (Qur'an 2:158) "Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah…" Then walk towards Marwah — Safa to Marwah is length 1, Marwah back to Safa is length 2 — completing 7 lengths and ending at Marwah. Men walk briskly (jog lightly) between the two green markers; women walk at a normal pace throughout. Remember Hajrah (AS), who ran here searching for water for her son Ismail (AS).

8

Halq or Taqsir — Umrah complete

Finally, men either shave the whole head (Halq — more reward) or trim the hair of the whole head by at least a fingertip length (Taqsir); women trim a fingertip length from the end of their hair. With this, your Umrah is complete, Ihram ends, and everything that was restricted becomes allowed again. May Allah accept it — Umrah Mabroor!

Source: Dawat-e-Islami — Hajj o Umrah Ka Mukhtasar Tariqa · Rafeeq-ul-Haramayn, retold in our own words above.

Complete Method · Tareeqa

How to perform Hajj — the complete method

First the three types of Hajj, then the days of Hajj in order, step by step.

The 3 types of Hajj

  • Hajj-e-Tamattu — Perform Umrah in the months of Hajj, come out of Ihram, then enter a new Ihram for Hajj on 8 Zul-Hijjah. (The most common for overseas pilgrims.)
  • Hajj-e-Qiran — One Ihram with the combined intention of Umrah and Hajj together, staying in Ihram until 10 Zul-Hijjah.
  • Hajj-e-Ifrad — Ihram with the intention of Hajj only, without Umrah.

A sacrifice (Dam) is required in Tamattu and Qiran; a Qurbani animal is also part of the 10th day rites for every pilgrim as explained below.

Before 8 Zul-Hijjah

  • Tamattu pilgrims: complete Umrah (see the Umrah method above), exit Ihram, and stay in Makkah
  • On the morning of 8 Zul-Hijjah, bathe, wear Ihram from where you are staying in Makkah
  • Make intention for Hajj and recite the Talbiyah — you are in Ihram again
8

8 Zul-Hijjah — Mina (Yawm-ut-Tarwiyah)

Travel to Mina and stay there, praying the 5 prayers — Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and the Fajr of the 9th — in Mina, shortening the 4-rakat prayers to 2 (Qasr) where applicable, each in its own time. Spend the night in remembrance, dua and rest.

9

9 Zul-Hijjah — Wuquf at Arafat

After sunrise, proceed calmly to Arafat. Pray Dhuhr and Asr together (combined and shortened) at Dhuhr time with the congregation. Then comes the greatest rite of Hajj: Wuquf-e-Arafat — standing in Arafat from after midday (zawal) until sunset, in dua, dhikr, Talbiyah and repentance. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Hajj is Arafat" (Tirmidhi). Do not leave Arafat before sunset.

9

Night of 9–10 — Muzdalifah

After sunset, move calmly to Muzdalifah (without praying Maghrib on the way). On reaching Muzdalifah, pray Maghrib and Isha together with one Azan and one Iqamah. Rest and sleep under the open sky, pray Fajr early, make dua at al-Mash'ar al-Haram until the light spreads, and collect pebbles (at least 49, or 70 if staying to the 13th) for Rami.

10

10 Zul-Hijjah — Rami, Qurbani, Halq (Eid day)

In Mina, throw 7 pebbles at Jamrat-ul-Aqabah (the big pillar only today), saying Bismillah, Allahu Akbar with each pebble. Then the Qurbani / Dam sacrifice. Then Halq or Taqsir (shave or trim the hair) — with this, the first exit from Ihram is achieved (everything becomes allowed except marital relations). Then go to Makkah for the next rite.

10

Tawaf-uz-Ziyarat

Perform Tawaf-uz-Ziyarat (Tawaf-ul-Ifadah) — 7 rounds around the Kaaba — and pray 2 rakat at Maqam-e-Ibrahim. If your Hajj type and sequence require it (Qiran/Tamattu), also perform the Sa'i of Hajj between Safa and Marwah if it was not already done after Tawaf-e-Qudum. This Tawaf is a pillar of Hajj and is best done on the 10th (it may be done up to sunset of the 12th). Now Ihram fully ends.

11

11–12 (13) Zul-Hijjah — Rami & nights in Mina

Spend the nights of Ayyam-ut-Tashreeq in Mina. On the 11th and 12th, after midday (zawal), throw 7 pebbles each at all three Jamarat in order — small, middle, then Aqabah — making dua after the first two. Pilgrims who leave Mina before sunset on the 12th may finish here; whoever stays past sunset stays for the 13th and repeats Rami on the 13th as well.

✦

Before leaving Makkah — Tawaf-ur-Rukhsat

When you finally depart Makkah, perform the farewell Tawaf, Tawaf-ur-Rukhsat (Tawaf-ul-Wida) — 7 rounds — as your last act in the city. (Women who are in menstruation are excused from this Tawaf.) Your Hajj is complete — may Allah grant you Hajj Mabroor, whose reward is nothing but Paradise (Bukhari & Muslim).

School-specific details can differ — follow your group scholar for rulings.
Source: Dawat-e-Islami — A Brief Method of Hajj · Ba Tasweer Umrah o Hajj, retold in our own words above.

Umrah & Hajj Guides

Guides for every rite

Clear guides in simple English, each one written out in full right here on this page.

01Umrah Step by Step

The whole Umrah, in the right order:

  • 1. Ihram at the Meeqat — Bathe, trim nails, put on Ihram, pray 2 rakat, make the intention for Umrah and recite the Talbiyah. From this moment the rules of Ihram apply: no perfume, no cutting hair or nails, no arguing.
  • 2. Enter Masjid al-Haram — Enter with the right foot while making dua, and make heartfelt dua at the first sight of the Kaaba.
  • 3. Tawaf — 7 rounds — In wudu, start in line with the Black Stone, say Bismillah, Allahu Akbar, signal towards it with the right hand, and walk anti-clockwise with the Kaaba on your left. Men uncover the right shoulder (Idtiba) and walk briskly (Ramal) in the first 3 rounds if it is easy.
  • 4. Pray 2 rakat & drink Zamzam — Pray behind Maqam-e-Ibrahim if you find space without troubling anyone, otherwise anywhere in the Haram; then drink Zamzam in three breaths and make dua.
  • 5. Sa'i — 7 lengths — Begin at Safa, face the Kaaba and make dua, then walk to Marwah (length 1) and back (length 2), finishing the 7th length at Marwah. Men walk briskly between the two green markers; women walk at a normal pace.
  • 6. Halq or Taqsir — Men shave the whole head (Halq — more reward) or trim the hair of the whole head; women trim a fingertip length from the ends. Umrah is complete and Ihram ends.

Source: Dawat-e-Islami — Hajj o Umrah Ka Mukhtasar Tariqa, retold in our own words.

02Hajj Step by Step

The days of Hajj, 8 to 13 Zul-Hijjah, one by one:

  • 8 Zul-Hijjah — Mina — Enter Ihram for Hajj from where you are staying, travel to Mina, pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and the next Fajr there (shortening the 4-rakat prayers), and spend the night.
  • 9 Zul-Hijjah — Arafat — After sunrise, proceed calmly to Arafat. Pray Dhuhr and Asr together and shortened at Dhuhr time. Then Wuquf: stand in Arafat from after midday until sunset in dua, dhikr and repentance — the Prophet ﷺ said, "Hajj is Arafat." Do not leave before sunset.
  • Night of 9–10 — Muzdalifah — After sunset move to Muzdalifah without praying Maghrib on the way. Pray Maghrib and Isha together with one Azan and one Iqamah, rest under the open sky, pray Fajr early, make dua, and collect your pebbles (49, or 70 if staying to the 13th).
  • 10 Zul-Hijjah — the busiest day — In Mina, throw 7 pebbles at Jamrat-ul-Aqabah only, saying Bismillah, Allahu Akbar with each. Then the sacrifice (Qurbani / Dam), then Halq or Taqsir — the first exit from Ihram. Then go to Makkah for Tawaf-uz-Ziyarat and the Sa'i of Hajj if it is due; with this, Ihram ends completely.
  • 11–12 (13) Zul-Hijjah — Mina & Rami — Spend the nights in Mina. Each day after midday, throw 7 pebbles at each of the three Jamarat in order — small, middle, then Aqabah — making dua after the first two. Whoever leaves before sunset on the 12th is done; whoever stays past sunset also performs Rami on the 13th.
  • Departure — Tawaf-ur-Rukhsat — Before finally leaving Makkah, perform the farewell Tawaf of 7 rounds as your last act in the city.

Source: Dawat-e-Islami, retold in our own words.

03Excellence of Hajj

Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam, an obligation once in a lifetime for every Muslim who has the health and the means to make the journey: "And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to undertake it" (Qur'an 3:97). Its excellence, in the words of the Prophet ﷺ:

  • A completely fresh start — "Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit any obscenity or sin returns as pure as the day his mother gave birth to him." (Bukhari & Muslim)
  • The reward is Paradise — Asked which deed is best, the Prophet ﷺ mentioned faith in Allah and His Messenger, then striving in Allah's path, then an accepted Hajj — and he said: "The reward of Hajj Mabroor (an accepted Hajj) is nothing but Paradise." (Bukhari & Muslim)
  • Previous sins erased — Hajj wipes out the sins that came before it, just as Islam and Hijrah wipe out what came before them. (Muslim)
  • Guests of Ar-Rahman — Those who come for Hajj and Umrah are the guests of Allah: when they call upon Him, He answers them, and when they seek His forgiveness, He forgives them. (Ibn Majah)
  • The Day of Arafat — "There is no day on which Allah frees more people from the Fire than the Day of Arafat." (Muslim) The pilgrim standing there in dua is at the very heart of this mercy.
  • Even the journey counts — Every step, expense and hardship on the way is written as reward; the one who comes out purely for Allah returns home spiritually reborn and wealthy in good deeds rather than poor.

Source: Dawat-e-Islami — Excellence of Hajj, retold in our own words.

04Virtues of Hajj & Its Rulings

Alongside its virtues (Guide 03), every pilgrim should know which acts the Hajj stands on, and which must not be missed:

  • The three obligations (Fara'id) — Hajj is not valid without all three: 1) Ihram — entering the sacred state with the intention, from the Meeqat. 2) Wuquf-e-Arafat — being present within the boundary of Arafat at any moment from midday of 9 Zul-Hijjah until dawn of the 10th. 3) Tawaf-uz-Ziyarat — the Tawaf performed after returning from Arafat, best done on 10 Zul-Hijjah and no later than sunset of the 12th.
  • The necessary acts (Wajibat) — Staying at Muzdalifah in the night after Arafat; Sa'i between Safa and Marwah; Rami, throwing the pebbles at the Jamarat on their days; the sacrifice, which is wajib for the Tamattu and Qiran pilgrim; Halq or Taqsir (shaving or trimming the hair); and the farewell Tawaf for pilgrims who live outside Makkah. Leaving out a wajib act on purpose is a sin, and the Hajj is completed by offering a compensatory sacrifice (Dam).
  • The Sunnah acts — Tawaf-e-Qudum on arrival for the Ifrad and Qiran pilgrim, spending the night of 8 Zul-Hijjah in Mina, running between the green markers in Sa'i, and the other practices of the Prophet ﷺ that fill the journey with reward.
  • The three types — Ifrad (Hajj alone), Qiran (Umrah and Hajj together in one Ihram) and Tamattu (Umrah first, then a fresh Ihram for Hajj) — explained in "How to perform Hajj" above.

Source: Dawat-e-Islami — The Virtues of Hajj and Its Rulings, retold in our own words.

05Umrah During Hajj Days

Can you start a new Umrah during the days of Hajj, 9–13 Zul-Hijjah? The ruling of Darulifta Ahlesunnat, summarised:

  • The ruling — In the Hanafi school, tying a new Ihram for a separate Umrah on five days — 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 Zul-Hijjah — is Makrooh-e-Tahrimi (prohibitively disliked), so it should not be done.
  • Why — These days belong to the rites of Hajj itself: the stay at Arafat, the sacrifice, the Rami of the Jamarat and the days of Tashreeq in Mina. They are not set aside for a separate Umrah.
  • What this does not cover — The Umrah that forms part of Hajj-e-Tamattu or Hajj-e-Qiran is a different matter: it is performed in the months of Hajj before the 8th, as part of the Hajj package itself, and is not the "new Umrah" this ruling is about.
  • How to plan — If you want an extra Umrah around Hajj, complete it before 9 Zul-Hijjah or wait until after the 13th, when Umrah can be performed again as normal.

Source: Darulifta Ahlesunnat, Dawat-e-Islami — ruling on Umrah during the days of Hajj, summarised in our own words. For a ruling on your own situation, ask a scholar.

06Hajj & Umrah at a Glance

Both journeys on one card — a first read, or a last-minute revision before you travel:

  • Umrah in one line — Ihram with intention → Tawaf (7 rounds) → 2 rakat at Maqam-e-Ibrahim → Sa'i (7 lengths) → Halq or Taqsir. Four rites, usually completed in two to three hours.
  • Hajj in one line — 8th: Mina · 9th: Arafat until sunset, then the night at Muzdalifah · 10th: Rami, Qurbani, Halq, Tawaf-uz-Ziyarat · 11th–13th: nights in Mina with Rami each day · Farewell Tawaf before leaving Makkah.
  • Shared ground rules — Both journeys begin with Ihram at the Meeqat and the Talbiyah, both include Tawaf and Sa'i, and in both the hair is cut at the end to leave the state of Ihram.
  • Madinah — Pray in Masjid-e-Nabawi, present yourself at the Rawdah with a Nusuk permit, offer Salam at the blessed chamber with full respect, and visit Masjid Quba, where praying 2 rakat carries the reward of a complete Umrah (Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah).
  • Before you travel — Learn the order of the rites by heart, keep your chosen duas written down, and keep saying the Talbiyah from the moment of Ihram until your Tawaf begins.

Source: Dawat-e-Islami — Hajj o Umrah Aik Nazar Main, retold in our own words.

Nusuk app, Rawdah, visa & packing

Rawdah permit in the Nusuk app

Visa basics

  • Umrah visa or tourist e-visa, depending on your country
  • Passport valid for at least 6 months
  • Apply only through official channels or licensed agents
  • Rules differ by nationality — always check the latest guidance

Packing checklist

  • Ihram garments (men) and a spare set
  • Comfortable sandals plus a small shoe bag
  • Unscented toiletries for Ihram days
  • Prayer mat, tasbih and a small duas book
  • Power bank and a universal travel adapter

Before you book — 4 honest tips

A package is a big purchase. Check these first, whoever you book with.

  • Ask for the exact hotel name and its real walking distance to the Haram gates.
  • Confirm whether the visa, transfers and Ziyarat tours are included or extra.
  • Get the full price in writing — including taxes — before paying any advance.
  • Pay only to a verifiable business account, never to an unknown personal account.

Azkar & Duas

Azkar & duas for the journey

Short, well-known supplications in Arabic with English translation and when to read them — for every day, and for Umrah and Hajj.

Every morning

Morning Azkar

أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ

"We have entered the morning and the whole kingdom belongs to Allah. All praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner."

Read after Fajr. Part of the daily morning remembrances (Muslim).

Every evening

Evening Azkar

أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ

"We have entered the evening and the whole kingdom belongs to Allah. All praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner."

Read after Asr / before Maghrib, the evening counterpart of the morning azkar (Muslim).

Morning & evening · protection

Dua for Protection

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ

"In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing."

Read 3 times in the morning and 3 times in the evening (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi).

Start of any journey

Dua for Travel (Safar)

سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ ۝ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ

"Glory to Him who has made this subservient to us, and we could never have controlled it ourselves. And surely, to our Lord we are returning."

Read when you board your transport and set off (Qur'an 43:13–14).

Umrah · entering Ihram

Talbiyah — at Ihram

لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ

"Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Truly all praise, blessings and dominion belong to You. You have no partner."

Recite after making the intention and entering Ihram at the Meeqat, and repeat it often until Tawaf begins.

Umrah & Hajj · during Tawaf

Dua in Tawaf

رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ

"Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."

Traditionally read between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone in every round (Qur'an 2:201).

Umrah & Hajj · Sa'i

Dua at Safa — start of Sa'i

إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ ۖ فَمَنْ حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا

"Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah — there is no blame upon him for walking between them."

Read on reaching Safa before starting Sa'i, then face the Kaaba and make dua (Qur'an 2:158).

Umrah & Hajj · drinking Zamzam

Dua at Zamzam

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا وَاسِعًا، وَشِفَاءً مِنْ كُلِّ دَاءٍ

"O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and healing from every illness."

Make this dua while drinking Zamzam, facing the Qiblah (Ibn Majah).

Hajj · Day of Arafat (9 Zul-Hijjah)

Best Dua of Arafat

لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things."

The best supplication on the Day of Arafah — repeat it abundantly during Wuquf (Tirmidhi).

Hajj · night of Muzdalifah

Dua at Muzdalifah

رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ۝ رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ

"Our Lord, accept this from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing. Our Lord, make us submissive to You."

After praying Maghrib and Isha together at Muzdalifah, rest, then remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram after Fajr (Qur'an 2:127–128, 2:198).

Hajj · Rami (stoning)

Takbir at Rami

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ

"In the name of Allah — Allah is the Greatest."

Say this with every pebble thrown at the Jamarat in Mina, on 10–13 Zul-Hijjah.

Madinah · at Roza-e-Rasool ﷺ

Salutations at Roza-e-Rasool

السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا خِيرَةَ اللَّهِ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ

"Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet of Allah. Peace be upon you, O the chosen of Allah from His creation."

Present yourself calmly and quietly before the Sacred Chamber in Masjid an-Nabawi, offer these salutations, then also greet Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA) beside him.

Each dua above carries its Qur'an or hadith reference with it, so you can look it up any time.

Raka'at Table

How many raka'at in each Namaz?

Fajr — 4 total

  • 2 Sunnah (emphasised)
  • 2 Farz

Dhuhr — 12 total

  • 4 Sunnah
  • 4 Farz
  • 2 Sunnah
  • 2 Nafl (optional)

Asr — 8 total

  • 4 Sunnah (non-emphasised)
  • 4 Farz

Maghrib — 7 total

  • 3 Farz
  • 2 Sunnah
  • 2 Nafl (optional)

Isha — 17 total

  • 4 Sunnah
  • 4 Farz
  • 2 Sunnah
  • 2 Nafl (optional)
  • 3 Witr (Wajib)
  • 2 Nafl (optional)

Jumu'ah (Friday)

  • Replaces Dhuhr on Friday
  • 2 Farz with the congregation after the Khutbah
  • Prayed in the masjid where possible
Wudu & Prayer Basics

Wudu step by step

1

Intention & Bismillah

Make the intention in your heart and say Bismillah. Using a miswak is a much-loved Sunnah. Wash both hands up to the wrists 3 times.

2

Mouth

Rinse the mouth 3 times, swirling the water around well. Gargle gently too — except when fasting, when deep gargling is avoided.

3

Nose

Sniff water up into the nose with the right hand and blow it out with the left hand, 3 times — gently when fasting, without drawing the water up strongly.

4

Face

Wash the whole face 3 times: from the hairline down to below the chin, and from ear to ear, so that no part of the face is left dry.

5

Arms

Wash the right arm, then the left, up to and including the elbows, 3 times each, passing wet fingers through the fingers of the other hand.

6

Head — Masah

With wet hands, wipe the whole head once, passing the palms and fingers from the front of the head to the back and back again.

7

Ears & neck

Wipe the inside of the ears with the index fingers and their backs with the thumbs, once. Then wipe the back of the neck with the backs of the fingers.

8

Feet & closing dua

Wash the right foot, then the left, up to and including the ankles, 3 times, rubbing between the toes. Finish by reciting the Shahadah and this dua: “Allahummaj-'alni minat-tawwabin, waj-'alni minal-mutatahhirin” — O Allah, make me among those who repent often, and among those who purify themselves.

How to pray — in short

  • Stand facing Qibla, make intention, say Allahu Akbar
  • Recite Surah Al-Fatiha and another surah in the first 2 raka'at
  • Bow (Ruku), stand, then prostrate twice (Sujood) — that is 1 raka'at
  • Sit for Tashahhud, and end with Salam to the right and left

Good habits

  • Pray as early in the time as you reasonably can
  • Keep a prayer mat and a quiet corner ready at home
  • Learn the meaning of what you recite — it brings khushu (focus)
  • Missed a prayer? Make it up (Qaza) as soon as you can

The 4 Farz (obligatory) acts of Wudu

  • Washing the face, once
  • Washing both arms, including the elbows, once
  • Wiping (Masah of) at least a quarter of the head, once
  • Washing both feet, including the ankles, once

Without these four, Wudu is not complete. Everything else in the steps above is Sunnah — it completes the Wudu and adds reward.

What breaks Wudu

  • Anything coming out of the private parts — urine, stool or wind
  • Blood or pus that flows out from anywhere on the body
  • Vomiting a mouthful or more
  • Sleeping while lying down or leaning against something, fainting, or losing one's senses
  • Laughing aloud during the prayer itself (Hanafi ruling)

If any of these happen, make Wudu again before praying. These rulings follow the Hanafi school, the same method used throughout this page.

Complete Method · Tareeqa

How to pray Namaz — step by step (Hanafi)

The complete method of one prayer, shown here with 2 rakat; the same steps repeat in every rakat as noted.

1

Wudu & preparation

Perform Wudu (see the steps above), wear clean clothes, stand on a clean place at the prayer time, and face the Qibla. Make the intention (niyyah) in your heart for the prayer you are offering — intention is in the heart; saying it verbally is also fine.

2

Qiyam — standing correctly

Stand upright facing the Qibla, keeping a gap of about four fingers between the feet, toes pointing towards the Qibla, gaze lowered to the place of Sajdah.

3

Takbir-e-Tahrima

Raise both hands up to the ears (thumbs touching the earlobes; women raise hands up to the shoulders), then say “Allahu Akbar” and fold the hands below the navel — right hand over the left (women fold their hands on the chest). Prayer has now begun; talking and eating/drinking are forbidden from here.

4

Sana, Ta'awwuz & Tasmiyah

Recite the Sana: “Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik, wa tabarakasmuk, wa ta'ala jadduk, wa la ilaha ghayruk.” Then Ta'awwuz: “A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim.” Then Tasmiyah: “Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim.” — all quietly.

5

Surah Al-Fatiha + a Surah

Recite Surah Al-Fatiha completely, saying Ameen quietly at its end. Then recite another Surah or at least three short verses (e.g. Surah Al-Ikhlas). When praying behind an Imam, the follower does not recite Fatiha or a Surah in the audible prayers — listen attentively instead.

6

Ruku — bowing

Say Allahu Akbar and bow: back level and straight, hands resting on the knees with fingers apart, head in line with the back. Recite “Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem” 3 times (or 5 or 7).

7

Qawmah — standing up straight

Rise from Ruku saying “Sami'Allahu liman hamidah” (the followers say “Rabbana lakal-hamd”), and stand completely straight and still for a moment, arms at the sides.

8

Sajdah — prostration (twice)

Say Allahu Akbar and go down: knees first, then hands, then nose and forehead on the ground. Seven bones touch the ground; fingers face the Qibla, elbows kept away from the sides (women keep the body gathered and compact). Recite “Subhana Rabbiyal A'la” 3 times. Sit briefly (Jalsah) completely still, then perform the second Sajdah in the same way. One rakat is now complete — stand up for the second rakat and repeat steps 5–8 (without Sana and Ta'awwuz).

9

Tashahhud (Qa'dah)

After the second rakat, sit on the left foot with the right foot upright (women sit on the left side with both feet out to the right), hands on the thighs, and recite Attahiyyat (the Tashahhud), raising the index finger at “la ilaha” and lowering it at “illallah”. In a 3- or 4-rakat prayer, stand up after Tashahhud for the remaining rakat and sit again at the end.

10

Durood Sharif & Dua

In the final sitting, after Tashahhud recite Durood-e-Ibrahim: “Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidum-Majid. Allahumma barik 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidum-Majid.” Then make a short dua from the Qur'an and Sunnah.

11

Salam — ending the prayer

Turn the face to the right and say “Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullah”, then to the left and say it again. Your prayer is complete. Afterwards, dhikr and dua are highly recommended.

Men & women — the differences in brief

  • Takbir: men raise hands to the ears; women raise hands to the shoulders, from inside the covering
  • Folding hands: men below the navel; women on the chest
  • Ruku: men bow fully with a straight, level back; women bow only slightly, just enough for the hands to reach the knees
  • Sajdah: men keep elbows raised and away from the body and thighs apart; women prostrate in a gathered way, arms close to the body
  • Sitting: men sit on the left foot with the right foot raised; women sit with both feet emerging to the right side

These are the Hanafi-method differences; other schools of fiqh have some differences of detail.

Umrah · RulingsUmrah Badal: How to Perform Umrah on Behalf of Someone Else

Umrah Badal, also called proxy Umrah, means performing Umrah on behalf of another person who cannot perform it themselves, so that the reward of the Umrah reaches them. Families most often ask about it for a parent who has passed away, or for one who longed to visit the Kaaba but whose health no longer allows the journey. Badal is firmly established in the Sunnah, as long as its conditions are met. Allah says: "Complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah" (Quran 2:196), and the scholars explain that a rite owed to Allah can be fulfilled by one person on behalf of another.

Who it is allowed for: The scholars are unanimous that Umrah Badal is permissible for a deceased Muslim, and performing it for a parent who wished for it is among the finest acts of kindness after their death. It is also permissible for a living Muslim who is permanently unable to travel: old age that makes the journey impossible, a chronic illness with no expected cure, or a lasting disability. It is NOT permissible for a healthy person who is able to travel and simply prefers to send someone else in their place. And where the inability is temporary, such as an illness that is expected to pass, the right course is to wait until they recover and perform Umrah themselves.

The evidence: Abu Razin (may Allah be pleased with him) asked about his elderly father, who could neither perform Hajj nor Umrah nor travel, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Perform Hajj on behalf of your father and perform Umrah" (Sunan Abi Dawud 1810, Jami at-Tirmidhi 930, graded sahih). A woman of Khath'am asked about her elderly father, who could not sit firmly on a mount, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) answered "Yes" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim). Another woman told the Prophet (peace be upon him) that her mother had vowed to perform Hajj and then died; he told her to perform it for her, explaining that the debt owed to Allah has more right to be paid (Sahih al-Bukhari).

The conditions: First, the performer must be a Muslim of sound mind who has already performed his own Umrah. This comes from the hadith of Shubrumah: when a man told the Prophet (peace be upon him) he was performing Hajj for Shubrumah and had not yet performed his own, the Prophet said: "Perform Hajj for yourself first, then perform Hajj on behalf of Shubrumah" (Sunan Abi Dawud 1811). Second, the intention (niyyah) must clearly name the person the Umrah is for. Third, one Umrah is for one person only; two people cannot be combined in a single Umrah. Fourth, the rites must be physically performed in Makkah by the performer himself; there is no remote or symbolic Umrah. Fifth, there is no chain deputation: the person appointed performs the Umrah himself and cannot pass it on to a third person. Note that some Maliki scholars disliked Badal for the deceased unless there was a bequest, so when in doubt, follow a trusted scholar.

Step by step: 1. Perform your own Umrah first and complete it fully, ending with the haircut. 2. For a Badal Umrah in the same trip, leave the Haram boundary and enter ihram from outside it, most commonly at Masjid Aisha at Tan'eem, making the niyyah for the other person by name: "O Allah, I intend Umrah on behalf of my father." 3. Book the Nusuk Umrah permit in your own name: the permit is for the traveller who enters the Haram, while the intention is for the other person. 4. Perform Tawaf, Sa'i and the haircut exactly as in a normal Umrah, keeping the person in your intention and in your duas throughout.

If you hire someone: Many families pay a student of knowledge or a resident of Makkah to perform a Badal Umrah. This is allowed, but agree only the genuine costs in advance, such as transport and a fair fee, in clear words. Beware of agents selling a "guaranteed" Badal: no one can guarantee how Allah accepts an act of worship. Choose someone known for honesty, and ask them to confirm once the rites are complete.

Madinah · TravelMadinah Airport to Masjid Nabawi: Taxi, Bus and Prices (2026)

Prince Mohammad bin Abdulaziz International Airport (MED) is the arrival point for most pilgrims visiting Madinah. The airport sits about 15 to 20 km from Masjid Nabawi, and the drive to the Central Haram area takes about 20 to 30 minutes in normal traffic. You have four real options: the official airport taxi, a pre-booked private transfer, the city bus, or a ride-hailing app. This guide gives the current prices and the honest pros and cons of each, plus what to do if you are heading straight on to Makkah.

Official airport taxi, fixed fare: The airport publishes a fixed tariff for its official taxis: SAR 75 for a car carrying up to five passengers, and SAR 90 for a larger vehicle carrying up to seven, to the Central Haram area, a trip of about 20 km. Use the official taxi queue inside the terminal and the licensed operators who run it, including Imtiaz Taibah, SATCO, Lemo Safwa and Al Safi Taxi. Because the fare is fixed by the tariff, there is nothing to negotiate and nothing extra to agree; if a driver asks for more than the tariff, simply walk to the next car in the queue.

Private pre-booked transfers: Hotels and transfer companies sell pre-booked pickups, with sedans starting from about SAR 150 per vehicle. That is roughly double the official taxi fare for the same road, so it is worth it only if you want a driver waiting with a name board, help with your luggage, and a car arranged in advance for a large family or a very late flight. For most pilgrims, the official taxi makes the same journey for less money and with no booking at all.

Madinah Bus Route 400, the budget option: Route 400 of the Madinah Bus network runs between the airport and the Prophet's Mosque 24 hours a day, with buses about every 30 minutes. The ride takes 25 to 40 minutes depending on traffic and stops. The fare is only a few riyals; published reports vary between SAR 3.45 and SAR 14, so confirm the current fare at the stop before you ride. The bus is the best option for a solo traveller with light bags, and the least practical for a family arriving tired with heavy suitcases.

Uber, Careem and the train question: Uber and Careem both operate at Madinah airport and are a comfortable middle option, with the fare shown in the app before you ride. One common confusion needs clearing up: there is NO Haramain high-speed train station at Madinah airport. The Madinah Haramain station is a city terminal, and a taxi from the airport to that station costs from about SAR 100, so the train only makes sense if you are genuinely travelling on to Makkah or Jeddah, not to reach the Haram.

Heading straight to Makkah: If your plan is to go directly to Makkah, take a taxi from the airport to the SAPTCO station in Madinah, about SAR 15 to 25 and 10 to 15 minutes away. From there, the SAPTCO bus to Makkah costs about SAR 80 to 85 per person and takes 5 to 6 hours. The bus stops for 15 to 20 minutes at the miqat of Masjid Dhul Hulayfah (Abyar Ali), just outside Madinah, where pilgrims enter ihram, so have your ihram ready and do not sleep through the stop.

Practical tips: If you land late at night, use the official taxi queue; it is staffed around the clock and the fixed fare removes any argument. Keep some small cash in Saudi riyals for your first hours, even if you plan to pay by app later. Have your hotel name and its location near the Haram ready to show the driver, ideally in Arabic from your booking confirmation. And if your group travels on to Makkah later in the trip, shared vans leaving from near the Prophet's Mosque charge about SAR 50 per person, a useful middle option between the bus and a private car.

Umrah · Step by StepSecond Umrah in One Trip: How to Do Another Umrah from Masjid Aisha (Tan'eem)

You have finished your first Umrah and you still have three or four days left in Makkah. The question almost every pilgrim asks is simple: can I do it again? The short answer is yes. The majority of scholars allow more than one Umrah in a single trip, especially for a traveller who has come from far away and may not return soon. The method is well known, and it starts at a small mosque on the edge of Makkah called Masjid Aisha, at Tan'eem.

Where the practice comes from: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) could not complete her Umrah because of her menses, while the other wives completed Hajj Tamattu with a separate Umrah. She was upset, so the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) told her brother Abdur-Rahman to take her to Tan'im, so she could enter ihram there and perform her Umrah (Sahih al-Bukhari 1215, Sahih Muslim 1211). That is why the mosque at Tan'eem is called Masjid Aisha. The reward is real too. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'Umrah is an expiation for the sins committed between it and the previous Umrah' (agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim).

Why a fresh ihram is needed: Your first Umrah ends when you shave your head or shorten your hair. At that moment the state of ihram is over. You cannot simply start a second Umrah from inside the Haram, because the miqat for anyone already in Makkah is to go outside the sacred boundary, an area called al-Hill. The nearest and easiest place is Masjid Aisha at Tan'eem, about 7 to 8 kilometres from the Grand Mosque, a drive of 15 to 25 minutes. Other places outside the boundary, such as Ji'ranah and Hudaybiyah, are also valid, but Tan'eem is the one most pilgrims use.

Step by step: 1. Book your new Umrah permit first. The Nusuk system allows only one active Umrah permit at a time, so book the new slot before you book a taxi, and keep the permit ready in the Nusuk app. 2. Do ghusl and trim your nails at the hotel, so you are not rushed at Tan'eem. 3. Take a taxi to Masjid Aisha and agree the fare and the waiting arrangement with the driver before you set off. 4. At the mosque, make the intention (niyyah) for Umrah and pray two rak'ahs, then say the talbiyah. 5. Return to the Haram and perform Tawaf, pray two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, drink Zamzam, then do Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, and finish by shaving or shortening your hair. The whole excursion usually takes about an hour plus the time of the rites themselves.

For yourself or for someone else: A second Umrah can be for yourself, or on behalf of a deceased loved one, or an elderly or ill person who cannot travel. Scholars including Ibn Baz (may Allah have mercy on him) said there is no harm in this, as long as you leave the sanctuary to enter ihram. Many pilgrims use their extra days in Makkah exactly this way, dedicating one Umrah to a parent who has passed away.

A note of balance: The Prophet's own practice was one Umrah per journey. He performed four Umrahs in his life, each in a different year, and he never repeated Umrah from Tan'eem himself. Scholars who permit repetition still advise balance: do not exhaust yourself or your elderly family with back to back Umrahs in the heat. One calm, focused Umrah is better than three rushed ones. Go at a quiet hour, such as early morning or after midnight, rest between rites, and keep the second Umrah simple.

Practical tips: Keep elderly family rested and hydrated at the hotel if they are not joining you. Carry water and a small snack. If you are travelling with a group, agree the meeting point at the Haram before you leave, because the mosque gets crowded at prayer times. And if your plans change, cancel the old permit slot before it starts and book a fresh one, because a permit time cannot be edited.
