Umrah Visa · Rejection HelpUmrah Visa Rejected? Common Reasons & How to Reapply

A rejected Umrah visa feels like the end of the journey, but most refusals come down to a small number of fixable issues. Saudi authorities do not publish a complete list of rejection reasons, and there is no standard public appeal process — in practice you find the reason, fix it, and submit a new application. Here are the reasons that come up most often, and what to do about each one.

1. Incorrect or inconsistent details — A wrong date of birth, a mistyped passport number, or a name spelled differently from the passport can sink an application. The official eVisa terms require true and accurate information and say an application with false or misleading details will be rejected. Once a tourist eVisa application is submitted it cannot be cancelled or refunded, so check every field against the passport before you pay.

2. Passport validity too short — The tourist eVisa requires at least 6 months of passport validity from your date of entry into Saudi Arabia. If your passport expires inside that window, renew it first and apply second — this is the cheapest fix of all.

3. Missing or invalid Nusuk Masar booking — Since 10 June 2025 a dedicated Umrah visa depends on accommodation and transport being documented and approved on the Nusuk Masar platform, and since January 2026 pre-booked accommodation through Nusuk-approved hotels and transport through licensed providers is required before the visa application is submitted. A hotel booking that cannot be verified — never real, already cancelled, or made through a channel the system cannot see — will block the visa. Book only through Nusuk-approved hotels and licensed transport providers, and keep the booking references.

4. ACWY vaccine record problems — Saudi Arabia asks every Hajj and Umrah traveller for a meningococcal ACWY vaccination record, with no exemption by nationality. The dose must have been given at least 10 days before arrival and within the last 3 years (polysaccharide vaccine) or 5 years (conjugate vaccine). The certificate must clearly state the vaccine name, its type and the date given — if the type is missing, the record counts as valid for 3 years only. An expired dose, or one given fewer than 10 days before arrival, is rejected even though a record exists.

5. Previous overstay or violation — If you overstayed a Saudi visa before, or were deported, later applications are likely to be refused. An open violation record leads to refusal, and this reason cannot be fixed by reapplying quickly.

6. Wrong channel or an unauthorised agent — There are three legitimate routes to Umrah: a dedicated Umrah visa through the Nusuk Umrah platform, a licensed travel agent, or a tourist eVisa for eligible nationalities. Unlicensed agents cause refusals: in February 2026 the Ministry suspended three Umrah companies over failures to provide approved accommodation, and a separate suspension affected 1,800 overseas agencies. Use only licensed agents and the official portals (visa.visitsaudi.com, Nusuk).

7. Photo problems — Photos must be recent, clear, on a white background, with the face fully visible. A cropped, dark or old photo is a common avoidable refusal.

8. Name mismatch across documents — The name, date of birth and passport number must match exactly across the passport, national ID (CNIC where applicable) and the application. Even a small spelling difference between documents can trigger a refusal.

9. Season cut-off dates — For the 1448H season, Umrah visa issuance ends 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027 and all pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027. Applications filed too close to the cut-off may not be processed. A dedicated Umrah visa issued in 2026 is valid for 30 days from issuance, so time your application to your travel dates rather than filing months ahead.

What to do after a rejection, step by step:

  1. Find the exact reason — check the application portal, the rejection email, or your provider's notice. If an agency applied for you, ask it for the specific status or error, not a general answer.
  2. Fix the underlying problem — correct the detail, replace the document, or sort out the booking before you apply again.
  3. Check your passport — renew first if it will have less than 6 months left on arrival.
  4. Pick the right visa type — if you are not eligible for the eVisa, a dedicated Umrah visa through Nusuk or a licensed agent is the route.
  5. Check the fee before reapplying — tourist eVisa fees are non-refundable when an application is unsuccessful, so a new application usually means paying again.
  6. Double-check everything before you submit — ask someone else to read your details against your passport.

Pre-application checklist:

  • Passport valid 6+ months from arrival date
  • Name, date of birth and passport number identical on every document
  • Recent photo, white background, face fully visible
  • ACWY certificate with correct vaccine, type and date, at least 10 days before arrival
  • Hotel and transport booked through Nusuk-approved providers, references saved
  • Application made on the official portal or through a licensed agent
  • Travel dates inside the 1448H season (entry before 23 March 2027, depart by 7 April 2027)

Umrah · Bosnia and Herzegovina GuideUmrah from Bosnia and Herzegovina — Visa & Flights Guide

Bosnian pilgrims now have one of the newest Umrah routes in Europe: Bosnia and Herzegovina is on the Saudi tourist eVisa list — added on 5 November 2026 — so you can apply for a tourist eVisa online before you fly, get a visa on arrival, or still use the dedicated Umrah visa route when you prefer a package. There are no direct flights from Sarajevo to Jeddah on most days, so the main route is one stop via Istanbul with Turkish Airlines, at about 6–8 hours in total including the layover. This guide covers both visa routes, the 1448H season dates, the documents and health rules, and the flights and fares. Travelling from elsewhere? Our newest companion guide, Umrah from North Macedonia, covers the same brand-new eVisa route for travellers from North Macedonia — the two countries were added to the list on the same day — and our Umrah from Serbia and Umrah from Croatia guides cover the region for travellers from Serbia and Croatia.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Umrah to Umrah expiates what is between them." (Sahih al-Bukhari 1773, Sahih Muslim 1349)

Do Bosnian pilgrims need a visa for Umrah? Yes — but you can get yours online in advance or at the airport. Bosnia and Herzegovina was added to the Saudi tourist eVisa list on 5 November 2026 — one of four countries added that day, alongside Mexico, Serbia and North Macedonia — and is one of the 72 countries named in the official eVisa Terms and Conditions at visa.visitsaudi.com, as also reported by Arab News, Khaleej Times, Gulf News and Saudi Life Guide. The dedicated Umrah visa through Nusuk remains available when you prefer everything arranged in a package. Our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out how the fees compare across the visa types.

Route 1: the tourist eVisa (or visa on arrival): Apply online at the official portal visa.visitsaudi.com. The eVisa costs SAR 535 in total, including the mandatory medical insurance (about US$143; the exact fee is shown in SAR at checkout on the portal). It is valid for 1 year with multiple entries and allows up to 90 days per visit. Your passport must be valid for at least six months from entry. Umrah is allowed on it outside the Hajj season — book the Umrah permit on the Nusuk app — and it is not valid for Hajj, which needs a separate Hajj visa, or for work. A visa on arrival is available on the same terms for Bosnian passport holders at Saudi international airports.

Route 2: the Umrah visa via Nusuk or an agent: Apply through the Nusuk app or a licensed travel agent, and enter Saudi Arabia within 30 days of the visa being issued. Since 20 July 2026 there is also a multiple-entry Umrah visa: valid for 365 days with up to 90 days of cumulative stay — each visit needs its own Nusuk service package and Umrah permit — and it is not usable during the Hajj season. Our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup and the permit booking step by step.

The 1448H season dates:

  • Umrah visas for the 1448H season have been issued since 31 May 2026.
  • Umrah visa issuance ends 9 March 2027.
  • The last entry date is 23 March 2027.
  • All Umrah visa holders must depart by 7 April 2027.

Documents and health checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months at entry.
  • Meningococcal ACWY vaccination is mandatory, at least 10 days before arrival — the conjugate vaccine is valid for 5 years and the polysaccharide vaccine for 3 years — with the certificate ready to show.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
  • A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are arriving from, or transiting, a yellow-fever risk country.
  • Women of all ages may travel for Umrah without a mahram — our Umrah for women travelling alone guide has the rules and practical detail.

Flights from Bosnia and Herzegovina to Jeddah: There are no direct flights from Sarajevo (SJJ) to Jeddah (JED) on most days. The main route is Turkish Airlines via Istanbul: Sarajevo–Istanbul takes about 2 hours and Istanbul–Jeddah about 3h 45m, for a total journey of about 6–8 hours including the layover. Pegasus via Istanbul Sabiha Gokcen is a budget alternative, and flynas lists direct Sarajevo–Jeddah flights of about 4h 15m on some dates — worth checking if your travel dates are flexible. Fly into Jeddah (JED) for Makkah; Madinah (MED) is the other gateway. Fares are indicative, checked 23 Nov 2026, and change daily — check live prices before booking. Bosnia and Herzegovina uses the convertible mark (KM/BAM), and cards are widely accepted in Saudi Arabia. Sarajevo is 2 hours behind Jeddah (CET, UTC+1, against AST, UTC+3) — once you land, set your prayer alarms by the local Makkah and Madinah times in this site's Namaz section. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your stay splits between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi, while our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

What it costs: On the eVisa route you pay the SAR 535 visa fee yourself and book flights and hotels separately; on the Umrah visa route the visa comes inside the package. Umrah packages from Sarajevo start from KM 1,385 per person for 8 nights including return flights and hotels (Yuusr, prices checked 23 November 2026), which can work out simpler than booking each part separately. See our Makkah hotels guide before you book, and add up the full budget — visa, flights, hotels, food and local transport — before you commit.

Entering the Nusuk competition? Community members share free Nusuk key codes on this site. Pick one from our codes list, enter it in the Nusuk app, and you are in the draw for a free Umrah trip — no payment and no password is ever needed to use a code.

Step by step:

  1. Choose your dates inside the 1448H season.
  2. Apply for the tourist eVisa first at visa.visitsaudi.com — or choose the Umrah visa via Nusuk or a licensed travel agent.
  3. Get the meningococcal ACWY vaccine at least 10 days before travel.
  4. Book your flights 6–8 weeks ahead, and book your hotels.
  5. Book the free Umrah permit on the Nusuk app before entering Masjid al-Haram.
  6. Book the Rawdah permit too if you will visit Madinah.
  7. Pack using our Umrah packing list, with your Ihram garments on top of the bag.

A short practical checklist: Apply for the eVisa first, as soon as your dates are set, and carry a printed copy of the approved eVisa with your passport, valid for at least six months; install the Nusuk app and book your Umrah permit before you fly, and book the Rawdah permit in the same app as soon as your Madinah dates are fixed, because slots go quickly; book flights 6–8 weeks ahead for the best fares via Istanbul; choose a hotel near the Haram in Makkah so the five daily prayers are an easy walk — our Makkah hotels guide compares the areas; and carry your Ihram in your hand luggage and work through our Umrah packing list so nothing essential is left behind — read our Ihram rules guide so you are ready to enter Ihram before the miqat announcement on board.

Preparing for the journey itself: With the visa and flights settled, the rest is preparation. Choose your dates with the best time to perform Umrah guide, which compares weather, crowds and cost across the year, and learn the supplications from Tawaf Duas and the wider Umrah Duas collection before you fly, so the rites themselves feel familiar when you reach the Haram.

It is valid for 1 year with multiple entries and allows up to 90 days per visit. Your passport must be valid for at least six months from entry. Umrah is allowed on it outside the Hajj season — book the Umrah permit on the Nusuk app — and it is not valid for Hajj, which needs a separate Hajj visa, or for work. A visa on arrival is available on the same terms for Mexican passport holders at Saudi international airports.

Route 2: the Umrah visa via Nusuk or an agent: Apply through the Nusuk app or a licensed travel agent, and enter Saudi Arabia within 30 days of the visa being issued. Since 20 July 2026 there is also a multiple-entry Umrah visa: valid for 365 days with up to 90 days of cumulative stay — each visit needs its own Nusuk service package and Umrah permit — and it is not usable during the Hajj season. Our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup and the permit booking step by step.

The 1448H season dates:

  • Umrah visas for the 1448H season have been issued since 31 May 2026.
  • Umrah visa issuance ends 9 March 2027.
  • The last entry date is 23 March 2027.
  • All Umrah visa holders must depart by 7 April 2027.

Documents and health checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months at entry.
  • Meningococcal ACWY vaccination is mandatory, at least 10 days before arrival — the conjugate vaccine is valid for 5 years and the polysaccharide vaccine for 3 years — with the certificate ready to show.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Mexico.
  • A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are arriving from, or transiting, a yellow-fever risk country.
  • Women of all ages may travel for Umrah without a mahram — our Umrah for women travelling alone guide has the rules and practical detail.

Flights from Mexico to Jeddah: There are no direct flights from Mexico City (MEX) to Jeddah (JED). The best route is Turkish Airlines via Istanbul: Mexico City–Istanbul takes about 14h 15m and Istanbul–Jeddah about 3h 45m, for a total journey of around 20 hours including the layover. Turkish Airlines Mexico City–Jeddah return fares start from MXN 28,083 (30 Dec 2026–13 Jan 2027 dates, turkishairlines.com). One-stop alternatives run via Doha (Qatar Airways, about 20 hours) or Paris (Air France, about 20 hours), and one-way fares start from about SAR 3,133 via Doha (MakeMyTrip). Fly into Jeddah (JED) for Makkah; Madinah (MED) is the other gateway. Fares are indicative, checked 23 Nov 2026, and change daily — check live prices before booking. Mexico uses the Mexican peso (MXN), and cards are widely accepted in Saudi Arabia. Mexico City is 9 hours behind Jeddah (CST, UTC-6, against AST, UTC+3) — once you land, set your prayer alarms by the local Makkah and Madinah times in this site's Namaz section. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your stay splits between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi, while our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

What it costs: On the eVisa route you pay the SAR 535 visa fee yourself and book flights and hotels separately; on the Umrah visa route the visa comes inside the package. Flights are the biggest variable on this long route, then hotels near the Haram. See our Makkah hotels guide before you book, and add up the full budget — visa, flights, hotels, food and local transport — before you commit.

If you would rather depart from Bratislava airport itself, one-stop routes run via Istanbul (Turkish Airlines), or via Dubai, Doha or Vienna. Fly into Jeddah (JED) for Makkah; Madinah (MED) is the other gateway. Schedules are indicative, checked 23 Nov 2026 — check live schedules and prices before booking. Slovakia uses the euro (EUR), and cards are widely accepted in Saudi Arabia. Bratislava keeps CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer, so Jeddah is 2 hours ahead of Bratislava in winter and 1 hour ahead in summer, while Jeddah stays on AST (UTC+3) all year — once you land, set your prayer alarms by the local Makkah and Madinah times in this site's Namaz section. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your stay splits between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi, while our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

Umrah · Poland GuideUmrah from Poland — Visa & Flights Guide

Route 1: the tourist eVisa (or visa on arrival): Apply online at the official portal visa.visitsaudi.com. The eVisa costs SAR 535 in total, including the mandatory medical insurance (about US$143, about €125). It is valid for 1 year with multiple entries and allows up to 90 days per visit. Do Greek pilgrims need a visa for Umrah? Yes — but you can get yours online in advance or at the airport. Greece is on the Saudi tourist eVisa list, and the dedicated Umrah visa through Nusuk remains available when you prefer everything arranged in a package. Our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out how the fees compare across the visa types.

Route 1: the tourist eVisa (or visa on arrival): Apply online at the official portal visa.visitsaudi.com. The eVisa costs SAR 535 in total, including the mandatory medical insurance (about US$143, about €125). It is valid for 1 year with multiple entries and allows up to 90 days per visit. Your passport must be valid for at least six months, and you must be 18 or older to apply on your own. Umrah is allowed on it outside the Hajj season — book the Umrah permit on the Nusuk app — and it is not valid for Hajj or work. A visa on arrival is available on the same terms for Greek passport holders at Saudi international airports.

Route 2: the Umrah visa via Nusuk or an agent: Apply through the Nusuk app or a licensed travel agent, and enter Saudi Arabia within 30 days of the visa being issued. Since 20 July 2026 there is also a multiple-entry Umrah visa: valid for 365 days with up to 90 days of cumulative stay — each visit needs its own Nusuk service package and Umrah permit — and it is not usable during the Hajj season. Our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup and the permit booking step by step.

The 1448H season dates:

  • Umrah visa issuance ends 9 March 2027.
  • The last entry date is 23 March 2027.
  • All Umrah visa holders must depart by 7 April 2027.

Documents and health checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months at entry.
  • Meningococcal ACWY vaccination is mandatory, at least 10 days before arrival — the conjugate vaccine is valid for 5 years and the polysaccharide vaccine for 3 years — with the certificate ready to show.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Greece.
  • A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are arriving from, or transiting, a yellow-fever risk country.
  • Women of all ages may travel for Umrah without a mahram — our Umrah for women travelling alone guide has the rules and practical detail.

Flights from Greece to Jeddah: Aegean Airlines flies non-stop from Athens (ATH) to Jeddah (JED) daily — flight A3950 departs Athens at 22:20 and arrives in Jeddah at 02:50 the next day, a flight of 3h 30m; the return flight A3951 departs Jeddah at 03:50 and arrives in Athens at 06:30, taking 3h 40m. Saudia sells the same route as a codeshare. Round-trip fares start from about US$324 (KAYAK, December 2026 dates) — book ahead, as fares vary by date. Travellers from Thessaloniki connect via Athens or Istanbul. All fares are indicative, checked 22 Nov 2026, and change daily — check live prices before booking. Jeddah is 1 hour ahead of Greece in winter (EET, UTC+2) and at the same time in summer (EEST, UTC+3), while Jeddah stays on AST (UTC+3) all year — once you land, set your prayer alarms by the local Makkah and Madinah times in this site's Namaz section. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your stay splits between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi, while our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

What it costs: On the eVisa route you pay the SAR 535 visa fee yourself and book flights and hotels separately; on the Umrah visa route the visa comes inside the package. Flights are the biggest variable, then hotels near the Haram. See our Makkah hotels guide before you book, and our Umrah cost breakdown for a full budget picture.

Umrah · Australia GuideUmrah from Australia — Visa & Flights Guide

Australian pilgrims have one of the simplest visa routes to Umrah: Australia is on the Saudi tourist eVisa list, so you can apply online before you fly or pick up a visa on arrival, and still use the dedicated Umrah visa route when you prefer a package. The journey itself is the long part — there are no direct flights, and the fastest trips take about 19 hours. This guide covers both visa routes, the 1448H season dates, the documents and health rules, and Sydney, Melbourne and Perth flights and fares. The same eVisa route from the Southern Hemisphere is covered in our companion guide, Umrah from South Africa, and for Asia in Umrah from Malaysia and Umrah from Turkey, while our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide walks through the same online application step by step.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Umrah to Umrah expiates what is between them." (Sahih al-Bukhari 1773, Sahih Muslim 1349)

Do Australians need a visa for Umrah? Yes — but you can get yours online in minutes or at the airport. Australia is on the Saudi tourist eVisa list, and the dedicated Umrah visa through Nusuk remains available when you prefer everything arranged in a package. Our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out how the fees compare across the visa types.

Route 1: the tourist eVisa (or visa on arrival): Apply online at visa.visitsaudi.com. The eVisa costs SAR 535 in total, including the mandatory health insurance, is valid for 1 year with multiple entries, and allows up to 90 days per visit (90 days total per year). Umrah is allowed on it outside the Hajj season. A visa on arrival is available on the same terms at Saudi airports, including at the self-service kiosks. Note that travellers under 18 must be accompanied by a parent, grandparent or adult sibling over 18.

Route 2: the Umrah visa via Nusuk or an agent: Apply on the Nusuk Umrah platform or through a licensed Australian Umrah agent. Since July 2026 there is also a multiple-entry Umrah visa: valid for 365 days with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days, and inactive during the Hajj season. Our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup and the permit booking step by step.

A route that does not exist — the Package eVisa: The Package eVisa is not available for Australia. It covers only seven countries — Jordan, Egypt, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Mexico and Pakistan — so do not plan around it.

The 1448H season dates:

  • Umrah visa issuance ends 9 March 2027.
  • The last entry date is 23 March 2027.
  • Pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027.

Documents and health checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months at entry.
  • ACWY meningococcal vaccination is mandatory, at least 10 days before travel, with the certificate ready to show.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Australia.
  • A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you are arriving from, or transiting, a yellow-fever risk country.
  • Women of all ages may travel for Umrah without a mahram.

Flights from Australia to Jeddah: There are no direct flights from any Australian city to Jeddah — every option is 1-stop, over a distance of about 13,302 km. The fastest 1-stop options take about 19 hours: via Abu Dhabi with Etihad (about 19h 15m), via Dubai with Emirates (shortest 1-stop average about 19h 01m), via Singapore with Singapore Airlines (about 19h 55m), or via Doha with Qatar Airways (about 20h 09m). Departures are from Sydney and Melbourne; Perth connects through the same hubs. One-way fares start from about AU$790; returns start from about AU$1,674, typically AU$1,678–AU$2,394 (KAYAK, November 2026), with Etihad from AU$2,184.92. Book about 10 weeks ahead for the best prices — November is usually the cheapest month. All fares checked 19 Nov 2026, prices change daily. Jeddah is 7–8 hours behind Sydney, depending on Australian daylight saving (AEST/AEDT against AST UTC+3), so allow a gentle first day after landing. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your stay splits between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi, while our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

What it costs: On the eVisa route you pay the SAR 535 visa fee yourself and book flights and hotels separately; on the Umrah visa route the visa comes inside the package. Flights are the biggest variable on a trip this long, then hotels near the Haram. See our general Umrah cost guide and the Makkah hotels guide before you book.

Step by step:

  1. Choose your dates inside the 1448H season.
  2. Pick the visa route — tourist eVisa online or on arrival, or the Umrah visa via Nusuk or a licensed agent.
  3. Get the ACWY vaccine at least 10 days before travel.
  4. Book your flights and hotels (or your service package on the Umrah visa route).
  5. Get your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app.
  6. Book the Rawdah permit too if you will visit Madinah.
  7. Pack using our Umrah packing list.

Preparing for the journey itself: With the visa and flights settled, the rest is preparation. A 19-hour journey rewards planning: choose your dates with the best time to perform Umrah guide, which compares weather, crowds and cost across the year, and if you are travelling as a family — remembering that under-18s must be accompanied by a parent, grandparent or adult sibling — our Umrah with Kids guide covers prams, pacing and child-friendly hotels.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Is Australia on the Saudi tourist eVisa list? Yes. Australians can apply online at visa.visitsaudi.com for SAR 535 including mandatory health insurance (1 year, multiple entry, up to 90 days per visit), or get a visa on arrival on the same terms, and perform Umrah outside the Hajj season.
  • Are there direct flights from Australia to Jeddah? No — there are no direct flights from any Australian city. The fastest options are 1-stop at about 19 hours, via Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Singapore or Doha.
  • Can travellers under 18 fly in on a visa on arrival alone? No. Travellers under 18 must be accompanied by a parent, grandparent or adult sibling over 18.
  • Is the Package eVisa available for Australia? No. The Package eVisa covers only Jordan, Egypt, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Mexico and Pakistan.
  • When does the Umrah season end in 1448H? Visa issuance ends 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027.

Sources: Visit Saudi — official tourist eVisa portal (visa.visitsaudi.com) · Nusuk platform (nusuk.sa) · KAYAK — Australia–Jeddah fares, November 2026 (kayak.com.au) · Etihad Airways fares (etihad.com). All fares checked 19 Nov 2026, prices change daily.

Umrah · Morocco GuideUmrah from Morocco — Visa & Flights Guide

Moroccan pilgrims cannot use the Saudi tourist eVisa — Morocco is not on the eVisa list — so the Umrah visa through Nusuk or a licensed agent is the normal route. This guide covers the visa options, the 1448H season dates, the documents and health rules, and direct flights from Casablanca. Moroccan pilgrims travel under the same broad system as readers of our other non-eVisa country guides — compare Umrah from Egypt and Umrah from Kenya, contrast it with Umrah from Turkey, where the tourist eVisa does exist, and see our Asian guide to Umrah from Pakistan.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Moroccans need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Moroccan passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa before travelling, and Morocco is not among the nationalities eligible for the Saudi tourist eVisa, so for almost every Moroccan pilgrim the visa is a dedicated Umrah visa arranged through the Nusuk platform or a licensed Moroccan Umrah agent. Our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out the wider fee picture across the visa types.

Route 1: the Umrah visa via Nusuk: Apply on the Nusuk Umrah platform — direct application has been possible since August 2025 — or through a licensed Moroccan Umrah agent. A service package (hotel + transport) from an approved Nusuk provider is required, and you must get your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app before arrival. A standard Umrah visa must be used to enter within 30 days of issue, and then allows a stay of up to 90 days. Our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup and the permit booking step by step.

Route 2: the one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa (since July 2026): Since July 2026 Saudi Arabia issues a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa: it is valid for 365 days, with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days. Each visit needs a service package from an approved Nusuk provider and an Umrah permit before arrival, and the visa is inactive during the Hajj season.

Route 3: the exception — a used Western visa or residence: Moroccans holding a used US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa, or a permanent residence permit from the US, the UK or an EU country, can apply for the tourist eVisa through the KSA Visa portal or get a visa on arrival. Moroccans living in France with a valid French residence permit are routed to the online visa on the KSA Visa portal.

A route that does not exist — the Package Visa: Morocco is not on the Package Visa list — the Ministry of Tourism names only seven countries (Jordan, Egypt, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan) — so do not plan around it.

The 1448H season dates:

  • The Umrah season opened 31 May 2026.
  • Umrah visas may be issued until 9 March 2027.
  • The last entry date is 23 March 2027.
  • Pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027.

Documents and health checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months at entry.
  • ACWY meningococcal vaccination at least 10 days before arrival, with the certificate ready to show.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Morocco.
  • Yellow fever vaccination is only needed if you are arriving from, or transiting, a yellow-fever risk country.
  • Women of all ages may travel for Umrah without a mahram.
  • Children need their own passport and visa.

Flights from Casablanca to Jeddah: Casablanca Mohammed V (CMN) to Jeddah (JED) direct takes about 6 hours, flown by Saudia (about 14 times a week), Royal Air Maroc (about 4 times a week) and flynas; Saudia also flies Casablanca to Madinah (MED) direct. One-way fares start from about US$309 (Saudia, November 2026); round trips start from about US$460, typically about US$650–880. All fares checked 19 Nov 2026, prices change daily. From Marrakech, Tangier, Agadir or Fes, connect through Casablanca, or through Istanbul or Doha. Jeddah is 2 hours ahead of Casablanca (3 hours during Ramadan, when Morocco's clocks go back an hour). Book the Umrah permit in the Nusuk app before you fly, and arrive at Jeddah with your hotel and transport already booked. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your stay splits between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi, while our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

What it costs: The visa comes inside the Umrah package, so compare packages from licensed agents rather than paying for a visa alone. Flights are the biggest variable, then hotels near the Haram. See our general Umrah cost guide and the Makkah hotels guide before you book.

Step by step:

  1. Choose your dates inside the 1448H season.
  2. Pick the visa route — Umrah visa via Nusuk or an agent, or the eVisa exception if you hold a used US/UK/Schengen visa or Western residence.
  3. Get the ACWY vaccine at least 10 days before travel.
  4. Book your service package and flights.
  5. Get your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app.
  6. Book the Rawdah permit too if you will visit Madinah.
  7. Pack using our Umrah packing list.

Preparing for the journey itself: With the visa and flights settled, the rest is preparation. Learn the supplications from Umrah Duas and Tawaf Duas before you fly, so the rites themselves feel familiar when you reach the Haram.

  • Can Moroccans get a Saudi tourist eVisa? Not on a Moroccan passport alone — Morocco is not on the eVisa list. The only exception is for Moroccans holding a used US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa, or a permanent residence permit from the US, the UK or an EU country, who can apply through the KSA Visa portal or get a visa on arrival.
  • How do most Moroccans get their Umrah visa? Through a dedicated Umrah visa arranged on the Nusuk Umrah platform or by a licensed Moroccan Umrah agent, with a service package (hotel + transport) from an approved Nusuk provider, and the Umrah permit booked in the Nusuk app before arrival.
  • Is Morocco on the Package Visa list? No. The Ministry of Tourism names only seven countries for the Package Visa — Jordan, Egypt, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Mexico and Pakistan.
  • When does the Umrah season end in 1448H? Visa issuance ends 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027.

Umrah · Malaysia GuideUmrah from Malaysia — Visa & Flights Guide

Malaysia is one of the easiest passports for Umrah: it is on the Saudi tourist eVisa list, so Malaysians can apply online in minutes or get a visa on arrival, and still use the dedicated Umrah visa route when they prefer a package. This guide covers both routes, the 1448H season dates, the documents and health rules — including Makkah Route pre-clearance at KLIA — and Kuala Lumpur flights and fares. Compare the eVisa route here with Umrah from Turkey, contrast it with the agent-based routes in Umrah from Egypt, Umrah from Indonesia and our newest guide, Umrah from Morocco, and see how the picture looks in Umrah from Pakistan.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Malaysians need a visa for Umrah? Yes — but unlike most of our readers, you can get yours online in minutes or at the airport. Malaysia is on the Saudi tourist eVisa list, and the dedicated Umrah visa through Nusuk remains available when you prefer everything arranged in a package. Our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out how the fees compare across the visa types.

Route 1: the tourist eVisa: Apply at visa.visitsaudi.com. The fee is SAR 535, including health cover up to SAR 100,000. The visa is valid for one year with multiple entries and a cumulative stay of up to 90 days, and it covers Umrah outside the Hajj season — never Hajj. A visa on arrival on the same terms is available at Saudi international airports.

Route 2: the Umrah visa via Nusuk: Buy a service package from an approved provider on the Nusuk platform — direct application has been possible since August 2025 — or go through a licensed Malaysian agency registered with MOTAC, or a Tabung Haji package. A standard Umrah visa must be used to enter within 30 days of issue, then allows a stay of up to 90 days. Get your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app before arrival — our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup step by step.

Route 3: the one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa (since July 2026): Since July 2026 Saudi Arabia issues a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa: it is valid for 365 days, with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days. Each visit needs a service package from an approved Nusuk provider and an Umrah permit before arrival, and the visa is inactive during the Hajj season.

The 1448H season dates:

  • The Umrah season opened 31 May 2026.
  • Umrah visas may be issued until 9 March 2027.
  • The last entry date is 23 March 2027.
  • Pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027.

Documents and health checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months at entry.
  • ACWY meningococcal vaccination at least 10 days before arrival, with the certificate ready to show.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Malaysia.
  • Yellow fever vaccination is only needed if you are arriving from, or transiting, a risk country.
  • Women of all ages may travel for Umrah without a mahram.

One-way fares start from about US$266 on AirAsia X, and from about US$540 on full-service carriers (Malaysia Airlines, Saudia); round trips start from about US$600. All fares checked 19 Nov 2026, prices change daily. From Penang, Kota Kinabalu or Kuching, connect through Kuala Lumpur. Jeddah is 5 hours behind Kuala Lumpur. Book the Umrah permit in the Nusuk app before you fly. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and our Madinah hotels guide helps you choose where to stay near the Prophet's Mosque.

What it costs: Roughly, in ringgit: the tourist eVisa is about RM620 (SAR 535). Flights are the biggest variable, then hotels near the Haram. See our general Umrah cost guide and the Makkah hotels guide before you book.

Umrah · Egypt GuideUmrah from Egypt — Visa & Flights Guide

Egypt sends one of the largest Umrah contingents in the world, and Cairo to Jeddah is one of the shortest flights to the Haramain anywhere — a little over two hours in the air. The visa, though, is where Egyptian pilgrims must be careful. Egypt is not among the nationalities eligible for the Saudi tourist eVisa, and there is no visa on arrival on an ordinary Egyptian passport. For almost every Egyptian pilgrim the visa is a dedicated Umrah visa, arranged through the Nusuk platform or a licensed Egyptian company, which also registers your programme on the Egyptian Umrah portal and issues the Egyptian Umrah barcode. This guide covers the visa routes that genuinely exist in the 1448 AH season, the one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa introduced in July 2026, the documents and vaccinations you need, and Cairo–Jeddah flights and fares. Egyptian pilgrims travel under the same broad system as readers of our other non-eVisa country guides — compare Umrah from Nigeria, Umrah from Kenya and Umrah from Indonesia, and our Asian guides to Umrah from Pakistan, Umrah from India and Umrah from Bangladesh.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Egyptians need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Egyptian passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa before travelling. When Saudi Arabia expanded its tourist eVisa list on 5 November 2026, the list grew to 72 eligible nationalities — and Egypt is not among them (VisaEntryRules; House of Saud; Travelobiz). Some older pages still quote a figure of 66 eligible nationalities; that number is out of date, but either way Egypt is not on the list, and there is no visa on arrival for Egyptians travelling on an ordinary passport alone. Anyone who offers you a tourist eVisa on an Egyptian passport alone, without the exception in Route 1 below, is mistaken. Note also that the Egypt–Saudi reciprocal short-stay visa exemption signed on 19 March 2026 covers holders of diplomatic, special and service passports only — it does not apply to ordinary Egyptian passports (Saudi Arabia Immigration).

Route 1: the tourist eVisa exception (only if you qualify): An Egyptian passport holder can still apply for the Saudi tourist eVisa if you hold a valid, previously used US, UK or Schengen visa, or you are a permanent resident of the EU, the UK, the US or a GCC state (VisaEntryRules; Saudi Arabia Immigration). Umrah may be performed on the tourist eVisa outside the Hajj season, with an Umrah permit booked in the Nusuk app, and our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out the wider fee picture.

Route 2: the dedicated Umrah visa (the route almost every Egyptian uses): The standard route is a dedicated Umrah visa arranged through the Nusuk platform or a licensed Egyptian Umrah company. Since August 2025, pilgrims can apply directly on Nusuk and book their accommodation, transport and tours on the platform itself. If you book through a company, the licensed company registers your programme on the Egyptian Umrah portal and issues the Egyptian Umrah barcode that Egyptian pilgrims need before departure (WowTrek). Note also that seasonal programme payments in Egypt are made in Egyptian pounds, not in dollars or riyals (WowTrek). Whichever route you use, you still book your Umrah permit and your Rawdah permit yourself in the Nusuk app — our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup step by step.

The one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa (since July 2026): Since July 2026 the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah has issued a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa: it is valid for 365 days from the date of issue, with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days shared across all your trips in that year. You must obtain an Umrah permit through Nusuk before each arrival, and the visa does not activate during the Hajj season — from 1 Dhu al-Qi'dah to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah (VisaEntryRules; WowTrek). The 90 days are a yearly total — they do not reset on each entry.

Single-entry rules and the 1448 AH season:

  • Since February 2025, Egypt has been one of fourteen nationalities limited to single-entry visit visas — but that restriction does not affect Umrah or Hajj visas, so it does not limit your Umrah options (VisaEntryRules).
  • The last day for Umrah visa issuance in the 1448 AH season is 9 March 2027.
  • The last day to enter Saudi Arabia on an Umrah visa is 23 March 2027.
  • Every Umrah visitor must depart by 7 April 2027, before the Hajj season closes the Haram to Umrah pilgrims.

Documents and vaccinations checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months beyond your arrival date.
  • Meningococcal ACWY vaccination — mandatory for every pilgrim, with the certificate issued at least 10 days before arrival. Carry the certificate in your hand luggage.
  • Polio vaccination is not compulsory for travellers from Egypt — Saudi Arabia only recommends it, so it is a sensible precaution rather than an entry requirement.
  • Yellow fever vaccination is required only if you are arriving from, or transiting, a yellow-fever risk country (WowTrek; Umrah Packages Deals).
  • Your verified hotel and transport bookings, arranged through Nusuk or your licensed company, plus a confirmed return ticket.
  • Women of all ages may perform Umrah without a mahram (Umrah Packages Deals).

Flights from Cairo to Jeddah: Jeddah (King Abdulaziz International, JED) is the arrival airport for Makkah: direct flights from Cairo (CAI) take about 2 hours 10 minutes to 2 hours 20 minutes. Eight airlines fly the route — EgyptAir, Saudia, flynas, flyadeal, Air Cairo, Nile Air, Air Arabia Egypt and Nesma Airlines — with Saudia operating about 61 flights a week and EgyptAir about 54 a week (Priceline schedule data). Fares checked on 18 November 2026: a round trip starts from about US$190 (Flighko); one-way fares start from about US$104 (Expedia) and about US$127 (Priceline), with a typical one-way range of US$75–305 (Expedia). All fares checked 18 Nov 2026, prices change daily. If you enter Ihram for the flight, the Miqat is crossed before landing — the crew normally announce it — and our Miqat guide explains the boundaries. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your programme splits the stay between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi.

Preparing for the journey itself: With the visa and flights settled, the rest is preparation. Pack with our Umrah packing list, learn the supplications from Umrah Duas and Tawaf Duas before you fly, and choose your dates with the best time to perform Umrah guide, which compares weather, crowds and cost across the year. If you hope to travel in the blessed month, our Umrah in Ramadan 2027 guide sets out the expected dates and booking deadlines.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can Egyptians get a Saudi tourist eVisa or visa on arrival? Not on an Egyptian passport alone — Egypt is not among the 72 eligible nationalities after the 5 November 2026 expansion, and there is no visa on arrival. The only eVisa exception is for holders of a used US, UK or Schengen visa, or permanent residents of the EU, UK, US or a GCC state.
  • How do most Egyptians get their Umrah visa? Through a dedicated Umrah visa arranged on the Nusuk platform or by a licensed Egyptian company, which registers the programme on the Egyptian Umrah portal and issues the Egyptian Umrah barcode. Seasonal programme payments are made in Egyptian pounds.
  • Which vaccinations do I need from Egypt? Meningococcal ACWY is mandatory, with the certificate issued at least 10 days before arrival. Polio vaccination is recommended but not compulsory for travellers from Egypt, and yellow fever applies only if you arrive from or transit a yellow-fever risk country.
  • When does the Umrah season end in 1448 AH? Visa issuance ends 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and all Umrah visitors must depart by 7 April 2027.

Umrah · Turkey GuideUmrah from Turkey — Visa & Flights Guide

Of all the country guides on this site, Turkey's is the most straightforward — because Turkey is on Saudi Arabia's tourist eVisa list. After the expansion of 5 November 2026, the list covers 72 countries, with Turkey listed in the Asia group (Travelobiz; House of Saud; Wego Blog). That means a Turkish passport holder can apply for a tourist eVisa online in advance, or obtain one on arrival at a Saudi international airport, and perform Umrah on it outside the Hajj season. A dedicated Umrah visa through the Nusuk platform remains the other route, including the one-year multiple-entry visa introduced in July 2026. This guide covers both routes, the documents and vaccinations you need — including the chipped-passport rule that catches some Turkish travellers out — and Istanbul–Jeddah flights and fares. Compare the eVisa route here with our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide, and contrast it with the agent-based routes in Umrah from Egypt, Umrah from Nigeria and Umrah from Indonesia, where no eVisa exists on those passports at all.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Turkish citizens need a visa for Umrah? Yes — but unlike most of our readers, you can get yours online or at the airport. The Saudi tourist eVisa is valid for one year, allows multiple entries, and permits a cumulative stay of up to 90 days. It costs SAR 535, a fee that includes health cover of up to SAR 100,000. Apply in advance at visa.visitsaudi.com; the same visa is also available on arrival at Saudi international airports (VisaEntryRules; House of Saud). The tourist eVisa covers tourism, family visits, events and Umrah — but Hajj is excluded, and no tourist visa can be used for Hajj. Our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out how this fee compares with the other visa types.

Route 1: Umrah on the tourist eVisa: This is the route most Turkish pilgrims now use. Apply at visa.visitsaudi.com before you travel, or take the visa on arrival, then book your Umrah permit through the Nusuk platform — the eVisa alone does not admit you to perform Umrah; the permit is booked separately in the Nusuk app, and Umrah on a tourist visa is performed outside the Hajj season (Wego Blog). You will also book your Rawdah permit in the same app when you visit Madinah — our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup step by step. Because you arrange everything yourself on this route, book your hotels and ground transport before you fly, and keep the confirmations with your passport. Travellers who prefer everything arranged for them can still book a complete programme through a Turkish Umrah company, which handles the visa, hotels and transfers together — the choice is genuinely yours, in a way it is not for pilgrims from non-eVisa countries.

Route 2: the dedicated Umrah visa through Nusuk: The alternative is a dedicated Umrah visa, and since July 2026 its headline form is the one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa issued via Nusuk: valid for 365 days from issue, with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days across the year, an Umrah permit required before each arrival, and the visa inactive during the Hajj season — from 1 Dhu al-Qi'dah to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah (VisaEntryRules). Pilgrims have been able to apply directly on the Nusuk Umrah service since 20 August 2025. One rule to plan around: since 10 June 2025, an Umrah visa is issued only once your accommodation and transport booking is documented and approved (VisaEntryRules; Şahinoğlu Turizm) — so fix your hotels and transfers first, then apply, rather than the other way round.

The 1448 AH season dates:

  • The last day for Umrah visa issuance in the 1448 AH season is 9 March 2027.
  • The last day to enter Saudi Arabia on an Umrah visa is 23 March 2027.
  • Every Umrah visitor must depart by 7 April 2027.
  • Neither the tourist eVisa nor the Umrah visa can be used for Umrah during the Hajj season itself, when the Haram is reserved for Hajj pilgrims.

Documents and vaccinations checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months beyond your arrival date.
  • The new chipped Turkish passport is mandatory — Saudi visas cannot be issued on old-style, non-chipped Turkish passports, so check your passport type before you book anything (Şahinoğlu Turizm).
  • Meningococcal ACWY vaccination, taken at least 10 days before arrival — the Saudi rule for all pilgrims, whichever visa you travel on. Carry the certificate in your hand luggage.
  • Your hotel and transport bookings — documented and approved before an Umrah visa is issued, and worth carrying in print on the eVisa route too.
  • A confirmed return ticket — airlines and immigration officers may ask to see it, whichever route you travel on.
  • Women of all ages may perform Umrah without a mahram.

Flights from Istanbul to Jeddah: Jeddah (King Abdulaziz International, JED) is the arrival airport for Makkah, and Istanbul (IST) is one of the best-connected departure points in this entire series of guides: about 12 nonstop flights a day link the two cities, with a direct flying time of about 3 hours 45 minutes to 3 hours 48 minutes. The nonstop carriers are Turkish Airlines, Saudia, flyadeal and flynas. Fares checked in November 2026 on KAYAK: a round trip starts from about US$234, with a typical round-trip range of US$249–327 and the cheapest nonstop at about US$260; one-way fares start from about US$129 (KAYAK) and about ₹11,313 on flynas (HappyFares, fares seen in the 30 days to 18 November 2026). All fares checked 18 Nov 2026, prices change daily. If you enter Ihram for the flight, the Miqat is crossed before landing — the crew normally announce it — and our Miqat guide explains the boundaries. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options, and if your trip splits the stay between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi.

Preparing for the journey itself: With the visa and flights settled, the rest is preparation. Pack with our Umrah packing list, learn the supplications from Umrah Duas and Tawaf Duas before you fly, and choose your dates with the best time to perform Umrah guide, which compares weather, crowds and cost across the year. Travelling from further east in Asia? Our guides to Umrah from Pakistan and Umrah from India show how different the visa picture looks there. And if you hope to travel in the blessed month, our Umrah in Ramadan 2027 guide sets out the expected dates and booking deadlines.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can Turkish citizens get a Saudi eVisa or visa on arrival? Yes. Turkey is among the 72 countries on the tourist eVisa list after the 5 November 2026 expansion. The eVisa is valid for one year, allows multiple entries and up to 90 days in total, costs SAR 535 including health cover up to SAR 100,000, and can be applied for at visa.visitsaudi.com or obtained on arrival at Saudi international airports.
  • Can I perform Umrah on the tourist eVisa? Yes, outside the Hajj season — but you must also book an Umrah permit through the Nusuk platform. The tourist eVisa never covers Hajj.
  • What passport do I need? A Turkish passport valid for at least six months beyond your arrival — and it must be the new chipped passport. Visas cannot be issued on old-style Turkish passports.
  • When does the Umrah season end in 1448 AH? Visa issuance ends 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and all Umrah visitors must depart by 7 April 2027.

Umrah · Kenya GuideUmrah from Kenya — Visa & Flights Guide
Travel warning — updated 18 November 2026, read this first: As of 18 November 2026, Saudi Arabia has suspended all visa issuance for travellers arriving from Kenya. The suspension was announced on 30 October 2026 in response to the Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo strain), after Kenya confirmed its first imported case on 6 October 2026. It covers Umrah, business, family visit and transit visas, and it also bars entry to anyone who was physically in Kenya within 21 days before arrival — even if they travel via a third country. There is no stated end date as of early November 2026: Kenya's government was pushing for the suspension to be lifted on 3 November 2026, and Africa CDC backed a review of the decision. Until it is lifted: do not pay for non-refundable bookings, and confirm the current status with a licensed agent and the Saudi embassy before paying anything at all.

Because of that warning, this guide is written in two parts. Everything below describes the normal route for Umrah from Kenya — the visa options, documents, vaccinations and flights that apply when travel is open — so that you can prepare calmly and book quickly once the suspension ends. Do not treat any of it as a reason to pay a deposit today. When the route reopens, Kenyan pilgrims will travel the same way our readers from other non-eVisa countries do: compare this guide with Umrah from Nigeria and Umrah from Pakistan to see how the agent-based system works across countries.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Kenyans need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Kenyan passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa before travelling, and Kenya is not on Saudi Arabia's tourist eVisa list — that position was checked on 3 October 2026 against official sources (Darbiya). There is no visa-free entry and no visa on arrival on a Kenyan passport alone. Anyone who offers you a tourist eVisa on a Kenyan passport alone, without one of the exceptions below, is mistaken.

The normal route: Umrah visa through a licensed agent via Nusuk: When issuance is open, the standard route is a dedicated Umrah visa arranged by a licensed travel agent. The agent files your application through the Nusuk system together with verified hotel and ground transport bookings — since 2025 an Umrah visa cannot be issued without those bookings attached, which is why genuine agents sell packages rather than bare visas. Once you hold the visa, you still book your Umrah permit and your Rawdah permit yourself in the Nusuk app; our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup step by step.

The eVisa exception (only if you qualify): A Kenyan passport holder can still reach the Saudi tourist eVisa through an exception: if you hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visa that you have already used to enter that country or region, you hold permanent residence in the US, UK or an EU country, or you are a GCC resident, you may apply for the visitor eVisa regardless of nationality — and Umrah may be performed on it outside the Hajj season, with a Nusuk permit. Our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide explains the eVisa steps in detail. Note that while the Kenya suspension is in force, it covers travellers arriving from Kenya however they are documented — the exception does not override it.

The stopover option: If you are flying with Saudia or flynas and transiting through Saudi Arabia, the free 96-hour stopover visa lets you perform Umrah within the stopover window, provided you book your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app. It suits a short visit bolted onto another journey; it is not a substitute for a full Umrah trip, and it is equally unavailable while arrivals from Kenya are suspended.

Key dates for the 1448 AH Umrah season:

  • The last day for Umrah visa issuance is 9 March 2027.
  • The last day to enter Saudi Arabia on an Umrah visa is 23 March 2027.
  • Every Umrah visitor must depart by 7 April 2027.
  • As across the site's other guides, a standard Umrah visa must be used for entry within 30 days of issuance, and the maximum stay after entry is 90 days — so fix your flight dates first, then apply. See our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide for the fee picture.
  • Umrah visas are not issued, and Umrah is not performed, during the Hajj season itself.

Women travelling without a mahram: Women of all ages may now perform Umrah without a mahram, so Kenyan women can travel alone or in a group of women on the normal route. Our guide for women travelling alone covers the current rules and practical safety advice.

Documents checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months beyond your arrival date.
  • Recent passport-size photographs, as your agent specifies.
  • Confirmed return ticket.
  • Proof of accommodation — your verified Nusuk hotel booking, arranged by your agent as part of the package.
  • Some agents also ask for a bank statement — around USD 2,500, per TurKenya (turkenya.com). Treat this as an agent-level requirement rather than a published Saudi rule, and ask your own agent exactly what they need before you pay.

Vaccinations — two certificates matter from Kenya:

  • Meningococcal ACWY — quadrivalent vaccination is mandatory for every Umrah pilgrim, and it must be taken at least 10 days before arrival. Carry the certificate in your hand luggage.
  • Yellow fever — Saudi Arabia lists Kenya as a yellow-fever risk country, so a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate is required. Expect to present it on arrival; do not pack it in a checked bag.

Flights from Nairobi to Jeddah: Jeddah (King Abdulaziz International, JED) is the arrival airport for Makkah. Saudia and Kenya Airways both fly direct from Nairobi (NBO) to Jeddah, a flight of about 3 hours 50 minutes. Fares checked in November 2026 on Airpaz (airpaz.com): Saudia one-way from about US$241–333, and Kenya Airways one-way from about US$555. Average return fares are reported at KSh 56,000–92,000 (flightticketagent.com, January 2026), and connecting budget options on carriers such as Air Arabia and flyadeal start from about KSh 48,000 return. Fares move sharply with the pilgrimage calendar, so treat these as planning figures and check live prices for your dates once travel reopens. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the taxi, bus and train options; for where to stay, see Makkah hotels near the Haram and Madinah hotels near Masjid Nabawi; and pack with our Umrah packing list so nothing essential is left behind.

Best time to go from Kenya: The most comfortable months are October to March, when Makkah and Madinah are at their coolest and fares outside the school holidays are at their kindest. Ramadan is peak season — the most rewarding and the most crowded and expensive time of year; our Umrah in Ramadan 2027 guide gives the expected dates and deadlines, and the best time to perform Umrah guide compares weather, crowds and cost across the whole year. All of this planning, of course, only becomes a booking once the suspension is lifted — prepare now, pay later.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can Kenyans do Umrah right now? No. As of 18 November 2026, Saudi Arabia has suspended all visa issuance for travellers arriving from Kenya — Umrah, business, family visit and transit visas — because of the Ebola (Bundibugyo strain) outbreak, and anyone who was in Kenya within 21 days before arrival is also barred, even via a third country. There is no stated end date. Do not pay for non-refundable bookings until the suspension is lifted, and confirm the current position with a licensed agent and the Saudi embassy before paying anything.
  • Do Kenyans need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Kenya is not on the Saudi tourist eVisa list, so the normal route is a dedicated Umrah visa through a licensed agent via the Nusuk system, with verified hotel and transport bookings. The only eVisa exception is for holders of a used US, UK or Schengen visa, permanent residents of the US, UK or EU, and GCC residents.
  • Which vaccines are needed from Kenya? Meningococcal ACWY is mandatory for every pilgrim, taken at least 10 days before arrival, and a yellow fever certificate is required because Saudi Arabia lists Kenya as a yellow-fever risk country. Carry both certificates in your hand luggage.

Umrah · Indonesia GuideUmrah from Indonesia — Visa & Flights Guide

Indonesia has the world's largest Muslim population and is Saudi Arabia's biggest Umrah market — well over a million Indonesian pilgrims travel in a normal year. If you are planning Umrah from Indonesia, the visa is the first thing to get right: Indonesia is not among the nationalities eligible for the Saudi tourist eVisa, and there is no visa on arrival on an Indonesian passport. For most Indonesians the visa comes through a licensed PPIU agent registered with Kemenag, although since August 2025 you can also apply directly on the Nusuk Umrah platform. This guide covers both routes, the one-year multiple-entry visa introduced in July 2026, the documents and vaccinations you need, and flights and package prices from Jakarta. Indonesian pilgrims travel under the same broad system as our readers elsewhere in Asia — compare Umrah from Pakistan, Umrah from Bangladesh and Umrah from India, and our original Umrah from Nigeria guide, to see how the routes differ by country.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Indonesians need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Indonesian passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa before travelling. Indonesia is not on the tourist eVisa list and there is no visa on arrival for Indonesian citizens travelling on an ordinary Indonesian passport alone (VisaEntryRules; UmrahDIY; Wego's 2026 Umrah visa guide). Anyone who offers you a tourist eVisa on an Indonesian passport alone, without the exception in Route 1 below, is mistaken.

Route 1: the tourist eVisa exception (only if you qualify): An Indonesian passport holder can still apply for the Saudi tourist eVisa if you hold a valid, previously used US, UK or Schengen visa, or you are a legal resident of a GCC country, the EU, the UK or the US. The eVisa costs about SAR 535 and is processed online in minutes to 24 hours (UmrahDIY). Umrah may be performed on it outside the Hajj season, with an Umrah permit booked in the Nusuk app. Our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide walks through the eVisa steps, and our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide sets out the wider fee picture.

Route 2: the Umrah visa through a PPIU agent (the route most Indonesians use): The standard route is a dedicated Umrah visa arranged by a PPIU — a licensed Umrah travel agent (Penyelenggara Perjalanan Ibadah Umrah) registered with Kemenag, Indonesia's Ministry of Religious Affairs. Only PPIU agents can legally process Umrah visas for Indonesians, so verify your agent's Kemenag registration before paying anything — unregistered sellers are the single biggest source of Umrah fraud in Indonesia. The agent files your application together with verified hotel and transport bookings, because an Umrah visa is no longer issued without them.

Applying directly on Nusuk: Since August 2025, pilgrims can also apply directly on the Nusuk Umrah platform (umrah.nusuk.sa), booking the visa together with verified hotel and transport, instead of going through an agent. Whichever route you use, you still book your Umrah permit and your Rawdah permit yourself in the Nusuk app — our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup step by step.

The one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa (since July 2026): Since July 2026 the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah has issued a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa: it is valid for 365 days from the date of issue, with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days shared across all your trips in that year. You must obtain an Umrah permit in the Nusuk app before each arrival, and the visa is inactive during the Hajj season — from 1 Dhu al-Qi'dah to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah. For frequent travellers it removes the need to apply again for every trip, but the 90 days do not reset on each entry.

Single-entry rules and the 1448 AH season:

  • A single-entry Umrah visa must now be used within 30 days of issuance — reduced from 90 days — and then allows a stay of up to 90 days (Wego, 2026). Fix your flight dates first, then apply.
  • The 1448 AH season opened on 31 May 2026, with entry to Makkah from 1 June 2026.
  • The last day for Umrah visa issuance is 9 March 2027 (Wego), and as across this site's guides every Umrah visitor must depart before the Hajj season closes the Haram to Umrah pilgrims.
  • One clarification that causes real confusion: since February 2025 Indonesia has been one of 14 nationalities limited to single-entry visit visas — but Umrah and Hajj visas were not part of that restriction, so it does not limit your Umrah options.

Documents and vaccinations checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months beyond your arrival date.
  • Meningococcal ACWY vaccination, taken at least 10 days before arrival — mandatory for every pilgrim, without exception. Carry the certificate in your hand luggage.
  • Polio vaccination where required under the current Saudi health rules — your PPIU agent will confirm whether it applies to your departure.
  • Your verified hotel and transport bookings, arranged by your PPIU agent or booked by you on the direct Nusuk route, plus a confirmed return ticket.

Flights from Jakarta to Jeddah: Jeddah (King Abdulaziz International, JED) is the usual arrival airport for Makkah. Garuda Indonesia and Saudia fly direct from Jakarta (CGK) to Jeddah, a flight of about 9 hours 55 minutes. Fares checked in November 2026 on Airpaz (airpaz.com): Garuda one-way from about US$499 and Saudia one-way from about US$521; Trip.com lists Garuda Jakarta–Jeddah from Rp 9,625,400 one-way. One-stop options via Emirates (Dubai), Qatar Airways (Doha) and Turkish Airlines (Istanbul) compete on price outside peak weeks. On arrival, our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the onward taxi, bus and train options; if your package splits the stay between the two holy cities, the Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares the Haramain train, bus and taxi; and for where to stay, see Makkah hotels near the Haram and Madinah hotels near Masjid Nabawi.

Packages and paying in instalments: Most Indonesian pilgrims buy a full package from their PPIU agent — flights, visa, hotels, transport and ziyarat in one price. Umrah packages from Jakarta start from about Rp 20 juta per person (yuusr.com, checked 17–18 November 2026), and instalment (cicilan) plans are commonly offered, letting you spread the cost over the months before departure. Whichever package you choose, get the hotel names and their distance from the Haram in writing, and pack with our Umrah packing list. For timing, the best time to perform Umrah guide compares weather, crowds and cost across the year, and our Umrah in Ramadan 2027 guide covers the peak season's dates and deadlines.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Do Indonesians need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Indonesia is not among the nationalities eligible for the Saudi tourist eVisa and there is no visa on arrival on an Indonesian passport. Most Indonesians travel on a dedicated Umrah visa through a PPIU agent licensed by Kemenag, or apply directly on the Nusuk Umrah platform. The only eVisa exception is for holders of a valid, previously used US, UK or Schengen visa, or legal residents of a GCC country, the EU, the UK or the US.
  • Can Indonesians apply on Nusuk directly? Yes. Since August 2025 you can apply on the Nusuk Umrah platform (umrah.nusuk.sa) with verified hotel and transport bookings, without going through an agent. You still need the Nusuk app for your Umrah permit and Rawdah permit once the visa is issued.
  • How long can I stay? On a single-entry Umrah visa, up to 90 days after entry — but you must enter within 30 days of the visa being issued. On the one-year multiple-entry visa introduced in July 2026, you may come and go for 365 days with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days in total, and the visa pauses during the Hajj season.

Umrah · Nigeria GuideUmrah from Nigeria — Visa & Flights Guide

If you are searching for how to perform Umrah from Nigeria, the visa is the first thing to get right. Nigeria is not on Saudi Arabia's tourist eVisa list, and there is no visa on arrival on a Nigerian passport — so almost every Nigerian pilgrim travels on a dedicated Umrah visa arranged through a licensed operator, with the visa linked to verified hotel and transport bookings on the Nusuk system. This guide covers the routes that genuinely exist in the 1448 AH season, the documents you need — including the yellow fever and polio rules that apply specifically to travellers from Nigeria — and flights from Lagos, Abuja and Kano.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Nigerians need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Nigerian passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa before travelling. There is no visa-free entry and no visa on arrival for Nigerian citizens travelling on an ordinary Nigerian passport alone. Anyone who promises you a tourist eVisa on a Nigerian passport alone is mistaken — Nigeria is not among the eligible nationalities for that visa.

Route 1: Umrah visa through a licensed operator via Nusuk Masar (the route almost everyone uses): You book through a licensed Umrah operator in Nigeria. The operator works with a Saudi-approved Umrah services company and files your application on the Ministry's operator platform, Nusuk Masar, together with a booked package. Since 2025, every Umrah visa must be linked to verified Nusuk hotel and ground transport bookings — there is no visa without a package attached, which is why honest operators sell packages rather than bare visas. The same operator-based system applies to our neighbouring guides: see Umrah from India and Umrah from Bangladesh for how the route compares.

Route 2: apply directly on the Nusuk Umrah service: Since August 2025, the Nusuk Umrah service also allows pilgrims to apply for the visa and book accommodation, transport and tours directly on the Nusuk platform, rather than only through an agent. Whichever route you use, you still book your Umrah permit and your Rawdah permit yourself in the Nusuk app — our Nusuk app guide walks through the setup step by step.

Key rules for the 1448 AH Umrah season:

  • Under rules in force since early November 2025, a standard Umrah visa must be used for entry within 30 days of issuance, down from 90 days. If you have not entered Saudi Arabia by then, the visa lapses — so fix your flight dates first, then apply.
  • Once you enter, the maximum stay is 90 days.
  • The season's closing dates are fixed: the last day for visa issuance is 9 March 2027, the last day to enter Saudi Arabia is 23 March 2027, and every Umrah visitor must depart by 7 April 2027.
  • Umrah visas are not issued, and Umrah is not performed, during the Hajj season itself.

The one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa (announced 20 July 2026): On 20 July 2026 the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah announced a multiple-entry Umrah visa valid for 365 days from issuance, reported by the Saudi Press Agency and The National. It allows repeat entries with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days across the whole year — the 90 days are shared between trips, not reset on each entry. Every arrival still needs its own Nusuk-approved service package and a fresh Umrah permit booked in the Nusuk app before you travel, and the visa is not active during the Hajj season. The announcement did not settle every detail of which nationalities can obtain it and through which channel, so confirm with your operator before planning a year of trips around it. For the wider fee picture, see our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide.

Route 3: the tourist eVisa exception (only if you qualify): A Nigerian passport holder can still reach the Saudi tourist eVisa through an exception: if you hold a valid UK, US or Schengen visa that you have already used to enter that country or region, or you are a permanent resident of the UK, US or an EU country, or a resident of a GCC country, you may apply for the visitor eVisa regardless of nationality — and Umrah may be performed on it outside the Hajj season, with a Nusuk permit. Our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide explains the eVisa steps in detail.

Documents checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months beyond your arrival date.
  • Recent passport photograph with a white background.
  • Meningococcal ACWY certificate — quadrivalent vaccination is required for all Hajj and Umrah pilgrims, taken at least 10 days before arrival.
  • Yellow fever certificate — Nigeria is a yellow-fever-endemic country, so carry a valid International Certificate of Vaccination showing yellow fever vaccination; expect to present it on arrival, so keep it in your hand luggage, not your checked bag.
  • Polio: Saudi health rules also list arrivals from Nigeria for polio vaccination proof (OPV/IPV), so carry your polio vaccination record as well and check the current requirement with your operator before you fly.
  • Your Nusuk-linked hotel and transport bookings, arranged by your operator (or booked by you on the direct Nusuk route), plus a confirmed return ticket.

Visas have reopened — and NAHCON is your regulator: Nigerian Umrah visas reopened in August 2026 after about two years of restrictions, so demand through licensed operators is high and rules are still settling. The National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON) is the Nigerian regulator for Hajj and Umrah travel: check NAHCON's announcements for last-minute changes before you pay a balance or fix non-refundable dates, and use only operators you can verify.

Flights from Nigeria to Jeddah and Madinah: Jeddah (King Abdulaziz International) is the usual arrival airport for Makkah; Madinah is the other gateway. Most Lagos and Abuja itineraries connect once — through Addis Ababa, Cairo, Istanbul or Doha — while Kano has seasonal direct services in peak periods. Airlines selling these routes include Saudia, Ethiopian Airlines, Turkish Airlines, EgyptAir and Qatar Airways. Return fare ranges reported by the House of Saud guide for Nigerian travellers (checked November 2026) are:

For where to stay, see Makkah hotels near the Haram and Madinah hotels near Masjid Nabawi. If you fly into Jeddah in Ihram, remember the Miqat is crossed before landing — the crew normally announce it — and pack with our Umrah packing list. Women travelling without a mahram should also read our guide for women travelling alone, and anyone choosing dates should check the best time to perform Umrah guide for weather and crowd trade-offs.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can Nigerians get a Saudi tourist eVisa or visa on arrival? Not on a Nigerian passport alone — Nigeria is not on the tourist eVisa list and there is no visa on arrival. The exception is for holders of a used UK, US or Schengen visa, permanent residents of the UK, US or EU, and GCC residents.
  • How long can I stay on an Umrah visa? Up to 90 days after entry on the standard visa, and you must enter within 30 days of the visa being issued. On the one-year multiple-entry visa announced in July 2026, the 90 days are a cumulative total shared across all trips in the year.
  • Which vaccinations do I need from Nigeria? Meningococcal ACWY for every pilgrim, a yellow fever certificate because Nigeria is endemic, and polio vaccination proof, which Saudi rules list for arrivals from Nigeria. Confirm the current list with your operator and NAHCON before travelling.
  • When does the Umrah season end in 1448 AH? Visa issuance ends 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and all Umrah visitors must depart by 7 April 2027.
