Umrah · Ramadan 2027 GuideUmrah in Ramadan 2027 — Dates, Costs & Tips

Planning Umrah in Ramadan 2027 means planning around two calendars at once: Ramadan 1448 AH itself, and the end of the Umrah season, which closes in the middle of it. This guide is the 2027-specific companion to our general Umrah in Ramadan article — here you will find the expected dates table, the visa deadline that falls on Eid day itself, what peak-season costs and crowds really look like, and how to pace fasting, Taraweeh and the last ten nights. For the wider year-round picture, see the best time to perform Umrah guide.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Umrah in Ramadan is equivalent to Hajj" — and in one narration, "equivalent to Hajj with me" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1782; Sahih Muslim 1256). The scholars explain that it equals Hajj in reward; it does not replace the obligatory Hajj for someone who later becomes able to perform it — see our Hajj 2027 guide for that journey.

Ramadan 2027 dates — all provisional: On Saudi Arabia's Umm al-Qura calendar, Ramadan 1448 AH is expected to run for 29 days, from Monday 8 February 2027 to Monday 8 March 2027, with Eid al-Fitr on Tuesday 9 March 2027. These are calculated dates only: the religious start and end of Ramadan are confirmed by the official moon sighting on the evening of 29 Sha'ban, and can shift by a day. Countries that follow local sighting — including Pakistan and India, which may begin on 8 or 9 February — can differ from Saudi Arabia by a day at either end, so Eid there may fall anywhere from 9 to 11 March. Build a day of flexibility into flights and hotel dates wherever you can.

Event (1448 AH)Expected date (provisional)
First Taraweeh (night before 1 Ramadan)Sunday evening, 7 February 2027
1 Ramadan — first fastMonday, 8 February 2027
Last ten nights begin (night of 21 Ramadan)Evening of Friday, 27 February 2027
Odd nights to seek Laylat al-QadrNights of 27 Feb, 1, 3, 5 and 7 March 2027
29 Ramadan — last fastMonday, 8 March 2027
Eid al-Fitr (1 Shawwal)Tuesday, 9 March 2027
Last day of Umrah visa issuance (1448 season)9 March 2027
Last day to enter Saudi Arabia on an Umrah visa23 March 2027

The deadline warning — read this first: The Umrah season's last visa issuance date is 9 March 2027 — Eid al-Fitr day itself. In practice that means a Ramadan Umrah cannot be a last-minute decision: your visa must be applied for well before Ramadan ends, and because a standard Umrah visa must be used for entry within 30 days of issuance, the working window is tight. Apply and book early — ideally months ahead — and remember the final backstop: the last permitted entry is 23 March 2027, and all Umrah visitors must depart by 7 April 2027. Check the fee and processing picture in our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide before you commit.

Costs in Ramadan 2027 — the peak of the year: Ramadan is the most expensive Umrah season, and the last ten nights are the most expensive days within it. Flights into Jeddah and Madinah and rooms near the Haram reach their highest prices of the year, and the closest hotels sell out first. There is no honest fixed price for a Ramadan 2027 package — it depends on your departure country, hotel distance and how early you book — so use our Umrah cost breakdown for the baseline budget, then expect Ramadan, and especially the last ten nights, to sit well above it. The two levers that actually move the price are booking 5–6 months ahead and choosing the first half of Ramadan over the last ten nights if your intention allows. Compare areas before paying with our Makkah hotels and Madinah hotels guides.

Crowds, Taraweeh and Qiyam: Expect the fullest Haram of the year. The Grand Mosque fills to the streets for Maghrib, Isha and Taraweeh, so arrive around 90 minutes early to pray inside rather than in the outer courtyards. Flip your day around: sleep after Fajr and again after Dhuhr, and give the nights to Taraweeh, Qiyam, Qur'an and du'a — our Umrah duas collection will help you prepare what to recite. You still need one Nusuk Umrah permit for each performance of Umrah, booked in the app as soon as your dates are fixed; Ramadan slots go fastest of all — the Nusuk app guide shows the booking steps. First-timers should read the first-timers' guide alongside this one, and pack for long nights and warm days with the packing list.

The last ten nights and Laylat al-Qadr: The last ten nights run from the evening of 27 February to 8 March 2027 (provisional). In them falls Laylat al-Qadr, the night better than a thousand months (Quran 97:3), sought on the odd nights — the 21st, 23rd, 25th, 27th and 29th. Many pilgrims aim specifically for these nights in Makkah or Madinah, which is why they are the most crowded and costly of the season. Increase du'a and night prayer, rest honestly in the day, and do not try to perform Umrah itself on the most packed nights if a quieter night in the same stay is possible.

Fasting while travelling: Allah says: "…whoever among you is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days [must be made up]" (Quran 2:185) — the concession to postpone fasts while travelling exists, and travellers differ in what they choose: many pilgrims fast in the holy cities and find it manageable with the flipped Ramadan schedule, while others use the concession on the travel days themselves and make the fasts up later. Decide with a scholar you trust before you go, not on the plane. Either way, eat a real Suhoor, break the fast simply — dates and Zamzam are distributed in the Haram — and hydrate steadily between Iftar and Suhoor.

Rawdah in Ramadan: A visit to the Rawdah in Madinah during Ramadan is booked exactly as at any other time — only through a Rawdah permit on the Nusuk app — but demand is at its yearly peak and slots disappear quickly. Book the moment your window opens, be flexible about which day of your Madinah stay you take, and keep checking the app for released slots.

Frequently asked questions:

  • When is Ramadan 2027? Expected Monday 8 February to Monday 8 March 2027 (29 days, Umm al-Qura calendar), with Eid al-Fitr on Tuesday 9 March 2027. All dates are provisional until confirmed by moon sighting, and Pakistan and India may differ by a day.
  • Can I still get an Umrah visa during Ramadan 2027? Yes, but not at the last minute: visa issuance for the 1448 season ends on 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and a visa must be entered on within 30 days of issue. Apply well before Ramadan ends — in practice, book the whole trip months ahead.
  • Which part of Ramadan 2027 is busiest? The last ten nights, from about 27 February to 8 March, when pilgrims gather for Qiyam and Laylat al-Qadr. They are also the most expensive nights of the year for flights and hotels near the Haram.
  • Does Umrah in Ramadan replace Hajj? No. It equals Hajj in reward (Sahih al-Bukhari 1782; Sahih Muslim 1256), but the obligation of Hajj remains for whoever becomes able to perform it.

Umrah · Pakistan GuideUmrah from Pakistan — Visa & Flights Guide

Pakistan sends more Umrah pilgrims than almost any other country, yet the Pakistani route has one rule that catches people out: you cannot apply for an Umrah visa yourself. The visa is issued only as part of a package, through a licensed Pakistani operator working on the Saudi Maqam system, with your hotels and transport booked first. This guide explains the visa routes that genuinely exist for Pakistani passport holders, the 1448 AH season dates, direct flights from Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad, and what a 10-day trip really costs in rupees.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Pakistanis need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Pakistani passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa before travelling. There is no visa-on-arrival for Pakistani citizens, and there is no way to file an Umrah visa application yourself on Nusuk or any other website. Anyone who offers you a "direct" or "visa-only" Umrah visa outside the operator system is not following the rules — see the scam warning below.

Route 1: Umrah visa through a licensed operator (the route almost everyone uses): You book through an Umrah tour operator in Pakistan that is attested by the Ministry of Religious Affairs (MoRA) and works with a Saudi-approved service company. The operator files your visa electronically through the Saudi Maqam platform, with the e-visa issued through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs system behind it — there is no sticker in your passport and no embassy visit for a standard Umrah visa. Since 10 June 2025, a confirmed hotel booking made through Nusuk Masar, with a Booking Reference Number (BRN), plus confirmed ground transport, must exist before the visa can be issued. That is why honest operators sell packages, not bare visas. Our Umrah from Pakistan — Complete Guide covers the operator system in more depth.

Key rules for the 1448 AH Umrah season:

  • The 1448 season opened with visa issuance from 31 May 2026 and entry from 1 June 2026.
  • The visa is valid for 30 days from the date it is issued. You must enter Saudi Arabia within that window; once you enter, you can stay up to 90 days. Apply only when your flight dates are fixed.
  • The 1448 season runs to 7 April 2027. Visa issuance ends on 9 March 2027 and the last entry date is 23 March 2027, and every Umrah visitor must leave by 7 April 2027.
  • Since July 2026 there is also a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa, valid for 365 days with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days. Each entry needs its own service package booked through an approved Nusuk provider, plus an Umrah permit in the Nusuk app. It is not valid during the Hajj season.
  • Umrah visas are not issued in the weeks around Hajj.

Route 2: Saudi tourist eVisa (only if you qualify): Pakistan is not on Saudi Arabia's tourist eVisa nationality list, so an ordinary Pakistani passport alone does not qualify. You can apply for the tourist eVisa on visa.visitsaudi.com only if one of these applies:

  • You hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visit visa that you have already used to enter that country.
  • You are a permanent resident of the US, the UK or an EU country.
  • You are a resident of a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) country.

The tourist eVisa costs about SAR 535 including insurance (around PKR 39,600) and permits Umrah, but not Hajj. Our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide walks through the eVisa steps, and our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide compares both routes side by side.

Route 3: the 96-hour stopover visa (free): If you fly Saudia or flynas and transit through Saudi Arabia, you can take the free 96-hour stopover visa and perform Umrah within that window, with an Umrah permit booked in the Nusuk app. It suits a short stop on the way somewhere else — not a full, unhurried Umrah trip.

Biometrics — the Saudi Visa Bio app: Your operator may ask you to enrol your fingerprints and photo in the official Saudi Visa Bio app. Do it as soon as you are asked: the visa file cannot move forward until the biometrics are done, and leaving it to the last week is one of the most common causes of delayed departures from Pakistan.

Documents checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months from your date of entry, with blank pages.
  • Recent passport-size photograph.
  • Polio (OPV) vaccination — required for Pakistani travellers. Keep the record, and get your NADRA digital vaccination certificate through the NIMS portal (PKR 100); carry a printout as well.
  • Meningococcal ACWY certificate: Saudi Arabia suspended the mandatory requirement in February 2025, but many operators still list it — check the current rule with your operator and carry the certificate if you have it.
  • Confirmed Nusuk hotel and transport bookings (with the BRN) made by your operator — mandatory before the visa is issued.
  • Confirmed return ticket.
  • Biometrics completed in the Saudi Visa Bio app, if your operator asks for it.

Flights from Pakistan to Jeddah and Madinah: Direct flights run from Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad to Jeddah (JED) and to Madinah (MED) on PIA, Saudia, flynas, Airblue and SereneAir, with schedules that expand in the peak Umrah months. Karachi to Jeddah is about 4 hours 30 minutes nonstop; Lahore and Islamabad flights run roughly 30 to 60 minutes longer. Flying into Madinah and home from Jeddah (or the reverse) saves one long road transfer — our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide covers the arrival side in detail.

Indicative fares seen in November 2026 checks (named sources):

  • Karachi to Jeddah return: Saudia round trips listed from PKR 92,053, with other airlines' returns from PKR 89,821 (trips.pk).
  • Lowest Saudia one-way fare Karachi to Jeddah tracked at PKR 80,860 on 17 November 2026 (FlightRate.pk).
  • flyadeal one-way Karachi to Jeddah from PKR 64,869 (Bookme.pk).
  • Typical return economy range Karachi to Jeddah: PKR 155,176 to PKR 286,510 for trips of up to 10 days (Mosafir.pk) — the spread shows how much the fare moves with dates and how early you book.

Fares change daily and climb steeply in Ramadan and school holidays. Lahore and Islamabad departures usually run about PKR 5,000 to 15,000 more than Karachi on the same route. Treat every figure here as indicative and check live fares for your own dates before paying.

What a 10-day Umrah costs from Pakistan (per person, PKR, November 2026 ranges):

Package price ranges advertised in 2026: economy packages run about PKR 245,000–320,000 per person for 7 days, PKR 275,000–360,000 for 10 days and PKR 315,000–415,000 for 15 days (quad sharing, 3-star hotels), with 5-star Haram-side packages starting from about PKR 395,000 for 7 days. In the last ten nights of Ramadan, expect PKR 600,000–800,000 or more. Our Umrah Cost from Pakistan 2026 breakdown checks any quote line by line.

Scam warning — check the licence before you pay: Umrah fraud rises every season, and the pattern is always the same: a very cheap "package", a request for full payment in cash, and then silence. Protect yourself:

  • Book only with an operator on the Ministry of Religious Affairs verified operators list at mora.gov.pk — check the name yourself before paying anything; do not rely on a screenshot the agent sends you.
  • Under the Hajj and Umrah Act 2024 (rules in force since July 2026), only verified operators may sell Umrah packages in Pakistan.
  • Pay through a bank and keep every receipt. A bank trail is your proof if anything goes wrong.
  • Beware the too-cheap package: a full package advertised far below PKR 220,000 usually leaves out the flight — the most expensive line of all.
  • Get the package in writing before you pay: visa, hotel names and their distance from the Haram, transport, meals, and what is not included.

Before you fly: the Nusuk app, step by step:

  • Download the official Nusuk app (Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah) and create your account with the passport details your operator used.
  • Your operator books the visa, hotels and transport; you manage your own permits in the app.
  • Book your Umrah permit for the day you plan to perform Umrah.
  • Book your Rawdah prayer slot in Madinah as early as it opens — slots fill quickly. Our Rawdah permit guide shows the steps.
  • Keep screenshots of your visa and permits offline; you will be asked to show them.

Our Nusuk App Complete Guide walks through setup in full. If you are flying into Jeddah, put your Ihram on before the Miqat crossing — the pilot usually announces it about 45 minutes before landing; see our Ihram Rules and Miqat guides, pack from our Umrah Packing List, and check our Best Time to Perform Umrah guide before fixing dates.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can I apply for an Umrah visa myself from Pakistan? No. On a Pakistani passport the Umrah visa is issued only inside a package from a Ministry of Religious Affairs attested operator, with Nusuk hotel and transport bookings made first. The only self-service route is the tourist eVisa, and only if you hold a valid, already-used US, UK or Schengen visa, or qualifying US, UK, EU or GCC residence.
  • Is there a visa on arrival for Pakistanis in Saudi Arabia? No. Pakistani citizens have no visa-on-arrival and no visa-free entry for Umrah. Your visa must be issued before you fly — either the Umrah e-visa through your operator, a qualifying tourist eVisa, or the 96-hour stopover visa booked with a Saudia or flynas ticket.
  • How much does a 10-day Umrah from Pakistan cost in 2026? About PKR 275,000–360,000 per person for an economy 10-day package with flights (quad sharing, 3-star hotels), based on November 2026 ranges. Budget trips start near PKR 245,000 and 5-star Haram-side trips pass PKR 420,000. Always compare itemised written quotes from at least three verified operators.

All prices are approximate November 2026 ranges, not quotes.

Madinah · Hotel GuideMadinah Hotels Near Masjid Nabawi — Where to Stay Near the Prophet's Mosque

Quick answer: Almost every pilgrim hotel in Madinah sits in the Markaziyah — the Central Area that rings Masjid an-Nabawi on all sides. Inside it, distance is money, exactly as in Makkah: front-row hotels under 200 metres from the mosque cost the most and ask almost nothing of your legs; the 200–500 metre band is the sweet spot for most pilgrims; beyond the Central Area you trade a lower price for a 15-minute-plus walk or a shuttle. If your Madinah nights are inside a package, the operator chooses the hotel — so this guide also shows you how to check what you are really being sold. For the Makkah side of the trip, see our Makkah Hotels Near Haram guide.

Why pilgrims pay to be close: The Prophet ﷺ said: "One prayer in my mosque is better than one thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque (in Makkah)" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1190; Sahih Muslim 1394). Staying a short walk away makes all five daily prayers in the Prophet's Mosque realistic, even for elderly parents.
Please note — ranges, not quotes: Every price on this page is an approximate nightly room range reported in September to November 2026 listings, never a fixed quote. Rates jump in Ramadan, school holidays and busy November weeks. Always confirm the live price — and the hotel's exact name and district — before you book or pay.

The distance bands around Masjid an-Nabawi:

BandDistanceWalkWhat it means
Front row0–200 m1–5 minThe towers touching the mosque courtyards inside Markaziyah. Highest prices; the right choice for elderly pilgrims, wheelchair users and families with infants
Central Area200–500 m5–10 minOuter Markaziyah. An easy walk five times a day for most people, at noticeably lower prices than the front row
Edge of centre500 m–1 km10–15 minFine for fit walkers; think honestly about doing it five times a day for a week or more
Outside the centre1 km+15–25 min or shuttleBudget districts further out. Workable only with a confirmed hotel shuttle or a taxi budget

The main hotel areas, side by side:

  • North side (King Fahd Gate side) — the most practical side for families travelling with women: women's prayer entrances are concentrated on the northern and western sides of the mosque, so a north-side hotel shortens the walk your mother, wife or daughters make five times a day. The Anwar Al Madinah Mövenpick here is described by its operator, Accor, as the nearest hotel to the women's prayer entrance.
  • South side (Bab al-Salam side) — the side men aim for: Bab al-Salam, the entrance used for the Rawdah visit and for greeting the Prophet ﷺ, is on the south-western side, and Jannatul Baqi lies to the east. Older, dense hotel stock, much of it a few minutes from the courtyard.
  • King Fahd Road (west) — major chain hotels roughly 300–800 metres out, typically 20–40% cheaper than the immediate Haram frontage for a similar standard of room.
  • As Salam district (north, beyond the Central Area) — quieter streets with mid-range and budget hotels, 10–20 minutes on foot. A fair trade for younger pilgrims who would rather spend the saving on a longer stay.

Example nightly prices (approximate, per room per night, as reported in late-2026 listings):

HotelDistanceApprox. nightly priceNotes
Sofitel Shahd Al Madinah~240 mabout SAR 8605-star, Central Area; listed at about $230 in September 2026
Anwar Al Madinah Mövenpick~240 m, north sideabout SAR 575Nearest hotel to the women's prayer entrance; listed at about $153 in September 2026

Which side suits your group?

  • Families with women: start on the north or north-west of the Central Area, near the women's prayer entrances.
  • Elderly parents or wheelchair users: ignore the side and buy the shortest genuine door-to-gate walk. A front-row room is worth more than any saving — see our Umrah for Elderly & Disabled guide for facilities.
  • Men hoping to visit the Rawdah: the south side, near Bab al-Salam, shortens the Rawdah route — but the permit itself is booked in the Nusuk app; see our Rawdah Permit guide.
  • Budget travellers: outer Markaziyah (200–500 m) keeps the walk easy without the front-row premium; beyond that, confirm the shuttle in writing.

Booking inside a package — the checks that matter: On the Pakistani and most other Umrah visa routes, your Madinah hotel is booked by your operator through Nusuk, so the hotel in your package is a decision made for you. Before you pay, get the exact hotel name (not "a 4-star near the Haram"), search its real walking distance to the mosque courtyard, and check whether your room is quad, triple or double sharing — the same package price can hide very different rooms. Our Umrah Cost from Pakistan breakdown shows what the Madinah nights should cost. A "Haram view" room costs more and is worth it to some pilgrims; a high-floor room facing the minarets is the cheaper way to keep the view.

Getting to your hotel: Madinah's Prince Mohammad bin Abdulaziz Airport (MED) is about 15 km from the Central Area, roughly 20–25 minutes by taxi. Coming from Makkah, the Haramain High-Speed Train reaches Madinah station in about two hours, with buses and taxis from the station to Markaziyah; our Makkah to Madinah transport guide compares train, bus and taxi. Once you are settled, plan your days with our Madinah Ziyarat guide — Masjid Quba and Jannatul Baqi are the visits almost every pilgrim makes.

Frequently asked questions:

  • How close should a Madinah hotel be to Masjid an-Nabawi? Inside the Markaziyah Central Area if you can — under 500 metres means every prayer is an easy walk. Under 200 metres is front row and best for elderly pilgrims. Beyond 1 km, only book if a frequent hotel shuttle is confirmed in writing.
  • Which side of the Prophet's Mosque is best for women? The north and north-west sides of the Central Area, because women's prayer entrances are concentrated on the northern and western sides of the mosque. The Anwar Al Madinah Mövenpick on the north side is marketed as the nearest hotel to the women's prayer entrance.
  • How much does a hotel near Masjid an-Nabawi cost per night? In late-2026 listings, front-row 5-star rooms ran from about SAR 470 to SAR 860 a night; Central Area rooms were about SAR 300–500, rising in November; and simpler hotels at the edge of the centre could be found around SAR 370 in quiet weeks. Ramadan prices are far higher — book months ahead.

(2026); Sahih al-Bukhari 1190; Sahih Muslim 1394. Prices are approximate reported ranges — confirm the live rate before booking.

Umrah · India GuideUmrah from India — Visa & Flights Guide

Planning Umrah from India is straightforward once you know which visa route applies to you. The one fact that surprises most first-time pilgrims is this: India is not on Saudi Arabia's tourist eVisa list, so most Indian passport holders cannot apply for a visa online by themselves. The standard route is a dedicated Umrah visa arranged through an approved agent on the Nusuk platform, with your hotel and transport booked as part of the package. This guide covers all three real routes, the documents you need, flights from Indian cities, and what the trip costs in rupees.

"And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Quran 3:97, Sahih International)

Do Indian citizens need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Every Indian passport holder needs a valid Saudi visa to enter the Kingdom and perform Umrah. There is no visa-free entry and no visa-on-arrival for Indian citizens travelling on an ordinary Indian passport alone. The Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah confirms that holders of tourist, eVisa and Umrah visas can all perform Umrah while in Saudi Arabia, as long as they secure the Umrah permit through the Nusuk app.

Route 1: Umrah visa through an approved agent (the route most pilgrims use): This is the standard route for Indian passport holders living in India. You book a package through an Umrah agent in India who is approved by the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. The agent arranges the visa through the Nusuk system together with your hotel and transport bookings. In 2026, Nusuk hotel and transport bookings are mandatory, and standalone visa-only bookings are not available for Indian passport holders — the visa comes as part of a package.

Key rules for the 1448 AH Umrah season:

  • The visa is valid for 30 days from the date it is issued, reduced from 90 days in earlier seasons. You must enter Saudi Arabia within that 30-day window. Once you enter, you can stay up to 90 days.
  • The 1448 season runs to 7 April 2027. Visa issuance ends on 9 March 2027 and the last entry date is 23 March 2027, so plan your travel dates before you apply.
  • Since July 2026 there is also a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa, valid for 365 days with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days. Each entry needs its own service package booked through an approved Nusuk provider, plus an Umrah permit in the Nusuk app. It is not valid during the Hajj season.
  • Umrah visas are not issued in the weeks around Hajj.

Before paying any agent, ask for the package in writing: the visa, hotel names and their distance from the Haram, transport, meals if included, and what is not included. A genuine agent will give you all of this without hesitation.

Route 2: Saudi tourist eVisa (only if you qualify): India is not among the 72 nationalities eligible for Saudi Arabia's direct tourist eVisa — that list was expanded on 5 November 2026 and India is still not on it. But an Indian passport holder can still apply for the tourist eVisa if any one of these applies to you:

  • You hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visit visa that you have already used to enter that country.
  • You are a permanent resident of the US, the UK or an EU country.
  • You are a resident of a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) country.

Apply directly on the official portal, visa.visitsaudi.com. Our Umrah Visa for UK & US Citizens guide walks through the eVisa steps in detail. The tourist eVisa permits Umrah, but not Hajj, and you still need to book your Umrah permit on Nusuk before entering the Haram. Note that since February 2025, Indian nationals have been limited to single-entry visit visas, so do not rely on a family visit visa as your Umrah route — use the dedicated Umrah visa instead.

Route 3: the 96-hour stopover visa (free): If you are flying with Saudia or flynas and transiting through Saudi Arabia, you can get a free 96-hour stopover visa. Within those 96 hours you can perform Umrah, provided you book your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app. This suits pilgrims who are already flying through Jeddah or Riyadh to another destination, but it is a tight window — it is not a substitute for a proper Umrah trip if you want unhurried days in Makkah and Madinah.

What the visa costs: The Saudi government charges SAR 300 for the visa plus SAR 100 to 180 for mandatory health insurance, a total of SAR 400 to 480 before any agent service fee. Indian agents advertise visa-only prices from around ₹14,990 to ₹15,999, with full packages priced separately. Always ask for a written breakdown of the government fee, insurance and the agent's own service charge. See also our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide for the full breakdown by visa type.

Documents checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months from your arrival date, with blank pages.
  • Recent passport-size photograph.
  • Meningococcal meningitis (ACWY) vaccination certificate, taken at least 10 days before arrival. Carry the original certificate with you.
  • Confirmed hotel and transport bookings made through Nusuk by your agent — mandatory in 2026.
  • Confirmed return ticket.
  • Your agent may ask you to complete biometrics in the Saudi Visa Bio app. If so, do it as soon as the agent asks, because the visa cannot be filed until it is done.

Flights from India to Jeddah and Madinah: Direct flights operate from Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Lucknow, on Saudia, IndiGo, Air India, Air India Express and Flynas, with one-stop options on Gulf carriers. Mumbai to Jeddah is about four and a half hours nonstop; Delhi to Jeddah is about six hours and forty minutes. You can fly into Jeddah (JED) for Makkah, or into Madinah (MED) if you want to start your trip in Madinah. Once you land, see our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide for taxi, bus and train options and 2026 costs.

Recent one-way economy fares seen in November 2026 checks:

  • Mumbai to Jeddah on IndiGo: median fare ₹26,579; lowest fare seen ₹15,655.
  • Delhi to Jeddah on IndiGo: median fare ₹39,377; best fare found ₹22,325.
  • Mumbai to Jeddah return: typically ₹30,551 to ₹44,609.
  • India to Madinah one-way from ₹17,803; return from ₹37,208.

Fares change daily and rise sharply in Ramadan and school holidays, so treat these as a guide and check live prices for your dates before booking.

Package or DIY? Most first-time pilgrims from India take a package, and on the Umrah visa route the package is effectively how the visa is issued. Advertised November 2026 package prices from Indian operators: economy 15 to 17-day packages from ₹99,000 per person; a 7-day Ramadan package from ₹98,000; deluxe packages around ₹1,24,000; and super-deluxe five-star packages around ₹1,45,000. All are per person on a sharing basis and include return flights, visa, hotels, transport and ziyarat. If you qualify for the tourist eVisa route, you can also book everything yourself — flights, hotels and transport — and manage the trip independently.

Best time to go from India: Winter, from November to February, is the most comfortable weather for Umrah, with cooler days and pleasant nights. The quieter weeks after Hajj and in late autumn often have the lowest fares. Ramadan is the most crowded and most expensive time, and Umrah visas are not issued around Hajj, so avoid planning travel in the Hajj window. Remember the 1448 season deadline: every Umrah visitor must leave Saudi Arabia by 7 April 2027.

Before you fly: the Nusuk app: Download the official Nusuk app and create your account before you travel — our Nusuk app guide walks through setup step by step. Use it to book your Umrah permit and your Rawdah prayer slot in Madinah. Permits are free and are issued only through the official Nusuk app. Book your Rawdah slot as early as you can, because slots fill quickly, and keep your passport and visa details handy when you register.

Practical tips:

  • Wear your Ihram before crossing the Miqat if you are flying directly to Jeddah; the pilot usually announces the Miqat about 45 minutes before landing.
  • Carry some Saudi riyals in cash for small expenses. Cards are widely accepted in Makkah and Madinah, but small shops and taxis may prefer cash.
  • Pack using our Umrah packing list so nothing essential is left behind.
  • Keep your hotel booking reference, return ticket and vaccination certificate in your hand luggage, not in checked bags.
  • Save your agent's number and your hotel address on your phone before you leave India.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can Indians apply for a Saudi eVisa directly? No. India is not on the tourist eVisa country list. You can only use the eVisa route if you hold a used US, UK or Schengen visa, hold permanent residence in the US, UK or EU, or live in a GCC country. Everyone else uses the Umrah visa through an approved agent.
  • How long is the Umrah visa valid? You must enter Saudi Arabia within 30 days of the visa being issued, and you can then stay up to 90 days. For the 1448 season, visas stop being issued on 9 March 2027, the last entry is 23 March 2027, and all visitors must leave by 7 April 2027.
  • Can I perform Umrah on a stopover in Saudi Arabia? Yes. The free 96-hour stopover visa on Saudia or flynas lets you perform Umrah if you book your Umrah permit in the Nusuk app. It is a short window, so it suits a brief visit rather than a full Umrah trip.

Umrah · Bangladesh GuideUmrah from Bangladesh — Visa, Flights & Costs Guide

Umrah from Bangladesh is a well-travelled route: direct flights leave Dhaka every week, licensed agencies in Dhaka handle the visa, and a full 10 to 14-day trip can be done on a modest budget if you book early. The rules changed in 2026, so this guide uses the current requirements — the 30-day visa entry window, mandatory Nusuk hotel and transport bookings, and the biometric step that now applies to Bangladeshi applicants.

Do Bangladeshis need a visa for Umrah? Yes. Bangladeshi passport holders must obtain an Umrah e-visa through an authorised operator before travelling. There is no visa-free entry and no visa on arrival for Bangladeshi citizens. The visa is issued electronically through the Nusuk and Maqam systems, so there is no need to visit the Saudi embassy in Dhaka for a standard Umrah visa — but you cannot apply for it on your own. It must be processed through a licensed Umrah agency.

Route 1: Umrah visa through a licensed agency (the route almost everyone uses): Choose a Hajj and Umrah agency in Bangladesh that is registered with the Ministry of Religious Affairs. The agency files your visa with a Saudi-licensed Umrah company through the Maqam system, after booking your hotel and transport in Nusuk.

Key rules for the 1448 AH Umrah season:

  • The visa must be used within 30 days of the day it is issued. If you have not entered Saudi Arabia by then, it is cancelled automatically, so apply only when your flight dates are fixed.
  • The permitted stay is printed on your e-visa. Agencies commonly quote a stay of up to 90 days, but always confirm the exact stay shown on your own e-visa before you travel.
  • The 1448 season runs to 7 April 2027. The last day to get a visa is 9 March 2027, the last day to enter Saudi Arabia is 23 March 2027, and every Umrah visitor must leave by 7 April 2027.
  • Since July 2026 there is also a one-year multiple-entry Umrah visa, valid for 365 days with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days. Each entry needs its own service package booked through a Nusuk-approved provider, plus an Umrah permit in the Nusuk app. It cannot be used during the Hajj season.
  • Umrah visas are not issued in the weeks around Hajj.

Route 2: Saudi tourist eVisa (only if you qualify): Bangladesh is not on the list of nationalities eligible for the Saudi tourist eVisa. A Bangladeshi passport holder can still apply if you hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visa that has been used at least once, are a permanent resident of the US, the UK or an EU country, or are a resident of a GCC country. The eVisa is valid for one year with multiple entries, each visit up to 90 days, and it permits Umrah outside the Hajj season. You book your own Umrah permit in the Nusuk app.

Route 3: the 96-hour stopover visa (free): If you are flying with Saudia or flynas and transiting through Saudi Arabia to another country, you can get a free 96-hour stopover visa and perform Umrah within those four days, with a Nusuk permit. It is a useful option if you are already travelling through Jeddah, but it is a short window for a full Umrah trip.

What changed in 2026: Three changes matter most for Bangladeshi pilgrims. First, the visa entry window is now 30 days from issue, not 90 — book your flights first, then apply for the visa. Second, Nusuk-verified hotel and transport bookings are now mandatory: every application must be tied to confirmed accommodation and transport before the visa is filed. Third, biometrics are now mandatory for Bangladeshi applicants: you must enrol your fingerprints and photo in the official Saudi Visa Bio app before the visa is issued.

Documents checklist:

  • Passport valid for at least six months from entry, with two or more blank pages.
  • Recent passport photograph with a white background.
  • Meningococcal (ACWY) vaccination certificate, taken at least 10 days before arrival, for everyone aged one year and over.
  • Fingerprints and photo enrolled in the Saudi Visa Bio app.
  • Hotel and transport confirmed in Nusuk by your agency before the visa is issued, with the booking reference.
  • Confirmed return air ticket — this must be shown when the file is opened.
  • A dual-currency card or cash in US dollars or Saudi riyals for spending in the Kingdom.

Flights from Dhaka to Jeddah and Madinah: Biman Bangladesh Airlines and Saudia operate direct flights from Dhaka (DAC) to Jeddah (JED) and Madinah (MED) in about six to six and a half hours. One-stop budget options include Gulf Air, SalamAir, Jazeera Airways, Air Arabia and Kuwait Airways. If you fly into Jeddah, wear your Ihram before crossing the Miqat — the pilot announces it about 45 minutes before landing on Biman and Saudia flights.

Recent return fares seen in 2026 checks:

  • Direct round trip, Dhaka to Jeddah or Madinah: BDT 74,000 to BDT 92,000.
  • One-stop round trip: BDT 56,000 to BDT 68,000.
  • One-way fares are quoted from around ৳48,000.

Fares change with the season and rise sharply in Ramadan, so treat these as a guide and check live prices for your dates.

Full cost breakdown: a 10-day Umrah from Bangladesh: All figures are per person in Bangladeshi taka (BDT), based on 2026 operator and guide prices. Prices move with the season, the hotel's distance from the Haram, and how early you book — always confirm the final price in writing before paying.

Visa and insurance:

  • Official Saudi visa fee: SAR 300, plus mandatory insurance.
  • Agency visa-only price: BDT 15,500 to BDT 19,500, or around BDT 17,000 with hotel and food booking references provided. Without those references, agencies quote around BDT 20,000. For the full fee picture, see our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide.

Flights (return, Dhaka to Jeddah or Madinah):

  • Budget, one-stop: BDT 56,000 to BDT 68,000.
  • Direct, Biman or Saudia: BDT 74,000 to BDT 92,000.

Hotels (5 nights Makkah plus 4 nights Madinah, per person on a sharing basis):

  • Budget three-star with shuttle: from around BDT 22,000.
  • Walking-distance four or five-star: up to around BDT 55,000.

Food and local transport:

  • Food: budget around BDT 1,000 to BDT 1,500 a day at local restaurants if your package does not include meals.
  • Makkah to Madinah: the Haramain high-speed train costs roughly SAR 50 to SAR 150 per person, booked on sar.hhr.sa. See our Makkah–Madinah transport guide for train times, bus options and fares. Airport transfers and ziyarat transport are usually included in a package.

Total for a 10-day trip, per person:

Trip styleTotal cost
Budget (one-stop flights, shuttle hotel, sharing)BDT 1,16,000 to BDT 1,32,000
Mid-range (direct flights, nearer hotel)BDT 1,35,000 to BDT 1,80,000
Comfort (direct flights, walking-distance four or five-star hotels)BDT 1,65,000 to BDT 2,15,000

Full packages advertised by Dhaka operators in November 2026: economy packages from ৳1,25,000 per person; a 14-day Saudia direct package from ৳1,70,000 for quad sharing, ৳1,85,000 for triple and ৳2,15,000 for double; and 14-day premium packages from ৳3,00,000 to ৳3,50,000. Packages normally include the visa, return flights, hotels, airport and Haram transfers, ziyarat in both cities and a Bengali-speaking guide. Ramadan departures cost significantly more. Travelling outside Ramadan and the Hajj window keeps costs down — see our best time for Umrah guide for the cheapest months.

Package or DIY? A package is the simplest choice and is how most Bangladeshis travel, because the visa itself is issued through an agency. But once you hold a valid Umrah e-visa or stopover visa, you are free to book your own flights and hotels and travel at your own pace. If you go DIY, book your Nusuk hotel and transport first, because the visa application depends on them.

Before you fly: the Nusuk app: Once your visa is issued, create an account on the official Nusuk app using your visa number and passport number — our Nusuk app guide walks through setup step by step. Use it to book your Umrah appointment slot and your Rawdah permit in Madinah. Rawdah permits for men and women open on separate schedules, so check Nusuk early and book as soon as your slot window opens. Permits are free and are issued only through the official Nusuk app.

Avoiding scams: Umrah fraud is a real problem, and the protection is simple. Use only an agency registered under the Hajj and Umrah Management Act 2021, ask for its licence number, and find it on the Ministry of Religious Affairs' approved list before paying. Get the package in writing: hotel names and their distance from the Haram, flight details, transport, meals and what is not included. Beware of prices far below the market — they usually mean a hotel far from the Haram or a visa that never arrives.

Hajj is a separate journey: Umrah and Hajj are different. You cannot perform the obligatory Hajj on an Umrah visa, a transit visa or a tourist visa. Hajj from Bangladesh runs on a strict quota system through the Ministry of Religious Affairs portal (hajj.gov.bd), with official pre-registration and final registration using your NID and e-passport. Saudi authorities enforce heavy penalties for attempting Hajj without an official Hajj permit — fines of SAR 10,000 or more, deportation and a 10-year entry ban.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Can Bangladeshis apply for an Umrah visa themselves on Nusuk? Not in practice. Bangladeshi ordinary passport holders get their Umrah visa through a Hajj and Umrah agency licensed by the Ministry of Religious Affairs, which works with a Saudi Umrah company. You still use the Nusuk app yourself for Umrah and Rawdah permits.
  • How much does an Umrah visa cost from Bangladesh? The official Saudi fee is SAR 300 plus mandatory insurance. Agencies in Dhaka charge around BDT 15,500 to BDT 20,000 for the visa and insurance, depending on whether hotel and food booking references are provided. A full 10-day trip usually totals BDT 1,16,000 to BDT 2,15,000 per person, depending on flights and hotels.
  • Can women travel for Umrah from Bangladesh without a mahram? Women aged 18 and over may perform Umrah without a mahram when travelling with an organised group, under the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah's rules. Check the current rule with your agency before booking, and read our guide for women travelling alone for the practical details.

Sources: URAL, "DIY Umrah from Bangladesh: Cost, Visa & Nusuk" (ural-travel.pages.dev); goFLY, "Umrah Visa from Bangladesh 2026" (goflybd.com); FlyNext, "Umrah Visa from Bangladesh: Documents & Steps" and "Umrah Visa from Bangladesh: Rules & Season Dates" (flynext.tours); Darbiya, "Umrah visa vs tourist visa for Bangladeshis" (darbiya.com); Travel Router, "Umrah Visa from Bangladesh 2026" (travelrouter.net); Umrah.com.bd packages (umrah.bd); Amin Travels Umrah packages (amintravels.com.bd); Holy Hajj & Umrah premium packages (holyhajjnumrah.com); Sky Holidays December Special Umrah Package 2026 (skyholidayshajj.com); Nusuk (nusuk.sa); Bangladesh Ministry of Religious Affairs Hajj portal (hajj.gov.bd).

Umrah Visa · eVisa GuideUmrah Visa for UK & US Citizens — eVisa Steps

Quick answer: If you hold a passport from the UK, the US or one of the other eligible countries, you do not need an agent, an embassy visit or a paper application to get permission for Umrah. Saudi Arabia's tourist eVisa, applied for online at the official portal visa.visitsaudi.com, covers Umrah outside the Hajj season. It is valid for one year, allows multiple entries, and permits stays of up to 90 days at a time. Most applications are decided within 24–72 hours. One step remains after the visa arrives: registering on Nusuk and booking the free Umrah permit, because the visa alone does not book your Umrah. This guide covers who is eligible, what it really costs, the application step by step, and the season dates that matter. Once the visa is sorted, our Umrah Cost 2026 guide shows what the rest of the trip adds up to.

Who can use the eVisa: Citizens of 66 countries can apply, including the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia, most European Union states, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia. The full country list sits on the portal itself, and it changes from time to time, so check your nationality there before anything else. The eVisa is a tourist visa that permits Umrah; it does not permit Hajj, paid work or study, and it cannot be converted into another visa type inside the Kingdom. If your country is not on the list, do not give up on the trip — the dedicated Umrah visa route further down this page was built for you.

What the eVisa gives you: One approval covers a full year of travel. You may enter Saudi Arabia multiple times within that year and stay up to 90 days on each visit, which makes the eVisa the natural choice for pilgrims who hope to return — for a second Umrah, or for Ramadan — without applying again. Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your travel dates; if it expires sooner, renew it before you apply, because the eVisa is issued against the passport you apply with. Medical insurance is not optional and not separate: every eVisa carries mandatory health insurance, assigned to you during the application and included in what you pay at checkout.

What it costs — the honest table:

ItemCostNotes
Government eVisa feeSAR 300Fixed fee, paid at checkout on the portal
Medical insurance (mandatory)Varies by insurerAssigned automatically during the application
Total eVisa costAbout SAR 400–535 (roughly $107–142)Depends on the insurer assigned to your application
Visa on arrivalAbout SAR 480For eligible nationals who prefer to apply at the airport

Because the insurance premium differs by insurer, two pilgrims can pay slightly different totals for the same visa. Treat every figure in this table — and every figure quoted by any agent — as an estimate: the total shown on the portal's checkout screen, before you pay, is the final truth.

How to apply — step by step:

  • Step 1 — Check your passport. Confirm it has at least six months' validity beyond your return date, and that the name on it is the name you will use everywhere else.
  • Step 2 — Go to the official portal. Open visa.visitsaudi.com and create an account with an email address you actually read — the decision and the eVisa itself arrive by email.
  • Step 3 — Start the application and choose the eVisa. Select the tourist eVisa and confirm your nationality is on the eligible list.
  • Step 4 — Enter your details exactly as printed in the passport. Names, passport number and dates must match letter for letter; a mismatch is the most common cause of delay.
  • Step 5 — Add your travel information and photo. Give your expected travel dates and upload a recent photograph that meets the portal's size and background requirements.
  • Step 6 — Review the assigned medical insurance. The portal attaches a policy from an approved Saudi insurer; its premium is added to your total.
  • Step 7 — Pay by card and submit. Check the full total on the checkout screen first — that figure is the one that counts — then pay and note your application reference.
  • Step 8 — Wait for the email, then print. Decisions typically take 24–72 hours, and many arrive within 6–12 hours. Print a paper copy of the eVisa and keep the PDF on your phone as well.

Visa on arrival — the alternative: Eligible nationals can instead obtain a visa on arrival at Saudi airports for about SAR 480, insurance included. There is also a wider door: holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen visa that has already been used to enter the country that issued it can get a visa on arrival regardless of their own nationality. The eVisa is still the calmer option for most pilgrims — it removes the airport queue, the card-terminal risk and any doubt before you board — but the arrival route is a genuine fallback if your plans change at the last minute.

After the visa — Nusuk registration is mandatory: A visa gets you into the Kingdom; it does not book your Umrah. Before you travel, register on nusuk.sa or in the Nusuk app and book the free Umrah permit for the day and time you plan to perform Umrah, and the Rawdah appointment for Madinah. Our Nusuk App Complete Guide walks through registration and permits screen by screen, and our Rawdah Permit guide covers booking the Rawdah slot, which fills fastest. Do this as soon as your dates are fixed — permits are released in batches and the popular times go first. With visa and permits in hand, work through our Umrah Packing List and choose your travel dates with our Best Time to Perform Umrah guide.

Health rule — do not leave it late: Pilgrims must show a meningitis ACWY vaccination received at least 10 days before travel. Book the vaccine as soon as your trip is likely, not the week you fly, and carry the certificate with your passport. Requirements are checked, and a certificate dated too close to departure can stop a journey at the airport.

Women travelling without a Mahram: Under the current rules, women aged 18 and over may travel for Umrah without a Mahram, and the eVisa application asks for no Mahram details. Women under 18 travel with a parent or guardian, as do all minors.

The 1448H Umrah season — key dates: Dedicated Umrah visa issuance for the 1448H season resumed on 31 May 2026. The last Umrah visa will be issued on 9 March 2027, the last entry on an Umrah visa is 23 March 2027, and all pilgrims who entered on an Umrah visa must leave by 7 April 2027, ahead of the Hajj season. If you are travelling anywhere near those closing dates, build your itinerary backwards from them and leave yourself margin — a missed deadline is not something an airline or an agent can fix at the airport.

Not on the eVisa list? The dedicated Umrah visa: Pilgrims whose nationality is not among the 66 can apply for a dedicated Umrah visa through the Nusuk Umrah platform at umrah.nusuk.sa. This route works differently: your hotel and transport bookings must be logged in Nusuk as part of the application, usually through an authorised Umrah company, and the issued visa must be used to enter Saudi Arabia within 30 days of issuance — so apply once your bookings are real, not months ahead on a hope. The Umrah permit and Rawdah bookings then follow in Nusuk exactly as they do for eVisa holders.

Please note — check the official portal before you book: Visa fees, insurance assignment and the eligible-country list all change, sometimes with little notice. This guide reflects the position checked in November 2026, but visa.visitsaudi.com on the day you apply is the final truth — if any figure or rule there differs from what you read here or anywhere else, the portal wins.

Quick questions:

  • Can UK and US citizens really perform Umrah on a tourist eVisa? Yes. The Saudi tourist eVisa covers Umrah outside the Hajj season for citizens of the 66 eligible countries, the UK and US included. You still need to register on Nusuk and book the free Umrah permit before you perform Umrah — the visa is entry permission, the permit is your Umrah booking.
  • How long does the eVisa take to come through? Typically 24–72 hours, and often within 6–12 hours. Apply at least a week before you fly anyway: a passport-detail mismatch or a photo rejection is easy to fix with days in hand and stressful without them.
  • What if my country is not on the eVisa list? Use the dedicated Umrah visa route via umrah.nusuk.sa, with your hotel and transport bookings logged in Nusuk as part of the application. Enter within 30 days of the visa being issued, and observe the season deadlines — for 1448H, the last Umrah visa is issued on 9 March 2027.

Umrah · Family GuideUmrah with Kids — Complete Family Guide

Quick answer: There is no minimum age for Umrah — a baby can be carried through every rite, and families do it every day of the year. The paperwork line sits at age five: the Nusuk Umrah permit starts at five, and children under five enter both mosques with their parents without a permit of their own. Every child, infants included, needs their own passport and visa, and everyone under 18 must travel with a parent or guardian. Beyond the paperwork, a family Umrah succeeds or fails on pacing: short visits, cool hours, a hotel near the Haram and a carrier you trust. This guide covers the rules first, then the age-by-age practice. If grandparents are coming too, pair it with our Umrah for Elderly Parents guide — the same gentle rhythm serves both ends of the family.

Children in Umrah — the religious basis: Taking children is not a modern concession; it is established practice from the Prophet's ﷺ own time. Ibn Abbas narrated that a woman lifted a child toward the Prophet ﷺ and asked, "Is there Hajj for this one?" He replied: "Yes, and you will have a reward" (Sahih Muslim 1336a). For a child below the age of discernment — generally under seven — the parent forms the intention of Ihram on the child's behalf and guides them through the rites; older children make their own intention with your help. One point to hold clearly: an Umrah performed before puberty is valid and rewarded, but it does not count as the obligatory one — your child will perform Umrah again as an adult with the duty fully their own. Nothing about that diminishes the trip: the reward is real, and so is the memory you are planting.

Permits and paperwork, child by child:

  • Passport and visa: every child — including a newborn — travels on their own passport with their own visa. There is no "added to a parent's passport" route.
  • Nusuk permit: children aged five and over need an Umrah permit booked on Nusuk like any other pilgrim; under-fives need no permit and enter Masjid al-Haram and the Prophet's Mosque with their parents.
  • Supervision: under-18s must be accompanied by a parent or guardian throughout the trip.
  • ID wristband: put a wristband on every young child with a parent's name and mobile number, and agree a fixed meeting point. In a crowd of a million, this five-minute job is the one that matters.

Vaccines — the rule covers children too: The meningitis ACWY requirement is not adults-only. Each child must be vaccinated at least 10 days before arrival, with a conjugate vaccine given within the last 5 years or a polysaccharide vaccine within the last 3 years. Book the children's appointments when you book your own, and carry every certificate together in one documents folder — checks happen, and a missing child's certificate holds up the whole family.

Strollers — where they work and where they do not: Strollers are banned on the ground-floor Mataf, the open floor circling the Kaaba, for safety and crowd density — no exceptions are made at the barrier, so do not plan a ground-floor Tawaf around one. They are generally permitted in the Mas'a corridor where Sa'i is walked, on the upper floors and in the outer courtyards. The kit that works, in practice: a soft carrier or sling for Tawaf and Sa'i, keeping your hands free and your child against you in the densest crowds, and a compact, foldable stroller for everything else — the hotel-to-Haram walk, the courtyards, and the long, calmer spaces of Madinah. If you only bring one, bring the carrier.

A facility most families never hear of — the Children's Nursery Centers: Inside the Grand Mosque's third expansion, the mosque runs Children's Nursery Centers staffed by trained carers, with meals and sleeping rooms, caring for girls aged 1–10 and boys aged 1–8 and handling around 1,500 children a day. For parents who want one rite — a quiet Tawaf, performed without a toddler in their arms — this is the official answer. Ask at the mosque's service points in the third expansion for the current intake arrangements when you arrive, as procedures are set by the mosque administration.

Age by age — what actually works:

  • Babies under 2: The easiest travellers of all, if you protect the routine. Carry them in a sling for the rites, time mosque visits around feeds and naps, and choose the quiet hours — after Fajr and late at night. Everything else is logistics: milk, nappies and a change of clothes for you as well as the baby, all in the bag you take into the mosque.
  • Toddlers 2–4: Mobile, curious and tireless at exactly the wrong moments. Keep Haram visits short and frequent rather than long; use the stroller everywhere it is allowed and the carrier where it is not; keep snacks and water on you; and expect to leave mid-plan sometimes — a calm exit beats a meltdown in the Mataf crowd.
  • School-age 5–12: Now it becomes their Umrah too. They need their own Nusuk permit; teach them the Talbiyah and a short dua before you travel; give them real jobs — carrying the Zamzam bottle, counting Tawaf circuits, holding the family's dua list. Most children this age can walk Sa'i at a gentle pace with breaks at the Zamzam points.
  • Teens 11+: Give them responsibility, not just instructions: navigating to the hotel, helping grandparents, keeping the group's documents photographed and backed up. A teen who is trusted with the trip's real work remembers it entirely differently from one who was simply brought along.

When to go with children: Heat is the family's real opponent. Makkah's summer passes 45°C, and small children dehydrate faster than adults and complain later. Aim for the mild months — roughly November to February — when Tawaf and the walk to the hotel stay comfortable for little legs; our Best Time to Perform Umrah guide maps weather, crowds and prices month by month. School holidays will pull you toward peak weeks; if you must travel then, lean harder on the quiet hours and the short-visit rhythm.

Where to stay: With children, distance is the whole decision. A hotel a short, flat walk from a Haram gate means a tired child is in bed ten minutes after leaving the mosque; a cheaper hotel across town means shuttle timetables ruling your prayers and your naps. Prioritise a family room, a fridge for milk and snacks, and breakfast timings that survive a Fajr start. Our Makkah Hotels Near Haram guide compares the areas by walking distance, and the same logic applies to your Madinah nights — the days there, planned with our Madinah Ziyarat guide, are usually the gentlest of the trip for children.

Between the two cities — the Haramain train with kids: The high-speed train is usually the family's best crossing: air-conditioned, spacious, and about two and a half hours against five on the road. On current published terms, children under 2 travel free on an adult's lap, and ages 2–11 travel at a discounted fare — but fares and child policies are revised, so confirm the current fare before booking. Book seats together, arrive with margin for the station taxi at each end, and keep the documents folder in hand luggage, never in the checked bags.

Packing checklist — the child-specific layer: Our Umrah Packing List covers the family's full list; add these for the children:

  • Soft carrier or sling, plus a compact foldable stroller.
  • ID wristbands with a parent's name and phone number.
  • Children's medicines, rehydration sachets and any prescription items, in hand luggage.
  • Snacks your children will actually eat, a refillable water bottle, wipes and nappy supplies for mosque-length outings.
  • A full change of clothes per child in the day bag — Zamzam spills and travel days guarantee the need.
  • Sun hat and light layers; mosque air-conditioning is cold on small bodies even when Makkah is hot.
  • One familiar comfort item from home, and a small dua book or audio duas for older children.

Quick questions:

  • Does my baby need their own visa and permit? Visa — yes: every child, including infants, needs their own passport and visa. Permit — only from age five: the Nusuk Umrah permit starts at five, and under-fives enter both mosques with their parents without a permit.
  • Can I take a stroller into the Grand Mosque? Not onto the ground-floor Mataf around the Kaaba, where strollers are banned for safety. They are generally permitted in the Mas'a corridor, on upper floors and in the outer courtyards. For Tawaf itself, use a soft carrier or sling.
  • Does my child's Umrah count, or must they repeat it? It counts as a valid, rewarded voluntary Umrah — the Prophet ﷺ confirmed the reward for the child and the parent alike (Sahih Muslim 1336a). It does not discharge the obligation, so they will perform Umrah again after puberty as their own duty.

Sources: Umrah with Kids Guide — Wego Blog ↗ · Umrah with Children Guide — Umrah My Way ↗ · Umrah with Kids Guide — Mecca Madinah Connect ↗ · Sahih Muslim 1336a — Sunnah.com ↗ — rules checked November 2026; confirm permits and fares before booking

Umrah · Elderly ParentsUmrah for Elderly Parents — Tips & Facilities

Quick answer: Taking elderly parents for Umrah is one of the most rewarding journeys a family can make, and the Two Holy Mosques are built for it: free wheelchairs around the clock, bookable electric carts, step-free gates, wheelchair lanes for Tawaf and Sa'i, and staff whose whole job is helping older pilgrims. What decides how easy the trip feels is not money — it is planning around your parents' energy: a hotel on a flat, short route, travel in the mild months, and every booking made before you leave home. This guide is written for the sons and daughters doing that planning. For the full list of accessibility services in both mosques, see our Umrah for Elderly & Disabled guide.

Wheelchairs at the Haram — free first: The General Authority for the Care of the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques lends manual wheelchairs free of charge, 24 hours a day, in Masjid al-Haram. The published collection points are the eastern courtyard at Bab Al Salam (Gate 19) and the western courtyard at the Al Shubaika Bridge. The chair is for use inside the mosque only and is returned to the point afterwards; you may be asked to leave an ID document as a deposit, and a family member does the pushing. Supply is first-come, first-served and runs short at peak times — Ramadan nights, Fridays and the last ten nights — so collect a chair early, not on your way into Tawaf.

Paid options, when free is not enough:

  • Official wheelchair pushers wait at the mosque's cart counters and entrances. Use the official counters only, and agree the price and the scope (Tawaf only, or Tawaf and Sa'i) before you start.
  • Electric carts via the Tanaqol app: Tawaf 50 SAR, Sa'i 50 SAR, the full Umrah 300 SAR — and pilgrims aged 65 and over pay half. Book in the app before you go; prices can change, so confirm in Tanaqol on the day.
  • A private rental for the whole stay: companies rent wheelchairs — including electric chairs with hotel delivery — at roughly SAR 100–120 per day. For a parent who needs a chair outside the mosque too, this is often the calmest option. Confirm the price and delivery before you pay.

Tawaf and Sa'i with limited mobility: A wheelchair Tawaf is valid — the Prophet ﷺ himself performed Tawaf riding (Sahih al-Bukhari 1633), and Allah says: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear" (Qur'an 2:286). In practice: the upper floors of the Mataf are calmer than the ground floor and are reached by lift and escalator; Sa'i has a dedicated wheelchair lane in the middle of the Mas'a, away from the fastest walkers; and the quietest hours — after Fajr and late at night — turn a crowded rite into a gentle one. Rest between the rites: sit, drink Zamzam, and only then begin Sa'i.

Hotels — distance beats stars: For an elderly parent, the best hotel is the one with the shortest, flattest walk to a Haram gate, step-free access and a lift that fits a wheelchair. A modest hotel 200 flat metres away is worth more than a grand one up a slope or a shuttle ride away — and shuttle drop-off points can still leave a long walk. Before paying, ask the hotel directly: is the route from the drop-off point to the gate step-free? How big is the lift? Can a wheelchair be stored or charged in the room? Our Makkah Hotels Near Haram guide compares the areas around the mosque.

Getting there, and between the two cities: Book airline wheelchair assistance when you buy the tickets — it is free, and a staff member meets your parent at the aircraft and stays with them through the airport. From Jeddah, the options are set out in our Jeddah Airport to Makkah guide. Between Makkah and Madinah you have a real choice:

  • Haramain high-speed train (about 2 hours 20 minutes): stations are step-free with lifts, trains carry dedicated wheelchair spaces, and staff assistance is available in the station and on board. The railway also gives 50% off for passengers with an official disability ID, and for one companion travelling with them — check the current conditions when you book. You still need a short taxi at each end. See our Haramain Train guide.
  • Private car (about 4–5 hours): slower, but door to door — no platforms, no transfers, stops whenever your parent needs one. For a parent who cannot manage a station, this is often the kinder choice; our Makkah to Madinah guide compares the costs.

Health — the part families skip: See the doctor before booking, not after: fitness to fly, and a plan for blood pressure, diabetes, heart or joint conditions. Carry all medicines in hand luggage, in their original packaging, with the prescription or a doctor's letter — our Umrah Packing List has the full checklist. Keep dose times steady across the time-zone change, and never let a parent "push through" the heat: Makkah is hot even in winter at midday, so plan rites for the cooler hours, keep water and Zamzam going, and build rest into every day. Take travel insurance that covers medical care and repatriation, and check the current vaccination requirements for the Umrah visa before you book — they change, and they are checked.

Permits — do the phone work for them: Every pilgrim needs their own Nusuk account and permits, including your parents. If the app is a struggle for them, sit with them before the trip: install it, register their account, and book the Umrah permit — and the Rawdah permit for Madinah — as early as the slots open, because the good times go first. Screenshot every permit and keep printed copies with their passports as a backup. The steps are all in our Nusuk App Complete Guide. EasyNusuk is an independent guide site — the permits themselves are only ever issued in the official Nusuk app.

When to go: For elderly parents, choose the mild months — roughly November to February — and avoid the crush of Ramadan's last ten nights and the Hajj season unless your parents are unusually strong. Our Best Time to Perform Umrah guide weighs weather, crowds and cost month by month.

What children should arrange in advance — the checklist:

  • Doctor's check-up done, medicines packed, prescription letter written, and travel insurance bought.
  • Airline wheelchair assistance requested on every flight, including connections.
  • Hotel confirmed in writing: step-free route, lift size, distance to the nearest gate.
  • Nusuk accounts set up; Umrah and Rawdah permits booked; screenshots and printouts made.
  • Tanaqol app installed for electric carts; Haramain tickets or a private car booked.
  • A gentle daily rhythm agreed: one big outing a day, rest after Dhuhr, early nights.
  • Documents in one folder your parent carries: passport copy, visa, insurance, hotel address, your phone number.

Quick questions:

  • Is the free wheelchair at the Haram really free? Yes. The General Authority lends manual wheelchairs free, 24/7, at the eastern courtyard (Bab Al Salam, Gate 19) and the western courtyard (Al Shubaika Bridge) in Masjid al-Haram. Take an ID for the deposit, use the chair inside the mosque, and return it to the same point. At peak times they run out — go early, and keep the Tanaqol electric carts (50 SAR for Tawaf) as your paid backup.
  • Can my parent complete Umrah entirely in a wheelchair? Yes. Tawaf can be done in a wheelchair — the Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf riding (Sahih al-Bukhari 1633) — on the calmer upper floors, and Sa'i has a dedicated wheelchair lane. With the free chairs, the electric carts and a companion to push, every rite can be completed without walking.
  • Train or private car between Makkah and Madinah for an elderly parent? The train is faster (about 2 hours 20 minutes), step-free and has wheelchair spaces and staff help — but it needs a taxi at both ends and a station to cross. A private car takes 4–5 hours yet goes door to door with stops on demand. If your parent tires easily or cannot transfer, the car is usually kinder; if they are steady and time matters, take the train.

Sources: Wheelchair in Haram Makkah: Free Service, Carts and Wristbands — Saudi Life Guide ↗ · Elderly & Wheelchair Guide — Mecca Madinah Connect ↗ · Haramain Railway — Guests with Disabilities or Reduced Mobility ↗ · Sahih al-Bukhari 1633 — Sunnah.com ↗ · Cart prices per the General Authority's Tanaqol service, as listed November 2026 — confirm in the app before travel

Madinah · Ziyarat GuideMadinah Ziyarat — Complete Guide

Madinah al-Munawwarah — the Illuminated City — is the city of the Prophet ﷺ and the second holiest city in Islam after Makkah. Pilgrims usually spend a few days here before or after Umrah: praying in the Prophet's Mosque and visiting the places of his life. Madinah lies about 450 km from Makkah, and the Haramain high-speed train covers the journey in about 2 hours 20 minutes. One thing to hold on to from the start: ziyarat is voluntary. None of these visits is a rite of Umrah, and none needs a ticket or a permit — except the Rawdah — so go at the pace your heart and your legs allow, and leave anything you cannot manage without regret.

Masjid an-Nabawi — the Prophet's Mosque: Built by the Prophet ﷺ himself after the Hijrah, it is the heart of every Madinah stay, and the Green Dome rises over his chamber at the mosque's south-eastern corner. Enter with your right foot, pray two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid — the greeting of the mosque — and settle into the rhythm of the place; many pilgrims aim to pray as many of their five daily prayers here as they can.

From the Sunnah: the Prophet ﷺ said: "One prayer in my mosque is better than one thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque (in Makkah)" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1190; Sahih Muslim 1394).

Etiquette in the Prophet's Mosque: Keep your voice low — Allah says: "Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet" (Qur'an 49:2) — and keep it low everywhere near his chamber. To offer your salutations, enter through Bab as-Salam (the Gate of Peace), on the western side, and walk to the front of the blessed chamber: send Salam upon the Prophet ﷺ, then move slightly to greet Abu Bakr (RA) and then Umar (RA), who rest beside him. Make your du'a to Allah alone, facing the qiblah; the Salam is a greeting, not a request. Photography and filming inside the mosque are not permitted — put the phone away indoors, and never let a picture disturb another person's prayer.

The Rawdah ash-Shareefah: Between the Prophet's chamber and his minbar lies the Rawdah, the most sought-after place of prayer in Madinah.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Between my house and my minbar is a garden from the gardens of Paradise" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1196; Sahih Muslim 1391).

Entry is by Nusuk permit only, with separate visiting periods for men and women, and slots go quickly. This guide does not repeat the booking steps — our Rawdah Permit guide walks through them one by one. Inside, pray two rak'ahs, make your du'a, and keep the visit calm and brief so others can enter.

Jannat al-Baqi: On the eastern side of the mosque lies the cemetery of Madinah, where thousands of the Companions rest — among them Uthman ibn Affan (RA), the third caliph, and the wives and daughters of the Prophet ﷺ. The gates usually open after Fajr and after Asr; men may enter, while women greet its people and make du'a from outside the railing. Go after Fajr, when it is cool and quiet. Our Jannatul Baqi guide covers the visit in full.

Masjid Quba: A short ride south of the Haram stands the first mosque in Islam, founded by the Prophet ﷺ when he arrived at Quba during the Hijrah, and praised by Allah as "a mosque founded on piety from the first day" (Qur'an 9:108). Perform wudu at your hotel before you go — the reward is recorded for the one who purifies himself at home and then prays there.

From the Sunnah: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Prayer in Masjid Quba is like Umrah" (Jami` at-Tirmidhi 324) — and in Sunan Ibn Majah 1412, two rak'ahs there carry the reward of a complete Umrah for the one who comes in a state of purity. Ibn Umar (RA) also reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to go to Quba every Saturday, walking or riding (Sahih al-Bukhari 1193) — so Saturday is the loveliest day to go, and the busiest. Our Masjid Quba guide has the history and the practical detail.

Mount Uhud: North of the city, the red ridge of Uhud overlooks the field of the battle of 3 AH, where seventy Companions were martyred — among them Hamza (RA), the Prophet's uncle. Visit the martyrs' graves, make du'a for them, and stand a moment on Archers' Hill (Jabal ar-Rumah), where the archers' early descent turned the day — a lesson in obedience that still speaks.

From the Sunnah: looking at Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it" (Sahih al-Bukhari 4083).

See our Mount Uhud guide for the story of the battle and how to plan the visit.

Masjid al-Qiblatain and the Trench: At Qiblatain, the Mosque of the Two Qiblas, the command came in the middle of a prayer to turn from Jerusalem towards the Kaaba — "So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram" (Qur'an 2:144) — and the congregation turned as one; our Masjid al-Qiblatain article tells it in full. Not far away, the site of the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq, 5 AH) — the trench dug on the advice of Salman al-Farsi (RA) — is marked by the small mosques known as the Seven Mosques; a short stop is enough.

The dates market and the Quba area: Madinah's dates are the gift pilgrims carry home across the world, and the place to compare them is the Central Dates Market (Souq Al Tumor), a short ride from the Prophet's Mosque, with more than 150 varieties on sale — Ajwa above all, then Safawi, Sukkari, Mabroom and Medjoul. Ajwa typically runs about SAR 40–120 per kilo depending on grade and packaging; taste before you buy, check the weight printed on the box, and confirm the price on the day, as prices move with the season. Date shops also cluster in the streets around the Haram and near Quba, handy if you are already out on a ziyarat round — most stalls trade from late morning into the night.

Best times for ziyarat: Start straight after Fajr — Baqi is open, Quba is cool and quiet, and you are back before the heat. Late afternoon suits Uhud and Qiblatain, and the evenings belong to the dates market and the streets around the Haram. Avoid the Friday midday crush around the mosque, and give the Rawdah whatever slot your permit gives you: build the day around it, not the other way round.

Practical tips:

  • Women's entry: women pray in their own sections of the mosque, reached by the designated women's gates — follow the signs and the staff, who manage the flows at prayer times. Rawdah visits for women run in their own periods on the Nusuk permit; follow the time printed on yours.
  • Shoes: numbered shoe racks stand at the entrances — note your rack and shelf number before you go in, or carry a small shoe bag and keep your shoes with you; in the courtyard rush, a lost sandal is a classic Madinah story.
  • Gates: learn two or three gates near your hotel and use them consistently — the mosque is vast, and a familiar gate is your landmark. For the Salam, head to Bab as-Salam on the western side.
  • Getting around: most ziyarat sites are a short taxi ride apart; agree the fare before you set off, or hire one driver for a half-day round of Quba, Qiblatain and Uhud.
  • Pace: 2–3 days covers the main ziyarat without rushing — and leaves the best hours free for prayer in the Prophet's Mosque itself. Our Makkah to Madinah guide helps you plan the journey at either end.

Quick questions:

  • Do I need a permit for Quba, Uhud or Qiblatain? No. The ziyarat sites are open visits with no permit, ticket or prescribed ritual. The only booking in Madinah is the Rawdah, which needs a free Nusuk permit — see our step-by-step Rawdah Permit guide.
  • Can women visit Jannat al-Baqi? Women greet the people of Baqi and make du'a from outside the railing; entry inside the cemetery is for men. Women visit the Rawdah in their own permitted periods and pray in the women's sections of the Prophet's Mosque.
  • How many days do I need in Madinah? 2–3 days covers the Prophet's Mosque, the Rawdah, Baqi, Quba, Uhud, Qiblatain and the Trench at a relaxed pace. Stay longer if you can — many pilgrims say the unhurried days of prayer in Masjid an-Nabawi were the heart of the whole journey.
