Tourist eVisa (online)SAR 480–535 in most 2026 guides; Visit Saudi lists SAR 395SAR 300 fee + about SAR 180 insurance + VAT/fees; 1-year multiple entry, up to 90 days per stay — the checkout screen is the final truth
Tourist visa on arrivalSAR 480SAR 300 fee + SAR 180 insurance; for eligible nationalities and holders of valid US, UK or Schengen visas
Umrah visa — government feeSAR 300 (approx. USD 80)The visa fee itself
Umrah visa — mandatory insuranceSAR 100–180Compulsory medical insurance
Umrah visa — total before agent feesAbout SAR 400–480Government fee + insurance
Agent service fee (where an agent is used)SAR 100–300Charged on top of the official total; ask for it itemised before you pay
Stopover visa (Saudia / flynas)Free96 hours in the Kingdom when you fly Saudia or flynas; Umrah is allowed during the stop
Umrah permit in the Nusuk appFreeSeparate from the visa — see below

The tourist eVisa, honestly priced: The eVisa is open to citizens of 60+ eligible countries, and also to anyone holding a valid US, UK or Schengen visa. It is a 1-year, multiple-entry visa allowing up to 90 days per stay, and it allows Umrah outside the Hajj season. Prices are quoted inconsistently, so here is the honest picture: most 2026 guides put the all-in online price at SAR 480–535 (the SAR 300 fee + about SAR 180 of insurance + VAT and processing), while Visit Saudi's own listing showed SAR 395 including insurance in October 2026. The amount on the checkout screen at visa.visitsaudi.com is the final truth on the day you apply.

How the Umrah visa is sold: The dedicated Umrah visa is issued through the Nusuk Umrah platform (umrah.nusuk.sa) or a licensed agent. Under the 2026 rule it is no longer sold standalone — it must be tied to a confirmed Nusuk-verified hotel and transport booking, and those bookings are part of the application, not an afterthought. If you are still setting the app up, our Nusuk App Guide walks through every screen, and our Umrah Visa 2026 guide explains the visa types and requirements in full.

The permit is not the visa: The Umrah permit you book in the Nusuk app once you have your visa is a separate thing — and it is free. You need both: a paid visa to enter the Kingdom, and the free permit to enter Masjid al-Haram for Umrah at your booked time. The same app books your Madinah visit — our Rawdah Permit — Step by Step guide walks through that booking — and before you pay for any visa, our Best Time to Perform Umrah guide helps you choose dates when crowds and prices are kinder.

The free stopover option: If your journey connects through Saudi Arabia on Saudia or flynas, you can take a free 96-hour stopover visa and perform Umrah during the stop. For a short visit built around a connection, that can remove the visa cost from your budget entirely.

Key dates for the 1448 AH Umrah season:

  • Visa issuance begins: 31 May 2026
  • Last Umrah visa issued: 9 March 2027
  • Last entry into the Kingdom: 23 March 2027
  • All Umrah-visa pilgrims must leave by: 7 April 2027
  • Use it or lose it: An Umrah visa must be used to enter within 30 days of issuance, or it is cancelled.

Pilgrims from Pakistan and India: You cannot apply directly through Nusuk — your Umrah visa must come through a licensed agent. On top of the official SAR 400–480, agents typically add a service fee of SAR 100–300, so ask for the government fee, the insurance and the service charge as separate lines before you pay. Agents in Pakistan currently report visa-only prices around PKR 48,000–65,000, before flights, hotels and transport are added.

Quick questions:

  • Which visa is cheapest for Umrah? The dedicated Umrah visa — about SAR 400–480 in government fee and insurance before agent charges. The tourist eVisa usually costs more (SAR 480–535 in most 2026 guides, though Visit Saudi has listed SAR 395 including insurance), but it is multiple-entry and valid for a year, so it can work out better if you plan to return. And if you are only connecting through the Kingdom on Saudia or flynas, the free 96-hour stopover visa beats both.
  • Is the Nusuk permit free? Yes. The Umrah permit booked in the Nusuk app is completely free — it is separate from your visa. Anyone charging you for the permit itself is charging for their time, not for a government fee.
  • Can I extend my stay? Plan to leave before your permitted stay ends — an Umrah visa must be entered within 30 days of issuance, and for the 1448 AH season every Umrah-visa pilgrim must be out of the Kingdom by 7 April 2027. Overstaying brings penalties, so build your return flight inside the dates and confirm the current rules on the official portal before you travel.

Madinah · Rawdah Permit GuideRawdah Permit — How to Book Your Rawdah Visit on Nusuk (Step by Step)

Inside the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah lies the Rawdah — the blessed area between the Prophet's ﷺ house and his pulpit. Entry is by permit only, the permit is free, and it is booked only through the official Nusuk app — since 31 October 2026 also on the Nusuk web portal at services.nusuk.sa. No agent can book it for you, and nobody should charge you for it. Here is the booking, step by step.

Why pilgrims long for the Rawdah: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise" — narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (1196) and Sahih Muslim (1391).

How to book — step by step:

  • Step 1 — Download the official Nusuk app and sign in with your passport and visa number, exactly as they appear on your documents. Our Nusuk App Guide covers registration in detail.
  • Step 2 — On the Home screen, open Rawdah, then Permits and Bookings.
  • Step 3 — Choose Men or Women. The two have separate visiting times, and a permit booked under the wrong category will not scan at the door.
  • Step 4 — Pick your date and time slot. Slots are grouped by prayer period — Midnight, Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha — and run about 20 minutes apart.
  • Step 5 — Confirm the booking and save the QR code — screenshot it. Mobile signal inside the mosque can be unreliable, and your screenshot opens the gate when the app cannot load.
  • Step 6 — Confirm your attendance in the app between 48 hours and 2 hours before the visit, then arrive 30 minutes early and join the queue for your slot.

When slots appear: Slots are usually released 7–14 days ahead — only 3–5 days ahead in Ramadan and Dhul-Hijjah — and they fill fast, so check the app daily once your Madinah dates are near. The general rule is one Rawdah permit every 365 days. Nusuk also offers an Instant Access option for eligible visitors who are near the Prophet's Mosque, subject to capacity on the day.

Visiting windows (published by the Saudi Press Agency on 20 October 2026): Men — 2:00 AM until Fajr, and 11:20 AM until Isha. Women — after Fajr until 11:00 AM, and after Isha until 2:00 AM. Windows can change with the season, so always follow the time shown in your Nusuk permit. While you are in the city, our Madinah Ziyarat Guide covers the other blessed places to visit.

Quick questions:

  • Is the Rawdah permit free? Yes — completely free. It is booked only in the official Nusuk app or on the Nusuk web portal (services.nusuk.sa); there is no fee, and no agent or website can issue it for you.
  • How often can I visit the Rawdah? The general rule is one permit every 365 days. If you are already in Madinah, the Instant Access option in Nusuk may allow an additional visit for eligible visitors near the Prophet's Mosque, subject to capacity.
  • What if no slots are available? Keep checking — new slots are released 7–14 days ahead (3–5 days in Ramadan and Dhul-Hijjah) and cancellations free up places. Check daily at different times, and try Instant Access when you are near the mosque.

Sources: Nusuk — Official Site ↗ · Sahih al-Bukhari 1196 — Sunnah.com ↗ · Sahih Muslim 1391 — Sunnah.com ↗

Umrah · Women TravellersWomen Travelling Alone for Umrah — Rules, Mahram, Visa & Safety Tips

It is now one of the questions sisters ask most: can a woman travel for Umrah on her own, without a mahram? For many years the answer, in visa terms, was no — a male guardian was a condition of the journey. That changed in 2022, and today thousands of women make the journey alone or in the company of other women. This guide separates the two things that are often mixed together: what the Saudi rules allow, and what the classical religious position says — so you can plan with clear eyes.

The rule today — no mahram required: In 2022, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah announced that women of any age may perform Umrah without a mahram. The mahram condition was removed: a woman can be issued an Umrah visa, book her permits and travel on her own or with a group of women. No mahram letter and no male guardian's permission is required for the visa.

The classical position, stated honestly: The Prophet ﷺ said: "A woman should not travel except with a mahram" — narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (1088) and Sahih Muslim (1339), where journeys of a day and a night are mentioned. Because of these hadith, many scholars have held that a woman should not travel without a mahram, while others have discussed travel in safe, trustworthy company. EasyNusuk does not issue fatwas. The visa rule tells you what the Kingdom permits; what your own situation requires is a religious question — please ask a trusted scholar who knows your circumstances before you decide.

Visa and permits — the steps:

  • Step 1 — Visa: Apply for an Umrah visa through an approved agent or platform, or use the tourist eVisa if your nationality is eligible — both allow Umrah. Our Umrah Visa 2026 guide explains the types, requirements and how to apply.
  • Step 2 — Nusuk app: Register in the Nusuk app with your passport and visa details, exactly as printed on your documents.
  • Step 3 — Permits: Book your Umrah permit and, in Madinah, your Rawdah permit — women have their own Rawdah visiting times, so choose the women's service in the app. Our Nusuk App Guide walks through every screen.
  • Step 4 — Save offline copies: Screenshot your visa, permits, hotel bookings and return ticket, so nothing depends on mobile signal.

Practical safety tips for travelling alone:

  • Stay near the Haram: Book a hotel a short, well-lit walk from Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and from the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, so you are never walking far, or late, on quiet streets.
  • Travel in company where you can: Join other sisters from your hotel or an organised group for Ziyarat trips and intercity travel; inside the two mosques, the women's sections are busy and supervised at all hours.
  • Keep documents and emergency numbers handy: Carry your hotel's address card, keep copies of your passport and visa on your phone, and save the numbers that matter — Saudi emergency 911, your hotel, your airline and your country's embassy or consulate.
  • Share your plan: Send your itinerary and hotel details to family at home before you fly, and check in with them each day.
  • Use official transport: Take licensed taxis or ride-hailing apps rather than unmarked cars, and keep your phone charged with a power bank in your handbag.

With the visa rule clear, your permits booked in the Nusuk app and these simple precautions in place, travelling alone for Umrah is a journey many women now complete safely and peacefully — may Allah accept it from every sister who undertakes it.

Quick questions:

  • Can a woman get an Umrah visa without a mahram? Yes. Since the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah's 2022 announcement, women of any age can be issued an Umrah visa and perform Umrah without a mahram — travelling alone or in a group of women.
  • Does the visa rule settle the religious question? No — it is a travel rule, not a fatwa. The hadith on travelling with a mahram (Sahih al-Bukhari 1088; Sahih Muslim 1339) lead scholars to different conclusions for different situations, so consult a trusted scholar about your own case.
  • Where should a woman travelling alone stay? As close to the mosques as your budget allows — around Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and the central Markaziyah area by the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah. Short walks on busy, well-lit streets make the biggest practical difference.

Sources: Nusuk — Official Site ↗ · Sahih al-Bukhari 1088 — Sunnah.com ↗ · Sahih Muslim 1339 — Sunnah.com ↗

Umrah · Packing ChecklistUmrah Packing List — What to Pack for Umrah (Complete Checklist)

Packing for Umrah is not like packing for a holiday. You will enter Ihram on the way, walk several kilometres a day between the Haram and your hotel, and spend long hours in worship — so your bag should carry what serves the journey and nothing that burdens it. This is the complete 2026 checklist for men and women: work through it group by group and you will arrive ready.

From the Qur'an: Allah says: "And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah (taqwa)" (Qur'an 2:197). Pack your bag with care — then remember that the provision which matters most on this journey is a heart full of taqwa.

1. Documents — always in your cabin bag:

  • Passport, valid for at least 6 months from your travel date
  • Visa printout — a printed copy of your visa, with the PDF saved on your phone as a backup. Check the cost and type before you apply with our Umrah Visa Fees 2026 guide
  • Flight and hotel booking confirmations for Makkah and Madinah
  • Travel insurance documents
  • Prescription medicines in their original packaging with a doctor's note — see the Health list below
  • Nusuk app installed and your account created before you fly, with permits booked or screenshotted — you will need it from day one
  • Vaccination proof where required — such as the meningitis ACWY certificate; check the current requirement for your country before you travel
  • Photocopies of everything, kept separately from the originals, plus copies saved on your phone

2. Ihram clothing:

  • Men: two unstitched white cloths — one to wear and one clean spare — plus a belt or pouch for your phone, cash and hotel key, because Ihram has no pockets. While in Ihram, men wear no stitched clothes. Pack one full set in your cabin bag: your flight may cross the Miqat before landing
  • Women: a loose abaya, hijab and a prayer dress — enough for the whole stay, in fabrics that wash and dry quickly — and comfortable modest clothing underneath
  • Unscented toiletries: while in Ihram, use no scented products — pack unscented soap, shampoo and deodorant, unscented wipes and an unscented lip balm, plus a toothbrush and miswak. Your normal scented items can be used before you enter Ihram and after you leave it — keep the two sets separate in your bag
  • Everyday clothes for your days in Makkah and Madinah, a light layer for air-conditioned spaces and cool evenings, sleepwear and enough undergarments

3. Footwear:

  • Comfortable sandals or slippers for the long walks between the Haram and your hotel — slip-on styles are easiest to take off and carry at the mosque doors
  • Socks — for cooler floors, evenings and the walks in between
  • Comfortable, well-worn-in walking shoes for Ziyarat days — never brand-new shoes
  • A small shoe bag, so your footwear stays with you inside the Haram

4. Prayer essentials:

  • A light prayer mat for travel and crowded times
  • A tasbih or counter for dhikr
  • A small dua book, and a pocket Qur'an or a Qur'an app on your phone
  • Your phone with the Nusuk app installed — your Umrah and Rawdah permits live in it. Book the Rawdah slot with our Rawdah Permit guide, and set the app up with our Nusuk App Guide

5. Health:

  • Your regular medicines, in their original packaging with a doctor's note, kept in your cabin bag
  • Painkillers
  • Oral rehydration salts — the walking, heat and crowds test every pilgrim
  • Sunscreen
  • Unscented moisturiser and lip balm — unscented, so they stay within the Ihram rules above
  • Plasters and blister plasters, and throat lozenges, are worth the small space they take

6. Money and tech:

  • Some Saudi riyals in cash for taxis, food and small purchases, plus your bank cards. Split your money between your cabin bag, your checked bag and a money belt — never keep it all in one place — and tell your bank you are travelling so your card is not blocked
  • Phone charger and a power bank — power banks travel in the cabin bag only, never in checked luggage
  • A travel adapter: Saudi sockets are Type G, 220V, like the UK — pack a Type G adapter if your plugs are different

7. Day bag:

  • A small backpack for Haram visits — light enough to carry through long hours of worship
  • A laundry bag for worn clothes
  • Zip-lock bags — for toiletries, snacks and keeping small items dry and together
  • A water bottle — you can refill it with Zamzam inside the Haram. Pack dates, nuts and biscuits alongside it for travel days and long waits

8. Zamzam on the way home: Each passenger may take one factory-sealed 5-litre Zamzam box, bought at the official counters at Jeddah or Madinah airports for about SAR 12.50. It travels always as checked baggage — never in the cabin and never packed inside a suitcase. Saudia gives a complimentary sealed pack from Madinah; from Jeddah it flies free but counts inside your checked allowance. Rules vary by airline, so confirm with your own airline before flying.

Before you close the suitcase: two jobs remain. Choose your dates with our Best Time to Perform Umrah guide, and make sure your visa is right with the Umrah Visa 2026 guide.

Quick questions:

  • Can I use scented toiletries during Umrah? Before you enter Ihram and after you leave it, yes. While you are in Ihram, use only unscented products — no scented products are permitted in Ihram.
  • What does a man wear for Ihram? Two unstitched white cloths, with a belt or pouch for essentials — and no stitched clothes while in Ihram. Pack two sets: one to wear and one clean spare.
  • Can I take Zamzam home in my suitcase or cabin bag? No — never inside a suitcase and never in the cabin. One factory-sealed 5-litre box per passenger, bought at the official airport counters for about SAR 12.50, travels as checked baggage only; confirm your own airline's rule before you fly.

Sources: Nusuk — Official Site ↗ · Visit Saudi — Official Visa Guidance ↗

Nusuk App · Complete GuideNusuk App Guide — How to Use the Nusuk App (Umrah & Rawdah Permits, Competition Codes)

The Nusuk app is the official app of Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. It is the one app almost every pilgrim now needs: through it you book Umrah permits, Rawdah (Riyadh al-Jannah) permits for the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, Hajj services and permits to visit the holy places. The official Nusuk site reports more than 26 million app downloads, over 130 services, more than 17 million Umrah permits and more than 13 million Rawdah permits issued through the platform. Behind every booking is a simple intention — Allah says: "And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah" (Qur'an 2:196).

Please note: EasyNusuk is an independent community website. It is not the official Nusuk site, it is not the Nusuk app, and it is not affiliated with the app or with the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. Permits are issued only inside the official Nusuk app and through the official Nusuk websites linked at the end of this guide.

Getting started:

  • Step 1 — Download the official app. Search for "Nusuk" in the App Store (iPhone) or Google Play (Android), or follow the download links on the official site, nusuk.sa. Check that the publisher is the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah — beware of imitation apps with a similar name or logo.
  • Step 2 — Create your account. Register with your own details and complete the verification steps the app asks for.
  • Step 3 — Keep your documents ready. Have your passport and your visa details (Umrah visa or tourist visa) at hand — you will need the numbers exactly as printed when you complete your profile and book permits.

Booking an Umrah permit — step by step:

  • Step 1 — Open the Nusuk app and sign in to your account.
  • Step 2 — Choose the Umrah permit service on the home screen.
  • Step 3 — Select the visitors — yourself, and any companions linked to your account.
  • Step 4 — Pick an available date and time slot and confirm the booking.
  • Step 5 — Your permit appears in the app, with its details and QR code. Show it whenever it is asked for at the Grand Mosque.

Permit rules — how far ahead slots open, and how often a permit can be booked — change from time to time. Always check the app itself for the current slot rules before planning around them.

Booking a Rawdah permit — step by step:

  • Step 1 — In the app, open Prophet's Mosque Services.
  • Step 2 — Tap "Praying in the Noble Rawdah". Men and women have separate services and separate visiting times — choose the correct one, because a permit booked under the wrong category will not be accepted at the gate.
  • Step 3 — Select the visitors, then pick an available date and time.
  • Step 4 — Confirm and issue the permit — it appears in the app straight away.
  • Step 5 — On the day: go to the gate shown on your permit and arrive on time. Your permit is checked at the gate before you enter the Rawdah.

Using Nusuk Free Umrah Competition codes in the app:

  • Step 1 — Open the Nusuk app and tap "Start the challenge".
  • Step 2 — Open the Keys tab.
  • Step 3 — Paste an NG- code — for example one of the free community codes listed on this site — into the "Add code to get new key" box.
  • Step 4 — Tap "Check the code", and the key is added to your account.

How keys work: you receive one free key every day. You earn one extra key each time you use someone else's code, and one extra key each time someone uses your code — but each pair of people can swap codes only once. Every key lets you answer one competition question, and a correct answer enters you into that day's draw for a free Umrah trip.

Practical tips:

  • Use a stable internet connection when booking — a slow connection can lose a slot while the page loads.
  • Screenshot every permit as soon as it is issued; the mobile signal around the mosques can be weak when you need to show it.
  • Book the Rawdah early — Rawdah slots fill very fast, so start checking the app as soon as your dates open.
  • Keep app notifications on, so you do not miss slot openings, waitlist updates or changes to your permits.
  • Keep the app updated to the latest version, and make sure the name and passport number on your permit match your documents exactly.

Quick questions:

  • Is the Nusuk app free? Yes — downloading the app and booking Umrah and Rawdah permits in it is free. Never pay anyone for a permit.
  • Is EasyNusuk the official Nusuk website? No. EasyNusuk is an independent community site that shares guides and community competition codes. The official app and websites belong to the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.
  • Can I perform Umrah or enter the Rawdah without a permit? No — book your permit in the app first, arrive at your booked time, and show the permit at the gate when it is checked.

Sources: Nusuk — Official Site ↗ · Nusuk Services Portal ↗

Umrah · Women's GuideUmrah for Women — Complete Guide

Umrah is a journey of a lifetime for a woman just as it is for a man, and most of its rites are exactly the same. Allah says: "And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah" (Qur'an 2:196). But there are a few rules that apply to women only — in Ihram, in Tawaf and Sa'i, and when the monthly period comes. This guide brings them together in one place.

Ihram for women: A woman enters Ihram in her normal, modest clothes — the abaya and hijab she usually wears. There is no special Ihram garment for women, and ordinary stitched clothing is allowed for her. Two things are forbidden for her in Ihram: the niqab (face veil) and gloves.

From the Sunnah: the Prophet ﷺ said: "A woman in Ihram should not wear a niqab, nor wear gloves" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1838). When non-mahram men pass by, she may lower her headscarf over her face to cover it — this is what the wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to do.

Travelling without a mahram: Saudi Arabia changed the rule in 2022: a woman aged 18 or over may now perform Umrah without a mahram. A girl under 18 still travels with a mahram or guardian. At every age, the Umrah visa and Umrah permit are booked through the Nusuk app, the same as for every other pilgrim.

How a woman's rites differ from a man's:

  • No Ramal — the brisk walk men do in the first three circuits of Tawaf. A woman walks at a normal pace in all seven circuits.
  • No Idtiba — baring the right shoulder is for men only; a woman's shoulder stays covered.
  • A normal pace in Sa'i too — between the two green lights men walk briskly; women walk normally throughout Sa'i.
  • The Talbiyah in a low voice — a woman recites "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk..." quietly, loud enough for herself to hear.
  • Ending Ihram: trim, do not shave — after Sa'i, a woman trims about a fingertip's length (1–2 cm) from the ends of her hair. With this, her Ihram ends and her Umrah is complete.

Menstruation during Umrah: A woman cannot perform Tawaf while menstruating. She waits in Makkah until she is pure, performs ghusl, and only then does her Tawaf. She may still enter Ihram at the Miqat while menstruating, and her Ihram stays valid while she waits — there is no need to panic or to cut the trip short.

From the Sunnah: when Aisha (RA) menstruated during the journey, the Prophet ﷺ told her: "Do everything that the pilgrims do, but do not circumambulate the House until you become pure" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1650; Sahih Muslim 1211).

Sa'i is different: Sa'i does not require wudu. So if a woman's period begins after she has completed her Tawaf, she may carry on with Sa'i, then trim her hair and finish her Umrah.

Visiting the Rawdah in Madinah: Women have their own separate visiting times at the Rawdah in the Prophet's Mosque — usually in the morning after Fajr and again at night after Isha. Entry is by permit only: book "Praying in the Noble Rawdah" and choose the women's service in the Nusuk app, then arrive at the gate shown on your permit 20–30 minutes early.

Practical tips:

  • Use the women's prayer areas — both Harams have large, clearly marked sections for women; in Makkah there are women's areas close to the Mataf, and mosque staff will guide you to them.
  • Pack for the journey: comfortable, well-worn-in shoes for the long walks; a spare abaya and extra hijabs; and unscented toiletries — no perfume, scented soap or scented wipes while in Ihram.
  • Travel in a group if you can — a family group or a women's group makes the journey easier and more relaxed, especially on a first Umrah.
  • Choose a hotel near the Haram — a short walk saves your energy for worship, above all when returning for Fajr.
  • Wheelchair assistance is available — wheelchairs can be arranged in both Harams for Tawaf and Sa'i if you need one; ask the staff at the mosque entrances.

Quick questions:

  • Can a woman perform Umrah without a mahram? Yes. Since 2022, Saudi rules allow women aged 18 and over to perform Umrah without a mahram; under 18, she travels with a mahram or guardian.
  • What if my period starts before Tawaf? Wait until you are pure, perform ghusl, and then do Tawaf. Your Ihram remains valid while you wait.
  • How does a woman come out of Ihram? By trimming about a fingertip's length (1–2 cm) from the ends of her hair after Sa'i — she does not shave her head.

Sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1838 — Hadith Unlocked ↗ · Can She Perform Umrah During Menses? — IslamQA ↗ · Umrah Without a Mahram — Wego Blog ↗ · Masjid an-Nabawi Guide — Divine Dua ↗

Umrah · Sa'i GuideSa'i Step by Step: Walking Between Safa and Marwa

Sa'i is the third rite of Umrah, performed after Tawaf. It means walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa, inside Masjid al-Haram in Makkah. In doing so, you follow in the footsteps of Hajar (may Allah be pleased with her), who searched between these two hills for water for her infant son Isma'il. Allah says: "Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah" (Qur'an 2:158).

The story of Hajar: The Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) left Hajar and her baby Isma'il in the barren valley of Makkah, by Allah's command. When their water ran out and the baby cried with thirst, Hajar climbed the hill of Safa looking for help, then ran to Marwa, and went back and forth seven times between the two hills. Then Allah caused the spring of Zamzam to flow for them — the same blessed water pilgrims drink today.

From the Sunnah: the full story of Hajar, Isma'il and the spring of Zamzam is narrated by Ibn Abbas (RA) and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari 3364.

Conditions of a valid Sa'i:

  • It must come after a valid Tawaf
  • It must start at Safa and finish at Marwa
  • It must be exactly seven laps — one way counts as one lap
LapWalk
1Safa → Marwa
2Marwa → Safa
3Safa → Marwa
4Marwa → Safa
5Safa → Marwa
6Marwa → Safa
7Safa → Marwa

Sa'i step by step:

  • Step 1 — Go to Safa. After the two rak'ahs of Tawaf and drinking Zamzam, go to Safa. As you approach it, recite: "Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'aa'irillah" — "Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah" (Qur'an 2:158).
  • Step 2 — Climb Safa and face the Kaaba. Climb Safa until you can see the Kaaba. Face it, raise your hands, and say the takbir and tahlil that the Prophet ﷺ said there: "Allahu Akbar. La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu, yuhyi wa yumit, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir" — say it three times, making your own personal du'a between each time.
  • Step 3 — Walk towards Marwa. Walk at a normal pace. Between the two green lights (Milayn al-Akhdharayn), men walk briskly or jog lightly; women walk normally throughout the whole Sa'i.
  • Step 4 — At Marwa, repeat the dhikr. Face the Qibla and repeat the same takbir, tahlil and du'a that you made at Safa. That completes lap 1.
  • Step 5 — Walk back to Safa. The return walk is lap 2. Continue in the same way — dhikr and du'a at each hill — until you complete seven laps, ending at Marwa.
  • Step 6 — Fill the walk with du'a. There is no fixed du'a for the walk itself — use the time for dhikr, Qur'an and personal du'a in any language. A beautiful du'a to repeat is: "Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah, wa fil-akhirati hasanah, wa qina adhaba n-nar" — "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and shield us from the punishment of the Fire" (Qur'an 2:201).
  • Step 7 — Cut the hair. After Sa'i, men shave the head (Halq) — which is more rewarding — or trim the hair (Taqsir), and women trim about a fingertip's length from the ends of their hair. With this, Ihram ends and your Umrah is complete.
From the Sunnah: the description of the Prophet's ﷺ Sa'i — the dhikr on Safa and Marwa, said three times with du'a in between — comes from the long report of Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) about the Farewell Hajj, recorded in Sahih Muslim 1218.

Practical tips:

  • The Mas'a corridor is about 450 metres one way, so seven laps are about 3.15 km and take roughly 40–60 minutes
  • The corridor is air-conditioned, has several floors and wheelchair lanes
  • Wudu is recommended but not required for Sa'i — Sa'i is valid without it
  • Women in menses may perform Sa'i (unlike Tawaf, which waits until purity)
  • You may pause and rest if you are tired — then continue from where you stopped
  • Keep to the right and do not stop in the middle of the walkway, so the flow keeps moving
  • Drink Zamzam afterwards and make du'a

Common mistakes:

  • Starting at Marwa — a lap that starts at Marwa does not count; Sa'i must begin at Safa
  • Counting a round trip as one lap — each one-way walk is a full lap
  • Men jogging outside the green-light stretch — the brisk walk is only between the two green markers
  • Women jogging — women walk at a normal pace everywhere in Sa'i
  • Rushing through without du'a — this walk is a time of remembrance; slow down and use it

Quick questions:

  • Do I need wudu for Sa'i? No. Wudu is recommended, but Sa'i is valid without it.
  • Can I do Sa'i on the upper floors? Yes. The Mas'a has several floors, and Sa'i on any of them is valid — the upper floors are often quieter.
  • What if I lose count of the laps? Take the lower number you are sure of and complete the rest from there.

Sources: Sa'i Guide — Halal Muslim Travel ↗ · Sa'i — Mahajja ↗ · Sa'i Between Safa and Marwa Explained — Muslim Flow ↗ · Safa and Marwa — Hajj Umrah Planner ↗

Umrah · Tawaf GuideTawaf Step by Step: How to Circle the Kaaba

Tawaf is walking seven complete circuits around the Kaaba, counter-clockwise, keeping the Kaaba on your left. Every circuit starts and ends at the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad). Tawaf is a pillar of Umrah — the Umrah is not complete without it — and it is also performed in Hajj and as a voluntary act of worship.

Before you start:

  • Be in a state of wudu
  • Make your intention (niyyah) for the Tawaf
  • Men performing a Tawaf that will be followed by Sa'i uncover the right shoulder (Idtiba) — this is the Sunnah for this Tawaf only

Step by step:

  • Step 1 — Start at the Black Stone. Stand level with the Black Stone — the line is marked by the green light on the wall. If you can reach it without pushing anyone, touch it or kiss it; otherwise raise your right hand towards it (Istilam) and say "Bismillah, Allahu Akbar". Never push or shove — harming another worshipper is never part of the Sunnah.
  • Step 2 — Walk counter-clockwise. Men walk briskly with short steps (Ramal) in the first three circuits only, then walk normally for the last four. Women walk normally throughout.
  • Step 3 — Make dua as you walk. There is no fixed dua for each circuit — make personal dua and dhikr in any language. Between the Yemeni Corner (Rukn Yamani) and the Black Stone, recite: "Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina adhaba n-nar" — "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and shield us from the punishment of the Fire" (Qur'an 2:201). Touch the Yemeni Corner with your right hand if you can reach it — without kissing it and without saying takbir.
  • Step 4 — Count carefully. Tawaf is exactly seven circuits. If you lose count, take the lower number and continue from there. A tasbih, your fingers or a phone counter all help.
  • Step 5 — After the seventh circuit. Cover the right shoulder again, then pray two rak'ahs of Tawaf at Maqam Ibrahim if you can — anywhere in the mosque is valid if it is crowded. The Sunnah is to recite Surah al-Kafirun in the first rak'ah and Surah al-Ikhlas in the second. Make dua at the Multazam if you can reach it calmly, then drink Zamzam water. If this Tawaf is followed by Sa'i, go on to Safa.

The main types of Tawaf: Tawaf al-Umrah — the Tawaf performed as part of Umrah; Tawaf al-Qudum — the arrival Tawaf when you reach Makkah for Hajj; and Tawaf al-Wada — the farewell Tawaf performed before leaving Makkah.

From the Sunnah: the longest description of the Prophet's ﷺ Hajj — including his Tawaf, the Ramal in the first three circuits and the two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim — was narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) and is recorded in Sahih Muslim 1218.

Sources: Tawaf Guide — Halal Muslim Travel ↗ · How to Perform Tawaf — Guide to Hajj ↗ · How to Perform Tawaf — The Umrah Bundle ↗ · Tawaf al-Qudum — Mahajja ↗

Madinah · Rawdah Permit GuideHow to Get a Rawdah Permit on the Nusuk App: Step by Step (2026)

The Rawdah, also called Al-Rawdah Al-Sharifah, is a very blessed place inside Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah. It is the area between the house of the Prophet ﷺ and his minbar (pulpit).

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Between my house and my minbar is one of the gardens of Paradise" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1196; Sahih Muslim 1391). This is why Muslims from all over the world wish to pray there.

A permit is mandatory in 2026. You cannot walk in without a Nusuk permit — walk-in entry without a permit is not allowed. The good news is that the permit is completely free. Do not pay anyone for it.

Book before you travel to Madinah, not after you arrive. Slots are limited and they fill very fast. If you wait until you reach Madinah, you may find no slots left for the days of your stay.

How to book — step by step:

  • Step 1 — Download the official Nusuk app. Get it from the App Store or Google Play. Check that the publisher is the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah — beware of imitation apps with a similar name or logo.
  • Step 2 — Register and complete your profile. Sign in or register with your passport number and your Umrah or tourist visa number. Complete your profile first, before you try to book.
  • Step 3 — Open Prophet's Mosque Services. On the home screen, go to Prophet's Mosque Services (shown in some versions as Holy Mosque Services).
  • Step 4 — Choose the Rawdah service. Tap "Praying in the Noble Rawdah" (also shown as "Book Rawdah Visit"). Men and women have separate services and separate time slots — choose the correct gender category carefully. A permit booked under the wrong category will not scan at the gate.
  • Step 5 — Select the visitors. Tick your own name. If you are booking for family members or companions, add them too — they must be linked to your account.
  • Step 6 — Pick a date and time. Choose a green available date and time slot. Grey or full slots cannot be booked.
  • Step 7 — Confirm and issue the permit. Confirm your booking, accept the terms, and tap Issue Permit. Your permit with a QR code appears instantly. Take a screenshot and save it — mobile signal in the mosque courtyard can be weak, and you will need to show the QR code at the gate.
  • Step 8 — Arrive early on the day. Go to the gate shown on your permit and arrive 20–30 minutes early. Staff will scan your QR code before you enter.

Important things to know:

  • Slots are normally released 7–14 days in advance. In peak seasons like Ramadan, they may open only 3–5 days ahead.
  • Slots fill within minutes. Start checking the app daily from 10 days before your visit and refresh often.
  • The full visit lasts about 30–45 minutes and the time is strictly enforced. Your time inside the Rawdah itself is short — around 10 minutes — so prepare your duas in advance.
  • The general rule is one Rawdah permit per person every 365 days — in simple words, one visit per year per person.
  • The app also offers Instant Track: when you are near the mosque, you can request an immediate slot every 20 minutes, subject to capacity.
  • The app also has a Waitlist — join it and you will be notified when a slot frees up.
  • Since 31 October 2026, the permit can also be issued on the Nusuk web portal at services.nusuk.sa — look for "Issue a Rawdah prayer permit".

What to do inside the Rawdah:

Once you are inside, stay calm and do not push anyone. Pray 2 rak'at, make sincere dua for yourself, your family and the whole Ummah, and send salawat (peace and blessings) upon the Prophet ﷺ. Keep your worship brief and focused so that other pilgrims waiting outside also get their turn.

Frequently asked questions:

  • Is the Rawdah permit free? Yes. The Rawdah permit is completely free in the official Nusuk app.
  • Can I visit the Rawdah without a permit? No. In 2026 a Nusuk permit is required — walk-in entry without a permit is not allowed.
  • How early should I book? As soon as slots open — normally 7–14 days ahead. Check the app daily starting 10 days before your visit.

Sources: Rawdah Permit on Nusuk — New Hajj ↗ · Nusuk Guide — HalalBooking ↗ · Nusuk App Guide — Wego Blog ↗ · Important Places Inside Masjid-e-Nabvi — Saudi Scoop ↗ · How to Book Rawdah Permits on Nusuk — Guide to Hajj ↗

Umrah · Packing GuideWhat to Pack for Umrah — Complete Packing List

Packing for Umrah is different from packing for an ordinary trip. You are dressing for worship as well as travel, walking long distances in heat, and entering Ihram on the way. This short list covers what you actually need — and what to leave behind — so you can focus on worship, not luggage.

1. Documents — in hand luggage, never in checked bags. If your suitcase is delayed, you still need to be able to travel and check in. Keep everything in one zipped pouch in your carry-on:

  • Passport valid for 6+ months from your travel date
  • Umrah visa — printed copy plus the PDF saved on your phone
  • Nusuk permit — saved as a screenshot in case the signal is weak
  • Flight tickets and hotel confirmations for Makkah and Madinah
  • Meningitis ACWY vaccination certificate — the vaccine must be taken at least 10 days before travel
  • Photocopies of everything, kept separately from the originals, plus digital copies on your phone

2. Men — Ihram essentials. Pack 2 Ihram sets in soft cotton or towel fabric — one will get sweaty or dusty, and a clean change is genuinely useful. Add an Ihram belt with pockets (Ihram has no pockets, yet you will be carrying your phone, cash and hotel key), and open sandals that leave the ankles uncovered. For toiletries, pack unscented soap, shampoo and deodorant — no perfume or scented products once you are in Ihram. Pack one full Ihram set in your hand luggage: if you are flying towards Jeddah, you may need to be in Ihram before the plane passes the miqat, and your suitcase will be in the hold.

3. Women — modest, breathable clothing. Women do not wear a special Ihram garment — normal modest clothing is worn. Pack 3–4 loose, breathable abayas and 4–5 hijabs in lightweight cotton or jersey that are easy to wash and manage through long days. While in Ihram, do not wear a niqab (face veil) or gloves.

4. Health — medicines done properly. Carry your regular medicines in their original packaging, in hand luggage, with prescriptions and a doctor's letter in case you are asked about them. Add basic pain relief and stomach medicine for headaches, fever and an upset stomach. If you take controlled drugs, you need an SFDA (Saudi Food and Drug Authority) permit arranged in advance through its traveller's permit system — do not leave this to the airport.

5. Money — riyals, a card, and split it up. Carry some Saudi riyals in cash plus at least one bank card, and split your money between bags — some in your hand luggage, some in a money belt — rather than keeping it all in one place. Travelling from Pakistan? The State Bank of Pakistan limit is US$5,000 in cash per visit for adults, so plan larger payments by card.

6. Electronics. Saudi Arabia uses Type G plugs at 220–230V — the same three-pin type as the UK and Pakistan — so pack a Type G adapter if your plugs differ. Bring a power bank (in hand luggage only) and your phone with the Nusuk app installed and set up before you fly — you will need it for permits from day one.

7. Day bag and Zamzam. Take a small day bag or crossbody bag for the Haram — for your phone, water bottle, shoe bag and any medication, leaving your hands free during Tawaf and Sa'i. On the way home, you are allowed one sealed 5L Zamzam bottle on the return flight, bought at the departure airport — never pack loose Zamzam bottles inside your suitcase.

8. What NOT to pack. Leave behind scented toiletries for your Ihram days (perfume, fragranced soap, shampoo and deodorant are not permitted in Ihram), valuables you do not need such as jewellery — one less thing to worry about losing in the crowds — and excess luggage. Makkah and Madinah have pharmacies and shops on every corner; pack light and leave room for what you buy there.

The carry-on rule: If you would need it in the first 24 hours, it goes in the carry-on — documents, medicines, one full Ihram set, sandals, chargers and one change of clothes. Everything else can go in the checked bag.

Sources: Ultimate Hajj & Umrah Packing Checklist — Travel in Makkah ↗ · Umrah Packing List for Pakistani Pilgrims — Sky Raah ↗ · Complete Packing Guide for Your Umrah Journey from America — Hisar Tour ↗ · Umrah Packing Checklist — Hajj Umrah Taxi ↗ · Complete Umrah Packing List Guide — Bank Jago ↗

Umrah Visa · Travel GuideUmrah Visa 2026: Types, Requirements and How to Apply

There is more than one way to get a visa that allows Umrah in 2026. Which route applies to you depends on your nationality and the visas you already hold. This guide explains each type, what documents you need, and the health and permit rules that apply to every pilgrim.

1. Tourist eVisa. Citizens of 60+ eligible countries — including the US, UK, EU countries, Canada, Australia and Japan — can apply online at visa.visitsaudi.com. The government fee is around SAR 300 plus mandatory medical insurance. The eVisa is valid for 1 year, multiple entry, with up to 90 days per stay. It allows Umrah outside Hajj season, but it does NOT allow Hajj.

2. Dedicated Umrah visa. For nationalities that are not eVisa-eligible — including Pakistan, India and Bangladesh — the Umrah visa is arranged through a licensed Umrah agent or the Nusuk Umrah platform. It is single entry and typically valid for 30 days. Since June 2025, accommodation must be registered on the Nusuk Masar system through a licensed hotel.

3. Visa on arrival. Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen visa can obtain a visa on arrival in Saudi Arabia, which can be used to perform Umrah.

4. Other valid Saudi visas. Holders of any valid Saudi visa — including work, family visit, business and transit visas — can also perform Umrah.

Required documents:

  • Passport valid for 6+ months
  • Recent photograph
  • Confirmed accommodation
  • Return ticket
  • Medical insurance

Vaccination. Meningitis (ACWY) vaccination is mandatory — it must be taken at least 10 days before travel, and you must carry an International Certificate of Vaccination as proof.

Women travelling without a mahram. Women aged 18+ can travel for Umrah without a mahram.

Visa is not the permit. The Umrah permit is separate from the visa and is booked free in the Nusuk app — you need both before you enter Masjid al-Haram for Umrah.

Hajj season cut-off. Umrah visa issuance stops weeks before Hajj season each year, so apply well in advance if you plan to travel close to Hajj.

Please note: Fees and rules can change. Always confirm the latest fees, eligibility and requirements on the official portals before applying.

Sources: Nusuk — Official Platform (nusuk.sa) ↗ · Saudi eVisa — visa.visitsaudi.com ↗ · Umrah Visa — How to Saudi Arabia ↗ · Saudi Umrah Visa Guide — House of Saud ↗ · Umrah Visa Guide — Saudi Utility Hub ↗

Nusuk App · Competition GuideHow to Use the Nusuk App to Enter the Free Umrah Competition — Step by Step

What is the Nusuk app? Nusuk is the official app for Umrah and visits to the holy cities, from the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. Pilgrims use it for Umrah permits, Rawdah bookings and other visit services. The free Umrah competition also runs inside this same official app.

How competition keys work. You get one free key every day. You can earn more keys with codes: each time you use someone else's NG- code, both of you get a key — you get one, and the person who shared the code gets one too. One simple rule to remember: each pair of people can only swap once, so you cannot use the same person's code again and again.

How to enter a code — step by step:

  • Step 1: Open the official Nusuk app on your phone.
  • Step 2: Tap Start the challenge.
  • Step 3: Open the Keys tab.
  • Step 4: Paste the NG- code in the “Add code to get new key” box.
  • Step 5: Tap Check the code.
  • Step 6: Stay on the Congratulations page — this confirms your new key has been added.

Tip: Codes are case-sensitive. Type or paste the code exactly as it is shown, with the same capital and small letters — for example, NG-7mpjM6vp is not the same as ng-7mpjm6vp.

What does a key do? One key lets you answer one question in the challenge. If your answer is correct, you are entered into that day's draw for a free Umrah trip. More keys simply mean more questions you can answer, and more chances in the daily draws.

Prizes. As announced for the competition, the prizes are 100 Umrah trips and 10,000 Zamzam cartons, with daily winners announced from 1 November 2026. Always check the latest prize and winner details inside the official app, as Nusuk itself makes the announcements.

If a code does not work, do not worry — just try the next code from the list. A code may already have been used, it may have expired, or you and that person may already have swapped once, and each pair can only swap once.

Stay safe: The competition runs only inside the official Nusuk app. EasyNusuk only shares community codes to copy and paste — we never ask for your Nusuk login, password or OTP. If any website or person asks for those, do not share them.

Umrah · Official Nusuk JourneyUmrah in Four Rites: What the Official Nusuk Journey Teaches

The official Nusuk Umrah Journey of the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah describes Umrah as four essential rites, in this order: Ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, and shaving or trimming the hair. Allah says: "And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah…" (Qur'an 2:196).

  • Ihram begins with a sincere intention and the Talbiyah, at or before the Meeqat — the journey starts in the heart before it starts on the road.
  • Tawaf: enter the Mataf, stand in line with the Black Stone on your left, raise the hand and say "Allahu Akbar", and circle the Kaaba seven times anti-clockwise, filling the rounds with dua and dhikr.
  • Sa'i: following the signs inside Masjid al-Haram to Safa, walk between Safa and Marwah seven lengths, beginning at Safa.
  • Hair: shaving or trimming completes the Umrah — what Ihram had restricted becomes permitted again.

See the Guides page for the full step-by-step method, with duas at every step.

Qur'an 2:196 · Umrah Journey ↗

Zamzam · HadithZamzam: The Blessed Water — Its Story and Its Virtue

Zamzam sprang up by Allah's command for Hajrah (AS) and her infant son Ismail (AS) in the empty valley of Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on the mother of Ismail. Had she left Zamzam alone, it would have been a flowing spring" (Sahih al-Bukhari 3364).

Authentic narrations: Abu Dharr (RA) lived for thirty days and nights in Makkah with no food except Zamzam; the Prophet ﷺ said of it: "It is blessed; it is food that nourishes" — and in one narration, "and a cure for sickness" (Sahih Muslim 2473). And he ﷺ said: "The water of Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for" (Sunan Ibn Majah 3062) — so drink it with a sincere intention and dua.
  • Drink facing the Qibla, saying Bismillah, in three breaths, until you are full
  • The dua taught at Zamzam: "O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision and healing from every illness"
  • Benefit is from Allah alone — Zamzam is a blessed means, not a substitute for medicine

Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 · Sahih Muslim 2473 · Sunan Ibn Majah 3062 · Merits of Zamzam Water ↗

Madinah · HadithThe Rawdah: A Garden from the Gardens of Paradise

Inside Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah, between the Prophet's ﷺ chamber and his minbar, lies the Rawdah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The area between my house and my minbar is one of the gardens of Paradise, and my minbar is on my Cistern (Hawd)" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1196; Sahih Muslim 1391).

Prayer anywhere in Masjid an-Nabawi carries its own immense reward: "One prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except Masjid al-Haram" (Bukhari & Muslim). Salamah ibn al-Akwa' (RA) used to seek out prayer in the Rawdah because he had seen the Prophet ﷺ keen to pray there (Bukhari 502; Muslim 509).

  • Book your Rawdah slot in the official Nusuk app — slots fill within minutes
  • Inside: pray 2 rakat calmly, send salutations, and make dua — without pushing or troubling anyone; eagerness for the Rawdah never justifies harming another worshipper
  • Afterwards, present your salam at the Sacred Chamber, then greet Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA)

Sahih al-Bukhari 1196, 502 · Sahih Muslim 1391, 509 · Ar-Rawdah an-Nabawiyah ↗

Madinah · Hadith & Qur'anMasjid Quba: Two Rakat with the Reward of an Umrah

Masjid Quba, on the southern edge of Madinah, is the first mosque built in Islam — founded when the Prophet ﷺ arrived during the Hijrah. Allah praises it in the Qur'an as "a mosque founded on righteousness from the first day" (Qur'an 9:108).

The promise: "Whoever purifies himself in his house, then comes to the Quba Mosque and offers one prayer in it, will have a reward like that of an Umrah" (Sunan Ibn Majah 1412; also Jami' at-Tirmidhi 324). Ibn Umar (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to go to Quba every Saturday, walking or riding, and pray two rakat there (Sahih al-Bukhari 1193–1194; Sahih Muslim 1399).
  • Do wudu where you are staying, before you set out — the wudu at home is part of the narration's wording
  • Pray two rakat (or any prayer) inside Masjid Quba
  • Many pilgrims walk the pleasant Quba pedestrian route from Masjid an-Nabawi (about 3.5 km)

Qur'an 9:108 · Sunan Ibn Majah 1412 · Jami' at-Tirmidhi 324 · Sahih al-Bukhari 1193 · Sahih Muslim 1399 · Masjid Quba — First Mosque & Umrah Reward ↗

Ihram · Qur'an & HadithIhram Explained: What Becomes Forbidden, and Why

Ihram is not just clothing — it is a sacred state entered with intention. Allah commands regarding Hajj: "…let there be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor wrangling in the Hajj" (Qur'an 2:197). Whoever performs Hajj avoiding these returns "as pure as the day his mother bore him" (Bukhari & Muslim).

  • Clothing (men): no sewn garments — no shirt, trousers, turban or hooded cloak, and no cloth touched by saffron or wars perfume; if sandals are unavailable, leather socks may be worn cut below the ankles (hadith of Ibn Umar, Bukhari & Muslim)
  • Women: normal clothing is worn, but no face veil (niqab) tied over the face and no gloves in Ihram
  • Perfume: none on body or clothes after entering Ihram — for men and women
  • Also forbidden: cutting hair or nails, hunting land game, marital relations and whatever leads to them, arguing and sinful speech
  • Forgotten mistakes: scholars note that what is done forgetfully or in ignorance is treated more leniently — ask a scholar about your specific case rather than worrying alone

Qur'an 2:197 · Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Ibn Umar, on Ihram clothing) · Restrictions of Ihram ↗

Hajj · Day by DayThe Days of Hajj, 8–13 Zul-Hijjah — and the Reward of Hajj Mabroor

The Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah orders the Hajj journey as: Mina on the Day of Tarwiyah (8th), then Arafat (9th), Muzdalifah (night), Jamrat al-Aqabah, the sacrifice, Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i (10th), the nights of Tashreeq in Mina (11th–13th), and finally Tawaf al-Wida. The pillars of Hajj are Ihram, the standing at Arafat, Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i.

The heart of it: the Prophet ﷺ said "Hajj is Arafat" (Tirmidhi) — the standing at Arafat on 9 Zul-Hijjah is the rite that cannot be missed. And he ﷺ said: "Umrah to the next Umrah is an expiation for what is between them, and the reward of Hajj Mabroor (an accepted Hajj) is nothing but Paradise" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1773; Sahih Muslim 1349). Scholars explain Mabroor as a Hajj performed correctly, sincerely, free of sin and showing-off.
  • 10th: 7 pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah only, then sacrifice, then Halq/Taqsir, then Tawaf-uz-Ziyarat
  • 11th–12th: all three Jamarat, 7 pebbles each, after midday; leaving Mina before sunset on the 12th is permitted, otherwise stay for the 13th
  • Full step-by-step method is on our Guides page

Sahih al-Bukhari 1773 · Sahih Muslim 1349 · Tirmidhi · Hajj Rites Day by Day ↗

Umrah Visa - 2026 RulesUmrah Visa 2026 Transport Rule - What Changed in January

If you are planning Umrah this year, the umrah visa 2026 transport rule is the change most likely to catch you out. Since January 2026, the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah requires every Umrah visa applicant to arrange accommodation and transport before the visa application is submitted, not after the visa arrives. Hotels and transport are no longer the last step of planning a trip. They are now part of the application itself, and an application that skips them cannot move forward.

What you must book first: Accommodation must be pre-booked through Nusuk-approved hotels, and transport must be pre-booked through licensed Nusuk-compliant providers. The transport booking has to cover the whole journey on the ground: your arrival from the airport, the Makkah to Madinah leg, and your departure. The system checks for valid confirmations for these bookings and blocks progress without them, so an application cannot be completed on the promise that bookings will be made later.

How the bookings join up with the visa: Your hotel and transport bookings are linked to your visa through a Booking Reference Number (BRN). Keep this number safe and share it with anyone helping you with the application, because it is the reference that ties your confirmed bookings to your visa file. If the BRN and the bookings behind it cannot be verified, the application stalls at exactly this point. Our general Umrah Visa 2026 guide explains the visa types this rule sits alongside.

The shorter entry window: A single-entry Umrah visa is now valid for only 30 days from issuance to enter Saudi Arabia, down from 90 days. If the pilgrim has not entered within that window, the visa is automatically cancelled. Once you are inside the Kingdom, the stay allowed is up to 90 days. A multiple-entry Umrah visa works differently: it is valid for one year from issuance, with up to 90 days of stay in total across that year. Because the single-entry window is now so short, timing matters: apply close enough to your travel dates that the 30 days do not run out before you fly.

Season deadlines for the 1448 AH cycle: The last date to issue an Umrah visa is 9 March 2027. The last date for pilgrim entry is 23 March 2027. All pilgrims must depart by 7 April 2027. Applications filed close to these dates leave no room for a failed booking check, so build your bookings well before the deadlines rather than in the final days.

How this rule causes rejections: Most problems under the new rule come from the bookings, not the pilgrim. A hotel reference that cannot be verified, perhaps because it was never a real confirmed booking or was made outside the approved channels, will fail the check. Missing transport confirmations for any leg of the journey, including the return to the airport, leave the application incomplete. A booking made through a provider that is not in good standing can also fail, even when the pilgrim paid in good faith. Remember too that tourist eVisa fees are non-refundable, so a failed application can mean paying again. Our Umrah visa rejection guide walks through what to do next, and Umrah Visa Fees 2026 explains the costs before you pay.

Checklist before you apply:

  • Passport valid for 6 months beyond your entry date
  • Names entered exactly as they appear on the passport
  • Hotel booking made through a Nusuk-approved hotel, with a reference that can be verified
  • Transport confirmations in hand for airport arrival, the Makkah to Madinah leg and departure
  • Transport provider licensed and Nusuk-compliant
  • Booking Reference Number (BRN) saved and ready to enter

For help planning the journey between the two holy cities, see our Makkah to Madinah transport guide. Please note: the rules in this article are checked against official pages, but requirements can change. Always confirm the current requirements on the Nusuk platform before you apply.

Sources: Wego - Umrah Visa 2026 Guide ↗ · Hajj Reporters - New Rules for Umrah Visa 2026-2027 Season ↗ · HalalTrip - This Season Umrah Rules Explained ↗ · Kimi Travels - Umrah Visa Rejection Reasons ↗

Umrah Visa - Status CheckHow to Check Your Umrah Visa Status Online

After your application goes in, the waiting is the hardest part. The good news is that you can check umrah visa status online yourself, free of charge, on official Saudi portals. You do not need to rely only on your agent's updates. This guide shows what to prepare before you check, the three official places to check, and what each status result means.

What you need before checking: Have these details ready, copied exactly as they appear in your documents: your passport number, exactly as printed; your visa number or application number, or the reference your operator gave you; your first name as printed in the passport; and your nationality. A single wrong character can make a real application look missing, so copy each detail slowly and check it twice.

Place 1 - The Saudi MOFA visa platform (visa.mofa.gov.sa):

  1. Open visa.mofa.gov.sa in your browser.
  2. Choose the enquiry or search option for visa applications.
  3. Enter any two identifiers, for example your passport number together with your visa number or application number.
  4. Choose your nationality, complete the captcha, and press Inquire.
  5. If the visa is approved, the full visa document is shown. Save it as a PDF and print a copy for your travel folder.

Place 2 - The KSA Visa portal (ksavisa.sa):

  1. Open ksavisa.sa and click Track Application.
  2. Enter your visa or application number and your passport number.
  3. Complete the captcha and click Enquiry.
  4. Click View to see the full visa document when it is ready.

Place 3 - Your Nusuk account (umrah.nusuk.sa): If you applied directly through Nusuk, sign in at umrah.nusuk.sa and open My Applications or My Bookings. Your visa status appears there alongside your package and permit details, which makes it the easiest place to follow everything for one trip in a single view. Our Nusuk app guide explains the account sections in more detail.

What the statuses mean: Under process means the application is still being worked on, so wait and check again later. Approved or issued means your visa is ready: open the full document, save the PDF and print it. Rejected means the application was refused. Not found usually means the details you entered do not match a record yet, which is often a typing error or a very recent submission rather than a refusal.

What to do for each result: If an agent submitted your application, wait at least 72 hours before checking, because new applications take time to appear. If nothing appears after that, re-check your numbers character by character against the passport, and ask your operator for the correct application reference if the one you have does not work. If the status says rejected, read our Umrah visa rejection guide before paying a new fee, so you fix the real reason first. If you are still preparing your application, the new booking requirements are explained in our Umrah Visa 2026 Transport Rule article, and the visa types themselves are covered in the Umrah Visa 2026 guide.

One safety warning: Always type the portal addresses yourself into your browser. Never follow a visa link sent in an unexpected message, even if it looks official. Fake visa pages are a common way to steal passport details and payments, and the real portals above cost nothing to use.

Sources: Wego - Umrah Visa Check 2026 ↗ · IlmKidunya - Umrah Visa Status Guide ↗ · Noble Core - KSA Visa Check by Passport Number ↗

🔄 Calibrate your compass: phone compasses drift near metal, cars and magnets. Hold the phone flat and move it in a figure-8 (∞) pattern 2–3 times to calibrate, keep it away from metal objects, then read the direction again. Cross-check with the sun or a known landmark when you can.

How it works

Why Qibla matters

  • Facing Qibla is a condition of valid Salah
  • All Muslims worldwide pray facing the one Kaaba — a sign of unity
  • Travelling? Recheck Qibla in every new city
Question & Answers

Question & Answers

The questions pilgrims and learners ask most — answered simply, grouped by topic.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Is EasyNusuk the official Nusuk website?

No. EasyNusuk is an independent community platform. It is not affiliated with Nusuk, the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah, or any government body. Always use the official Nusuk app for permits and bookings.

Are the Nusuk key codes free?

Yes, community codes are shared for free. We never ask for your Nusuk password, OTP or login details. Only Featured placement at the top of the list is paid — a code itself is never sold.

How do I book a Rawdah permit?

Use the official Nusuk app: sign in, open "Prophet's Mosque services", choose Rawdah booking and pick a date and time slot. Slots fill quickly, so book as early as the system allows and save your QR permit.

What is the difference between Hajj and Umrah?

Umrah can be performed at any time of the year and takes a few hours. Hajj is performed once a year on fixed dates (8–13 Zul-Hijjah), is one of the five pillars of Islam, and includes additional rites such as the Day of Arafat, Muzdalifah and Rami.

What happens after the competition ends on 20 December?

The codes pause until the next season, and EasyNusuk opens on this homepage: guides, azkar and duas, articles and package help stay live all year.

More Answers

Namaz, Qibla & learning

What should I do if I miss a prayer?

Pray it as Qaza as soon as possible. Missing a prayer deliberately is a serious matter, so keep a routine — alarms and the prayer-times page above both help.

How do I find Qibla in a hotel or new city?

Open the Qibla page on EasyNusuk, tap “Use My Location”, and face the bearing shown. Many hotels also mark Qibla on the ceiling or in a drawer.

Can children play the Islamic Quiz?

Yes — the quiz was made for all ages. Questions cover Hajj, Umrah, Namaz, the Qur'an and Islamic history, and every answer teaches something, right or wrong.

Is EasyNusuk free to use?

Yes. Guides, Azkar, Namaz times, Qibla, articles, Q&A and the quiz are all free. On the Competition page, only optional Featured placement for a code is paid — codes themselves are always free.

Privacy Policy

How easynusuk.com handles your information — short and in plain words. Last updated: 10 November 2026.

What we collect

Very little. If you submit a Nusuk key code, we receive the code, the display name and the country you enter with it, so the code can be shared with the community. That is all we ask for. We never ask for your Nusuk password, OTP or login details, and you should never share those with anyone.

Location

Prayer times and the Qibla finder can use your location, but only when you tap to allow it. Your location is used in your own browser to work out the times and direction. It is never stored by us and never sent to us.

Cookies

This site uses only the cookies it needs to work. Third-party services shown on this site, including advertising partners, may also set their own cookies, as explained below.

Advertising — Google AdSense and third parties

We may show adverts through Google AdSense and other third-party advertising partners. Google and these partners use cookies to serve adverts based on your visits to this and other websites, and to measure how adverts perform. You can turn off personalised advertising in your Google Ads Settings, and you can block or delete cookies in your browser settings at any time.

Not the official Nusuk

EasyNusuk.com is an independent community website. It is not the official Nusuk website or app, and it is not affiliated with the Nusuk app or with the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.
